https://leadership.ng/ebola-oyo-activate.title: Ebola: Oyo Activates Rapid Response Teams, Strengthens Disease Surveillance
https://leadership.ng/ebola-oyo-activate.summary: As part of the measures, the state has strengthened the Infectious Disease Centre at Olodo and placed rapid response teams on standby to ensure a coordinated response to suspected cases. The involvement of the Ministries of Health, Agriculture, Information and Environment is expected to support coordinated disease surveillance, public communication and preventive measures within their respective areas of responsibility.
https://leadership.ng/ebola-oyo-activate.summary_zh: 作为相关措施的一部分，该州已加强Olodo传染病中心，并安排快速反应小组待命，以確保对疑似病例采取协调一致的应对措施。卫生、农业、信息和环境各部的参与，预计将支持各自职责范围内的疾病协调监测、公众沟通和预防措施。
https://leadership.ng/ebola-oyo-activate.body: The government has also brought relevant ministries, departments and agencies, including the Ministries of Health, Agriculture, Information and Environment, under a coordinated platform to improve preparedness and emergency response. The initiative, coordinated by the Ministry of Health under Commissioner for Health, Dr Oluwaserimi Ajetunmobi, is aimed at strengthening inter-agency collaboration, public awareness and early detection of suspected Ebola cases and other infectious diseases. As part of the measures, the state has strengthened the Infectious Disease Centre at Olodo and placed rapid response teams on standby to ensure a coordinated response to suspected cases. The government has also distributed Information, Education and Communication materials to educate residents on Ebola symptoms, transmission and preventive measures. Ajetunmobi said public enlightenment efforts had been intensified, while healthcare workers had been directed to observe infection prevention and control protocols, including the proper use of personal protective equipment such as face masks, face shields and gloves when attending to patients. She explained that the risk of Ebola transmission is generally lower before an infected person develops symptoms, but urged residents to remain vigilant and comply with public health advisories. The commissioner cautioned residents against panic and the spread of unverified information, advising them to report suspected symptoms promptly to the appropriate health authorities. She noted that Ebola’s early symptoms could resemble those of malaria and typhoid fever, making it important for residents to take unusual symptoms seriously and seek medical attention. The government has also directed hospitals across the state to strengthen infectious disease preparedness, with emphasis on screening procedures, protective equipment and infection prevention protocols. The involvement of the Ministries of Health, Agriculture, Information and Environment is expected to support coordinated disease surveillance, public communication and preventive measures within their respective areas of responsibility. The state government urged residents to remain calm, avoid spreading rumours and cooperate with health authorities as it continues to strengthen surveillance, public awareness and emergency response measures. https://leadership.ng/ebola-oyo-activate.body_zh: 政府还召集卫生、农业、信息和环境部等相关部委、部门及机构，建立协调统筹平台，以提升应对准备和应急响应能力。该举措由卫生部长奥卢瓦瑟里米·阿杰通莫比博士协调，旨在加强机构间协作、公众宣传以及疑似埃博拉病例和其他传染病的早期发现。作为相关措施的一部分，州政府加强了奥洛多的传染病中心，并安排快速响应小组待命，以便协调应对疑似病例。政府还分发了信息、教育和宣传材料，向居民普及埃博拉症状、传播途径和预防措施。阿杰通莫比表示，公众宣传力度已经加大，同时已要求医务工作者遵守感染预防和控制规程，包括接触患者时正确使用口罩、面罩和手套等个人防护装备。她解释道，感染者在出现症状前通常传播埃博拉的风险较低，但敦促居民保持警惕并遵守公共卫生建议。部长提醒居民不要恐慌，也不要传播未经核实的信息，并建议他们一旦出现疑似症状，应立即向有关卫生部门报告。她指出，埃博拉的早期症状可能与疟疾和伤寒相似，因此居民应认真对待异常症状并及时就医。政府还已指示全州各医院加强传染病应对准备，重点完善筛查程序、防护装备和感染预防规程。卫生、农业、信息和环境部的参与预计将有助于在各自职责范围内开展协调一致的疾病监测、公众沟通和预防措施。州政府敦促居民保持冷静、不要散播谣言，并与卫生部门合作；政府将继续加强疾病监测、公众宣传和应急响应措施。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、独家内幕和独特视角将直接推送到您的手机上。不要满足于过时新闻。加入 LEADERSHIP NEWS 的 WhatsApp 频道，随时获取全天候最新动态 →

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.title: Does Nigeria truly have over 103 million voters?, By Chidi Anselm Odinkalu
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary: Out of more than 93.4 million registered voters, 24.9 million total votes were cast. A register of voters does not automatically change because a person whose name is on it has died. In 1999, Nigeria had 57.94 million registered voters.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary_zh: 在逾93.4万名登记选民中，共投出2,490万张选票。选民名册不会因为名册上的某个人去世就自动更改。1999年，尼日利亚有5,794万名登记选民。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body: Ahead of Nigeria’s general elections in January and February 2027, Africa Confidential warns that “turnout in the elections is likely to be even lower than the average 26.7% four years ago. Nigerian voters are among the least enthusiastic in the world…. Out of more than 93.4 million registered voters, 24.9 million total votes were cast. This represented an 8.03-point decline from the 2019 elections and was the lowest voter turnout since Nigeria’s return to civilian rule in 1999.” Complaints about “voter apathy” are the staple of Nigeria’s electoral commentariat. The numbers and patterns seem to bear this out . In 1999, turnout was 52.3 per cent. Officially, it grew to 69 per cent in 2003; and has fallen since then to 57.5 per cent in 2007; 53.7 per cent in 2011; 43.7 per cent in 2015; and 34.8 per cent in 2019, before cratering to 26.7 per cent in 2023. These claims require us to accord credibility to the underlying numbers from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). That begins with belief in the baseline of INEC’s electoral register against which turnout is judged. If that register is flawed, then all calculations hinged on it also suffer. Yet, the foundational affliction underlying of Nigeria’s elections is not in INEC’s numbers. Rather, it is an absence of credible demographic management system against which to verify INEC’s claims. The National Population Commission (NPoPC) claims 53 per cent of births in the country are registered and only 10 per cent of deaths are. The implications of this for the credibility of the electoral register should worry everyone. To be sure, electoral rolls are ambulatory. People are not static: we move; relocate, and die too. This is why a demographic management system is essential. In Nigeria, this does not exist. A register of voters does not automatically change because a person whose name is on it has died. But a person should also not be on the register one decade after their death. In Nigeria, there is no way of stopping this. These define the many curiosities about Nigeria’s voting numbers. First, they bear no rational relationship to wider demographic trends. Nigeria’s pattern of supposedly precipitous collapse in voter turnout, for instance, is inversely proportional to both baseline population and civic gripe. In 1999, Nigeria’s population was estimated to be 115,766,000. Nigeria’s current population is estimated at 244 million . That means the country has more than doubled its population since 1999 by 128,234,000 or 110.77 per cent. Over the same period, the voting roll has grown by 81.4 per cent, even as life expectancy in the intervening quarter century has increased by about nine years. If life expectancy is growing with the population and crude death rates falling, then the rate of growth in the voting population should ordinarily outstrip the underlying population growth rate. In 20 years from 1999 to 2023, Nigeria’s population rose by about 87 per cent but the register of voters grew by 36,530,063 or 63.05 per cent. The mis-match between the two trendlines is significant. In 1999, Nigeria had 57.94 million registered voters. This rose by 2.88 million or 4.97 per cent to 60.82 million in 2003 and then by a mere three-quarters of a million or 1.23 per cent to 61.57 million in 2007. By 2011, the number of registered voters climbed by over 12 million (20.5 per cent) to 73.53 million, representing an average yearly growth rate of nearly 5.12 per cent, where previously it had grown by 1.24 per cent in 1999-2003 and 0.3 per cent between 2003 and 2007. By 2015, the population of registered voters fell to 68.83 million, a deficit of 4.7 million voters or 6.39 per cent, representing an annualised rate of reversal of 1.6 per cent. Yet, over the same period, Nigeria, a country with a median age of just under 18 years, had grown in population from an estimated 162.9 million to 181.2 million, an increase of 15.174 million or 11.23 per cent, representing an annual growth rate of 2.8 per cent. The patterns from these numbers do not lend themselves to easy explanations. It is possible to speculate about what may explain this significant delta in growth between the general population and register of voters. Rational factors such as migration; agency dysfunctions in INEC; civic inertia or disaffection; or high transaction costs may be relevant. But there remain worrying patterns that are not easily accounted for even by all these. As the Justice Uwais presidential committee on electoral reform pointed out in its 2008 report, much of what passed for electoral numbers in Nigeria before 2011 was voodoo. Just to illustrate this point, the INEC does not have a breakdown of official results for the 2007 presidential elections yet there are turnout figures for that election. This leads to a second issue: Nigeria’s register of voters has always had invalid voters. The current register of voters in Nigeria dates back to November 2010 when the Attahiru Jega-led INEC set about establishing a credible register of voters for the country. The Commission had limited time to authenticate the raw data before the 2011 general election. When the Automatic Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS) finished its work on the 2011 register nearly four years later, INEC invalidated 4.7 million entries, which reduced the number of registered voters from 73.53 in 2011 to 68.83 in 2015 but not before these invalid 4.7 million were eligible to vote in 2011. Third, the biggest problem may be dead voters. That’s an oxymoron because the dead should not vote. In 2022, INEC explained that it could not expunge the dead from the register because “the country does not have reliable data of births and deaths and the commission cannot engage in arbitrary removal of the names of individuals it suspects are deceased.” This has not changed. It means we have no way of knowing how many ghosts there are among the 103.4 million on INEC’s current register. By failing to display the register as required by law , the Commission does not even care to disabuse suspicions that its register may be bloated. Its response to non-compliance is institutional insouciance. Nigeria’s register of voters is the classic Hotel California : it is “programmed to receive” and, for anyone with their name on it, “you can check out any time you like but you can never leave.” The implications of this for electoral integrity are staggering. But not all these will be adults. Mortality rate for under-5s is 117 per 1000 live births. That’s 700,000 to 855,000 under-five child deaths yearly . To 2025, that could be about 12 million dead under-fives since 2011. The country also reported an estimated median of 111,425 deaths among 5–14-year-olds from 1990 to 2016 . Applied again to a 2011 baseline, that’s another 1,671,375. In total, there could be up to 13.67 million infants, children, and adolescent deaths since 2011. Adjusting the crude death rates for mortality among infants, children, and adolescents, there could be about 18-20 million people liable to be lanced from the electoral register since 2011. Applying the same methodology to a baseline of the 2023 register, that could be up to five million dead people alone on the register since the last election. In its latest announcement, however, INEC said it captured a total of 10,772,421 new voters . It has not accounted for deaths or natural attrition. Separately, at the end of 2025, the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre, (IDMC) reported that Nigeria had at least 3.7 million in internal displacement . The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees adds up to 478,000 Nigerian refugees outside the country. Admittedly not all of these are adults of voting age. Almost assuredly, INEC’s 103.4 million voters is corpulent. When you look at the numbers on INEC’s register and account for the fact that the baseline data goes back to 2011, there is a reasonable likelihood that up to about 25 per cent on it could be dead or dud. That should put all the talk about voter apathy in perspective. But this story has a uniquely Nigerian sting: our diaspora on earth may not have a vote, but we may have a diaspora in Heaven with a veto. Chidi Anselm Odinkalu , a lawyer, teaches at the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy and can be reached through [email protected]
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.title_zh: 尼日利亚真的拥有超过1.03亿名选民吗？作者：齐迪·安塞尔姆·奥丁卡卢
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body_zh: 在尼日利亚2027年1月和2月举行大选之前，《Africa Confidential》警告称，“此次选举的投票率可能甚至会低于四年前26.7%的平均水平。尼日利亚选民是全球热情最低的选民群体之一……在超过9340万名登记选民中，共投出2490万张选票。这一数字较2019年大选下降8.03个百分点，也是尼日利亚自1999年恢复文官统治以来的最低投票率。”关于“选民冷漠”的抱怨，是尼日利亚选举评论中的老生常谈。数字和趋势似乎也印证了这一点。1999年，投票率为52.3%。官方数据显示，2003年投票率升至69%；此后不断下降，2007年为57.5%，2011年为53.7%，2015年为43.7%，2019年为34.8%，到2023年则跌至26.7%。要接受这些说法，就必须相信独立国家选举委员会（INEC）的基础数据。首先，要相信作为衡量投票率基准的INEC选民登记册。如果登记册存在缺陷，所有以此为依据的计算也会受到影响。然而，尼日利亚选举的根本问题并非出在INEC的数字上，而是缺乏可信的人口管理系统，导致INEC的统计无法得到核验。国家人口委员会（NPoPC）称，全国53%的出生人口进行了登记，但死亡人口中只有10%完成登记。这一状况对选民登记册可信度的影响，应当令所有人担忧。当然，选民名册会不断变化。人并非静止不动：我们会迁移、搬迁，也会死亡。因此，人口管理系统至关重要。然而，尼日利亚并不存在这样的系统。选民去世后，其登记信息不会自动从名册中删除；但一个人去世十年后也不应仍在名册上。在尼日利亚，没有办法阻止这种情况。这些现象解释了尼日利亚投票数字中的诸多异常。首先，这些数字与更广泛的人口趋势毫无理性关联。例如，尼日利亚选民投票率据称急剧崩塌的模式，与人口基数和公民不满程度均成反比。1999年，尼日利亚人口估计为115,766,000。目前，该国人口估计为2.44亿。这意味着，自1999年以来，尼日利亚人口增加了超过一倍，增量达128,234,000，增幅为110.77%。同期，选民名册增长81.4%，尽管在此后四分之一个世纪里，人均预期寿命增加了约9岁。如果预期寿命随人口增长而延长、粗死亡率下降，那么投票人口增长率通常应高于总体人口增长率。从1999年至2023年的20年间，尼日利亚人口增长约87%，但选民登记册仅增加36,530,063人，增幅为63.05%。两条趋势线之间的错位十分显著。1999年，尼日利亚有5794万名登记选民。到2003年，这一数字增加288万，即4.97%，达到6082万；此后到2007年仅增加75万，即1.23%，达到6157万。到2011年，登记选民增加逾1200万，增幅20.5%，达到7353万，平均年增长率接近5.12%；而此前1999年至2003年的增长率为1.24%，2003年至2007年间仅为0.3%。到2015年，登记选民人数降至6883万，减少470万，降幅6.39%，年化逆转率为1.6%。然而，在此期间，人口中位年龄不足18岁的尼日利亚，人口从估计的1.629亿增至1.812亿，增加1517.4万，增幅11.23%，年增长率为2.8%。这些数字所呈现的模式很难轻易解释。可以对造成总人口与选民登记册增长显著差异的原因作出推测。人口迁移、INEC的机构失灵、公民冷漠或政治厌弃，以及高昂的办事成本等理性因素，都可能与此有关。但仍有一些令人担忧的模式，即使用上述所有因素也难以充分说明。正如乌瓦伊斯的选举改革总统委员会在2008年报告中所指出的，尼日利亚2011年以前许多被视为选举数据的数字，实际上是巫术。仅举一例来说明：INEC至今没有2007年总统选举的官方结果明细，却有该次选举的投票率数据。这就引出了第二个问题：尼日利亚选民登记册中始终存在无效选民。尼日利亚现行选民登记册始于2010年11月，当时由阿塔希鲁·杰加领导的INEC着手为全国建立可信的选民登记册。委员会在2011年大选前核实原始数据的时间有限。自动指纹识别系统（AFIS）在近四年后完成对2011年登记册的处理时，INEC注销了470万条记录，使登记选民人数从2011年的7353万降至2015年的6883万；然而，在2011年，这470万无效选民仍具有投票资格。第三，最大的问题可能是已死亡选民。这是一个矛盾说法，因为死者不应投票。2022年，INEC解释称，其无法将死者从登记册中删除，因为“该国没有可靠的出生和死亡数据，委员会不能任意删除其怀疑已经死亡者的姓名。”这一状况至今没有改变。这意味着，在INEC现行登记册的1.034亿选民中，无从得知有多少已经成为幽灵。委员会未按法律要求公开登记册，甚至不去消除外界对其登记册可能膨胀的疑虑。委员会对不遵守法律要求的回应，是机构层面的漠不关心。尼日利亚选民登记册就是经典的“加州旅馆”：它被“设定为接待顾客”，而任何名字在册的人“随时都可以退房，却永远无法离开”。这对选举诚信的影响令人震惊。但上述所有人并不都是成年人。5岁以下儿童死亡率为每1000名活产儿中117人，即每年有70万至85.5万名5岁以下儿童死亡。自2011年至2025年，这可能意味着约1200万名5岁以下儿童死亡。该国还报告称，1990年至2016年间，5至14岁儿童死亡人数中位数为111,425人。将这一数字再次套用于2011年基准，又相当于1,671,375人。合计而言，自2011年以来，可能有多达1367万名婴幼儿、儿童和青少年死亡。若根据婴幼儿、儿童和青少年的死亡率对粗死亡率进行调整，自2011年以来，可能约有1800万至2000万人应从选民登记册中剔除。若将同样方法套用于2023年登记册基准，则仅在上次选举以来，登记册上就可能有多达500万名死者。然而，INEC在最新公告中称，共登记了10,772,421名新选民，却没有就死亡或自然减员作出核算。另据国内流离失所问题监测中心（IDMC）2025年底的报告，尼日利亚境内至少有370万人流离失所。联合国难民事务高级专员署另统计，流亡境外的尼日利亚难民多达478,000人。诚然，并非所有这些人都是达到投票年龄的成年人。几乎可以肯定，INEC登记的1.034亿选民人数严重失实。审视INEC登记册上的数字，并考虑其基准数据可追溯至2011年这一事实，登记册上最多约有25%的人可能已经死亡或成为无效选民。这样一来，有关“选民冷漠”的种种说法便应放在恰当背景下看待。然而，这个故事带有独特的尼日利亚意味：我们在人间的侨民或许没有选票，但我们在天堂的侨民却可能拥有否决权。律师Chidi Anselm Odinkalu在弗莱彻法律与外交学院任教，可通过[email protected]与之联系。

https://leadership.ng/medical-tourism-mo.title: Medical Tourism: Monarch Calls For Specialist Hospitals In Every State
https://leadership.ng/medical-tourism-mo.summary: The monarch also urged the West African College of Physicians (WACP) to collaborate with governments, medical professionals and wealthy Nigerians to mobilise resources for the development of advanced medical facilities. The monarch questioned why Nigeria and other African countries had lost their previous appeal as destinations for medical treatment, calling for an examination of the factors responsible for the trend.
https://leadership.ng/medical-tourism-mo.summary_zh: 这位君主还敦促西非医师学会（WACP）与各国政府、医疗专业人员及尼日利亚富人为发展先进医疗设施动员资源。这位君主质疑尼日利亚和其他非洲国家为何失去了作为医疗目的地原有的吸引力，并呼吁审查造成这一趋势的因素。
https://leadership.ng/medical-tourism-mo.body: The monarch also urged the West African College of Physicians (WACP) to collaborate with governments, medical professionals and wealthy Nigerians to mobilise resources for the development of advanced medical facilities. Kupi made the call during a visit by the WACP delegation to his palace ahead of a free medical outreach at LEA Primary School, Waru community, Abuja, organised as part of activities marking the college’s 50th anniversary. He expressed concern that Nigerians continued to travel to countries such as the United States, the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Turkey and India to access specialised healthcare, despite the financial burden associated with seeking treatment abroad. “My prayer and request to this body is that you people are trying. You are trying, but I want us to see how you can do more so that we can have special hospitals that will serve as tourist destinations,” he said. The monarch questioned why Nigeria and other African countries had lost their previous appeal as destinations for medical treatment, calling for an examination of the factors responsible for the trend. “It baffles me sometimes because I remember that when we were children, especially before we came to Nigeria, many people from outside our countries came here to seek medical treatment in our institutions. “So, I do not know where we got it wrong. Is it the environment? Is it us? Or is it our governments that have created this problem?” he asked. Kupi urged the WACP to engage prominent investors and philanthropists, including Aliko Dangote, to support the establishment of specialist hospitals capable of providing advanced medical services locally. According to him, investing in specialised healthcare facilities at home would help reduce the substantial foreign exchange spent by Nigerians seeking treatment abroad while making advanced medical services more accessible. “We should invest that money here. We should be able to put something on the ground rather than continue travelling abroad,” he added. He also warned that overseas medical trips could be expensive and risky because of the cost and demands of travelling long distances to obtain treatment. The monarch commended the college for choosing Waru community for its medical outreach, saying the initiative had brought healthcare services closer to residents. Meanwhile, the President of the WACP, Dr Mamadou Mourtalla Ka, reaffirmed the college’s commitment to improving healthcare delivery and specialist training across West Africa. “Healthcare has no borders. Healthcare does not recognise borders,” he said. Ka said the college was working to improve healthcare standards and specialist training in English-, French- and Portuguese-speaking West African countries. The college’s 50th anniversary celebration, themed : “ WACP@50: Celebrating a Legacy and Envisioning the Future,” featured its Annual General and Scientific Meeting and community health activities. At the medical outreach, a Fellow of the WACP in the Faculty of Family Medicine, Dr Pemi Daniel, said about 15 patients had been selected and screened for free surgical services. He said patients with conditions including hernia, hydrocele and lipoma were assessed for treatment, adding that some had already received surgical care. “We are attending to people with medical conditions and surgical conditions. In this place, we have about 15 people who have been selected and screened for free surgical services,” he said. Daniel added that other residents presenting with various medical conditions were also receiving attention from members and fellows of the college. Similarly, the Chairman of the Medical Outreach Committee, Dr Nnena Okafor, said the programme provided health education, treatment for common illnesses and minor surgical procedures. She said patients presenting with fever, headaches, abdominal pain and malaria were receiving medical attention, while procedures including lump excision and herniorrhaphy were being performed at the primary healthcare centre. Okafor said the medical team had attended to its sixth surgical patient at the time of the interview. She expressed satisfaction with the turnout, noting that residents had come out in large numbers and that sufficient medical personnel were available to attend to them. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/medical-tourism-mo.title_zh: 医疗旅游：莫纳克呼吁每个州都设立专科医院
https://leadership.ng/medical-tourism-mo.body_zh: 君主还呼吁西非医师学会（WACP）与各国政府、医疗专业人员及富裕的尼日利亚人合作，调动资源发展先进医疗设施。库皮是在WACP代表团访问其宫殿、准备在阿布贾瓦鲁社区LEA小学开展免费义诊之际提出这一呼吁的。此次义诊是学院成立50周年系列活动的一部分。库皮表示，尽管赴海外治疗会带来沉重的经济负担，尼日利亚人仍持续前往美国、阿拉伯联合酋长国、埃及、土耳其和印度等国家接受专科医疗。他说：“我向该机构祈祷并提出请求，希望你们正在努力。你们确实在努力，但我希望我们共同思考如何做得更多，从而建立能够成为旅游目的地的专科医院。”君主质疑尼日利亚和其他非洲国家为何失去了此前作为医疗目的地的吸引力，呼吁审视造成这一趋势的因素。他说：“有时我感到不解，因为我记得我们还是孩子的时候，尤其是在我们来到尼日利亚之前，许多来自我们国家以外的人都会来这里在我们的医疗机构接受治疗。所以，我不知道我们在哪里出了问题。是环境的问题？是我们的错，还是我们的政府制造了这个问题？”库皮呼吁WACP争取知名投资人和慈善家，包括阿利科·丹戈特，支持建立能够在本地提供先进医疗服务的专科医院。据他表示，投资本土专科医疗设施，既能减少尼日利亚人赴海外治疗所耗费的巨额外汇，也能使先进医疗服务更容易获得。他补充道：“我们应该把钱花在这里。我们应该能够在本地落地建设一些设施，而不是继续前往海外。”他还警告说，海外就医可能既昂贵又有风险，因为长途跋涉接受治疗会产生高昂成本和各项要求。君主赞扬学院选择瓦鲁社区开展医疗义诊，称这一举措使医疗服务离居民更近了。与此同时，WACP主席马马杜·穆尔塔拉·卡博士重申，学院致力于改善整个西非地区的医疗服务并加强专科培训。他说：“医疗没有国界，医疗也不承认国界。”卡表示，学院正努力改善讲英语、法语和葡萄牙语的西非国家的医疗标准和专科培训。学院以“WACP@50：庆祝传承，展望未来”为主题纪念成立50周年，活动包括年度大会暨科学会议以及社区健康活动。义诊期间，WACP家庭医学科会士佩米·丹尼尔博士表示，已筛选出约15名患者，为他们提供免费外科服务。他说，患疝气、鞘膜积液和脂肪瘤等疾病的患者接受了治疗评估，其中一些人已经获得外科治疗。丹尼尔说：“我们正在为患有疾病和需要外科手术的人提供诊疗。这里约有15人经过筛选，可以接受免费外科服务。”丹尼尔补充说，其他患有各种疾病的居民也在接受学院成员与会士的诊疗。医疗义诊委员会主席恩妮娜·奥卡福博士表示，该项目提供健康教育、常见疾病治疗和小型外科手术。她说，发热、头痛、腹痛和疟疾患者正在接受诊疗，基层医疗中心还在开展肿块切除和疝修补术等手术。奥卡福表示，接受采访时，医疗团队已经为第六名外科患者进行了诊疗。她对居民积极参与表示满意，并指出居民大批到场，医疗人员也足够，能够为她们提供服务。我们掌握最新动态。获取实时报道、独家内幕和独特视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS，通过WhatsApp获取全天候更新→

https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.title: Akwa Ibom Pledges More Support For Vulnerable Residents
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.summary: According to her, the interventions cover food security, support for vulnerable households, housing for disadvantaged families, women and youth empowerment, assistance for elderly citizens, inclusion of persons with disabilities, and emergency and disaster response. She said the creation of a dedicated Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs reflected the governor’s commitment to coordinating interventions, strengthening social protection and ensuring vulnerable individuals and families received organised support.
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.summary_zh: 据她介绍，这些干预措施涵盖粮食安全、为弱势家庭提供支持、为处境不利的家庭提供住房、赋权妇女和青年、为老年公民提供帮助、确保残障人士获得包容，以及开展紧急和灾害应对工作。她说，设立专门的人道主义事务部体现了州长承诺协调各项干预措施、强化社会保护，并确保弱势个人和家庭获得有组织的支持。
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.body: The Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs, Princess Emem Ibanga, gave the assurance at the weekend during the launch of the EL ZAIN Women, Children and Peace Development Initiative at IBOM LED, along IBB Avenue, Uyo. Ibanga described the administration’s policies as people-centred, noting that the government had invested billions of naira in welfare interventions over the past three years. She said the humanitarian governance model was designed to integrate vulnerable and disadvantaged people into the government’s programmes and address their needs. According to her, the interventions cover food security, support for vulnerable households, housing for disadvantaged families, women and youth empowerment, assistance for elderly citizens, inclusion of persons with disabilities, and emergency and disaster response. She said the creation of a dedicated Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs reflected the governor’s commitment to coordinating interventions, strengthening social protection and ensuring vulnerable individuals and families received organised support. The commissioner commended the EL ZAIN initiative for its humanitarian work and urged its leadership to sustain its partnership with the ministry and align its programmes with the state’s priorities. “I am pleased that the EL ZAIN Women, Children and Peace Development Initiative has registered with the ministry. I encourage its leadership to sustain this relationship and align its programmes with the state’s humanitarian priorities and coordination framework,” she said. Chairman of the launch, Paul Usoro, SAN, praised the support provided by the founder’s husband, describing it as a demonstration of the initiative’s slogan, “love in action”. Usoro called for prayers and material support for the initiative, saying humanitarian service required collective effort. The founder, Dr Zeinab Akpan, described the launch as a new beginning in humanitarian assistance, recalling that the initiative grew out of years of engaging with disadvantaged people, supporting vulnerable households and offering guidance to those in need. She said her experience as Acting President of the Naval Officers’ Wives Association (NOWA) strengthened her resolve to develop structured programmes to support vulnerable groups. According to her, the initiative would focus on empowering women, nurturing children, promoting peace, encouraging self-reliance, and supporting education and dialogue. She said the initiative was associated with the Institute of Public Policy and Diplomacy Research (IPPDR), New York, and aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals on gender equality, education and peace. Akpan listed the initiative’s planned interventions to include micro-business grants for 20 women selected through a screening process, healthcare support, assistance with hospital bills, educational awards for students who finish first to third in their categories, and childcare support across local government areas. She thanked Governor Eno and the commissioner for their support, urging stakeholders to take practical steps to improve the lives of vulnerable people. The initiative’s Executive Director, Rear Admiral Joseph Akpan (retd.), said his wife’s difficult childhood experiences inspired the establishment of the foundation. He expressed gratitude that the initiative was beginning to yield results and pledged to expand its work through partnerships with other organisations. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.title_zh: 阿夸伊博姆承诺为弱势居民提供更多支持
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.body_zh: 人道事务专员埃梅姆·伊班加公主于周末在位于乌约IBB大道沿线IBOM LED举行的“EL ZAIN妇女、儿童与和平发展倡议”启动仪式上作出上述保证。伊班加称本届政府的政策以人为本，并指出，过去三年政府已投入数十亿奈拉用于福利干预。她说，人道治理模式旨在将弱势和处境不利群体纳入政府各项计划，满足他们的需求。据她介绍，这些干预措施涵盖粮食安全、为弱势家庭提供支持、为处境不利家庭提供住房、赋权妇女和青年、援助老年公民、吸纳残障人士，以及开展紧急救援和灾害应对。她说，设立专门的人道事务部体现了州长对协调各项干预措施、加强社会保护以及确保弱势个人和家庭获得有组织支持的承诺。专员称赞EL ZAIN倡议的人道工作，并敦促其领导层维持与该部的合作关系，使各项计划与本州优先事项相衔接。她说：“我很高兴EL ZAIN妇女、儿童与和平发展倡议已在本部登记注册。我鼓励其领导层维持这层关系，并使各项计划与本州的人道优先事项和协调框架相衔接。”启动仪式主席保罗·乌索罗律师称赞了创办人的丈夫所提供的支持，称这是该倡议“行动中的爱”这一口号的体现。乌索罗呼吁为该倡议祈祷并提供物质支持，称人道服务需要集体努力。创办人泽纳布·阿克潘博士称，此次启动标志着人道援助的新起点，并回顾称，该倡议源于她多年来与处境不利群体接触、扶持弱势家庭以及为有需要者提供指导的历程。她说，担任海军军官夫人协会（NOWA）代理主席的经历，强化了她制定结构化计划以支持弱势群体的决心。据她介绍，该倡议将重点关注赋权妇女、关怀儿童、促进和平、鼓励自立，以及支持教育和对话。她说，该倡议与纽约公共政策与外交研究所（IPPDR）合作，并与联合国关于性别平等、教育与和平的可持续发展目标相契合。阿克潘列出的计划干预措施包括：通过筛选程序选出的20名女性获得微型企业补助、医疗支持、医院账单援助，为各自类别中名列第一至第三的学生颁发教育奖励，以及在地方政府辖区提供儿童照护支持。她感谢州长埃诺和专员的支持，敦促各方采取切实行动，改善弱势群体的生活。该倡议执行主任约瑟夫·阿克潘海军少校（退役）表示，妻子艰难坎坷的童年经历促使她创立该基金会。他对倡议开始取得成果表示感激，并承诺通过与其他组织建立合作来扩大工作。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、独家内幕和独家视角将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS，通过WhatsApp获取全天候最新消息 →

https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-plans-na.summary: He explained that the proposed naval base would help secure waterways and creeks along the Gulf of Guinea corridor. The plan comes amid security concerns in coastal oil-bearing communities, including Eket, Oron, Eastern Obolo and Ibeno, where residents have continued to seek government intervention to address challenges affecting riverine communities.
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-plans-na.summary_zh: 他 explained称，拟议中的海军基地将有助于保障几内亚湾走廊沿线的航道和溪流安全。该计划出台之际，产油沿海社区，包括Eket、Oron、Eastern Obolo和Ibeno，正面临安全担忧；这些地区的居民持续寻求政府介入，以解决影响河流社区的各种问题。
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-plans-na.body: The Commissioner for Internal Security, General Koko Essien (retd.), disclosed this during the ongoing ministerial media briefing by ministries, departments and agencies at Government House, Uyo. He explained that the proposed naval base would help secure waterways and creeks along the Gulf of Guinea corridor. “Every community has needs. The government is planning a lot for Stubb Creek, but first will be the establishment of a naval base in Stubb Creek,” Essien said. The plan comes amid security concerns in coastal oil-bearing communities, including Eket, Oron, Eastern Obolo and Ibeno, where residents have continued to seek government intervention to address challenges affecting riverine communities. Essien also disclosed that the Nigerian Army would establish a new battalion at Urue Offong Oruko, while the proposed naval base would complement existing security operations across the state’s waterways. According to him, the state government has acquired 14 gunboats to strengthen maritime security and complement existing federal security assets. He added that the government had procured 17 patrol vehicles, deployed largely to the police, to improve security operations across the state. On other security initiatives, Essien said the government was working with the Federal Ministry of Interior to relocate the correctional centre on Wellington Bassey Way to Nung Ukim, Ikono, noting that land had been secured for the project. He also announced plans to establish a police division along Banking Layout, Udoma Udo Road, while preparations for the proposed state police system were ongoing, subject to the completion of the necessary legislative process. The commissioner said the government had established a Security Trust Fund chaired by Paul Usoro, SAN, to support security initiatives, urging individuals and organisations to contribute to the fund. On the Ibom Community Watch, Essien dismissed concerns over unpaid salaries, insisting that members were paid when due. Meanwhile, the Commissioner for Transport, Dr Anthony Luke, said the state government planned to remove all illegal motor parks before Christmas to improve security visibility and boost revenue. https://www.myjoyonline.com/mtn-yellow-l.summary: The Yellow Ladies Network, a non-profit organisation made up of female staff of MTN, has organised a free breast cancer screening for 500 women in Accra as part of activities to mark this year's Breast Cancer Awareness Month. https://www.myjoyonline.com/mtn-yellow-l.summary_zh: 由MTN女性员工组成的非营利组织“黄色 Ladies Network”在阿克拉为500名女性组织了免费乳腺癌筛查，作为今年乳腺癌宣传月系列活动的一部分。MTN加纳首席财务官兼MTN Yellow Ladies Network主席Antoinette Kwofie在活动上表示，该网络正将活动从员工福利拓展至社区，通过卫生干预产生积极影响。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mtn-yellow-l.body: The Yellow Ladies Network, a non-profit organisation made up of female staff of MTN, has organised a free breast cancer screening for 500 women in Accra as part of activities to mark this year's Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The programme was used to educate women on maintaining healthy breasts. Speaking during the programme, MTN Ghana's Chief Finance Officer and Chairperson of the MTN Yellow Ladies Network, Antoinette Kwofie, said the network is extending its activities beyond staff welfare to impact communities through health interventions. Madam Kwofie said the Yellow Ladies Network was established in 2025 to empower, inspire, and coach women within MTN, but it was not limited to staff; it also reaches out to customers and communities. She said last year the network organized a fundraising walk and donated the proceeds to the Breast Cancer Unit of the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital and to Breast Care International. She said this year's theme focuses on better outcomes through action, hence the decision to take screening to the community, particularly market women who hardly get time to visit hospitals." We thought we would come to the marketplace because as women, we always put ourselves last when it comes to healthcare," she said. She said the outreach was designed to bring healthcare providers to the women, educate them, share survivors' experiences, teach self-examination and offer free screening. She said early detection saves lives and the exercise sought to help women know their status and identify lumps that need further checks. No specific target was set, as the aim was to screen as many women as possible. She said envoys were sent to market queens and beauticians' associations to mobilize participants, with doctors from various hospitals conducting the screening and referring cases that need further attention. She expressed satisfaction with the turnout, noting that screening started at 8:00 a.m. and women had already formed long queues to be screened, indicating that many had overcome fear. The President of Breast Care International and CEO of Peace and Love Hospitals, Dr Beatrice Wiafe Addae, who partnered MTN for the exercise, called for increased awareness to reduce fear, stigma and mortality. She said many people still attribute breast cancer to witchcraft, leading women to prayer camps and delaying treatment. She disclosed that over 5,000 Ghanaian women are diagnosed with breast cancer annually and over 2,300 die, but early reporting can reduce mortality. Dr Wiafe Addae said breast cancer is not painful at the early stage, hence the need for monthly self-examination and education. She said about 60 to 70 per cent of patients are diagnosed at stage three or four cancers, but detection at stages one and two allows for breast-conserving surgery. She said risk factors include being a woman, family history, late childbirth, excessive alcohol intake, smoking including shisha, skin-lightening products, hair relaxers, lack of exercise and fatty diets. She cautioned against cosmetic products without English labelling, noting some contain carcinogens, and called for financial support for patients, since screening and biopsy are not covered by health insurance. She proposed enrolling vulnerable breast and prostate cancer patients on the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty programme
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mtn-yellow-l.title_zh: MTN Yellow Ladies Network为500名市场妇女筛查乳腺癌
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mtn-yellow-l.body_zh: 由MTN女性员工组成的非营利组织“黄色女士网络”在阿克拉为500名女性组织了免费乳腺癌筛查，作为今年乳腺癌宣传月系列活动的一部分。该项目旨在向女性普及乳房保健知识。MTN加纳首席财务官兼MTN黄色女士网络主席Antoinette Kwofie在活动期间表示，该网络正将活动从员工福利拓展至社区，通过卫生干预产生积极影响。Kwofie女士表示，黄色女士网络成立于2025年，旨在赋能、激励并指导MTN女性，但其工作并不局限于员工，还会惠及客户和社区。她说，去年该网络组织了一次募款步行活动，并将所得款项捐赠给Korle Bu Teaching Hospital乳腺癌科和Breast Care International。她说，今年的主题聚焦于通过行动改善结果，因此决定将筛查带到社区，尤其是几乎没有时间前往医院的市场女性。“我们认为应该来到市场，因为作为女性，在医疗保健方面，我们总是把自己放在最后。”她说。此次外展活动旨在把医疗服务提供者带到女性身边，向她们普及知识，分享幸存者的经历，教授自我检查方法，并提供免费筛查。她说，早期发现能够挽救生命，此次活动旨在帮助女性了解自身健康状况，并发现需要进一步检查的肿块。活动没有设定具体目标，而是希望尽可能为更多女性筛查。她说，网络派代表联络市场女王和美容师协会，动员参与者参加筛查；来自多家医院的医生负责开展筛查，并将需要进一步治疗的病例转诊。她对参与情况表示满意，并指出筛查于上午8:00开始，妇女们已经排起长队等待检查，这表明许多人已经克服了恐惧。Breast Care International总裁兼Peace and Love Hospitals首席执行官Dr Beatrice Wiafe Addae与MTN合作开展此次活动。她呼吁加强宣传，以减少恐惧、污名化和死亡率。她说，许多人仍将乳腺癌归因于巫术，导致女性前往祈祷营并延误治疗。她透露，加纳每年有超过5,000名女性被诊断患有乳腺癌，其中超过2,300人死亡，但及早报告能够降低死亡率。Dr Wiafe Addae说，乳腺癌在早期并不会疼痛，因此女性需要每月进行自我检查并接受相关知识教育。她说，约60%至70%的患者在癌症第三或第四期才得到诊断，而在第一或第二期发现病症，则可以接受保乳手术。她说，风险因素包括身为女性、家族病史、生育较晚、过量饮酒、吸烟（包括使用水烟）、使用美白产品、头发 relaxers、缺乏运动以及高脂饮食。她提醒公众慎用没有英文标签的化妆品，指出其中一些含有致癌物质，并呼吁为患者提供资金支持，因为筛查和活组织检查不在健康保险保障范围内。她提议将弱势乳腺癌和前列腺癌患者纳入“为减贫而拓宽生计计划”……

According to the statement, the disagreement escalated into a physical altercation, during which Dalha allegedly picked up a knife and stabbed her husband in the stomach. https://leadership.ng/police-rescue-woma.summary_zh: 事件发生于2026年10月25日，地点是达斯镇Lirr Bajar，起因是双方因据称由丈夫持有的钱、包装纸和一部手机发生争执。声明称，争执升级为肢体冲突，期间Dalha据称拿起刀刺入丈夫腹部。据报道，居民聚集在现场并威胁要私刑处死该女子，随后派驻达斯分局警察总部的警员赶到并将她救出。
https://leadership.ng/police-rescue-woma.body: The incident occurred on October 25, 2026, at Lirr Bajar in Dass, following an argument over money, wrappers and a mobile phone allegedly in the husband’s possession. The police spokesperson, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, identifying the suspect as Fatima Dalha. According to the statement, the disagreement escalated into a physical altercation, during which Dalha allegedly picked up a knife and stabbed her husband in the stomach. Residents reportedly gathered at the scene and threatened to lynch the woman before police operatives attached to the Dass Divisional Police Headquarters arrived and rescued her. Habib said the injured husband was taken to a hospital for treatment, while the suspect was arrested and the knife allegedly used in the attack recovered. He added that the case would be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Bauchi for further investigation. Reacting to the incident, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, expressed concern over domestic violence among young couples and urged them to settle disputes through dialogue, family intervention and other lawful means. “A moment of anger can destroy two lives forever,” the commissioner warned. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary_zh: Aláàfin Májòótú在一场ordinary疫情中不幸去世，这永远提醒人们，疫情肆虐时，即便是最神圣的圣林和最尊贵的王室也难逃劫难。Pẹhẹ疫情犹如往敞开的流血伤口上撒粗盐。据记载，尽管Pẹhẹ疫情在1831年直接导致数千人死亡，但Ọyọ-Ilé早已因饥荒、内乱和疾病共同造成逾100,000名居民死亡而濒临窒息。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body: History provides a stern warning about what happens when public health complacency meets administrative lethargy. Between 1827 and 1831, in Ọyọ-Ilé, the majestic capital of the Old Oyo Empire, the people tried to ignore the subtle signs of danger. But as the Yoruba say, bullets eventually escaped, the gun boomed, and the snake’s bite led to documented catastrophe. A strange, debilitating disease called Pẹhẹ had suddenly sprouted from nowhere. It was an infectious, highly contagious disease that waged a deadly, relentless war on the human respiratory system. Pẹhẹ ravaged the capital of the Empire, a tragic chapter meticulously recorded by the legendary historian Samuel Johnson on page 254 of his monumental work, History of the Yoruba . Because it is only the beginning of a war that human beings can anticipate and never its ultimate ending, by 1831, Pẹhẹ had mutated from a localized health scare into an uncontrollable pestilence. In that fatal year, it breached the sacred palace walls and took away the highly revered supreme monarch of the Empire, Aláàfin Májòótú. When Májòótú succumbed to the breath-stealing plague, Aláàfin Amodo ascended a throne already sitting atop a crumbling nation. The tragic death of Aláàfin Májòótú’s in the hands of an ordinary pandemic stands as an eternal reminder that not even the most sacred grove or exalted royal court is spared when pestilence wages war. Plagues are fiercely democratic; they respect neither crown nor stool. This tragic historical truth brings to mind one of my favorite musical lines by Kelani Yesufu, the legendary Egba-born Yoruba Sakara music singer and social poet. It was in a masterwork track that the bard titled “Ikú ò Mo Olówó ”. It is a profound philosophical treatise asserting that death is no respecter of wealth, crown, or social status. Yesufu composed the track as a grieving tribute to Shittu Shitta Alabi, his master lead drummer, who suddenly slumped and died on stage at Sokenu Village, Abeokuta, during a live performance in 1972. In a haunting symbol of lifelong devotion to craft, Alabi passed into eternity with his Sakara drum still clutched tightly in his lifeless hands. Kelani Yesufu’s musical prowess and cultural prominence reached its zenith during the mid-to-late 20th century. Standing tall alongside contemporaries like S. Aka (Sanusi Ayinde Aka, Baba Wahidi, a.k.a. Omo Lawale), the legendary Sakara genre lord Yusuff Olatunji, Haruna Ishola, and Lefty Salami, Yesufu combined traditional Yoruba instrumentation, specifically the solemn, melancholic goje violin and rhythmic Sakara hand drums, to attack public decay and social vices. Kelani became renowned as an against-the-grain musician due to his unorthodox, cutting poetry. He deployed his storytelling craft in fighting well-known social crusades, manifested in tracks like “ Emu Ògùrò” (where he mercilessly attacked reckless drunkenness) and “April Fool ,” another of his sharp, satirical social commentaries. Yesufu was the courageous bard who first dared to break the ancient cultural taboo surrounding venereal diseases with his famous track “À tòsí” (Gonorrhea). Before Yesufu’s bold intervention, Yoruba society was conditioned to mask the disease under the deceptive, romanticised label À rùn Gbajúmò — an infection reserved for notables and men of means. In his track, Yesufu urged society to face hard epidemiological facts, dismantling the hypocritical contradictions inherent in romanticising a disgraceful affliction simply because it affected the elite. While lamenting the death of his master drummer in a grief-encrusted voice, Kelani sermonized on the absolute inevitability and impartiality of death. The track eventually became a sacred document frequently cited by cultural historians, a poignant testament to the profound, lifelong spiritual bond developed between traditional Yoruba vocalists and their lead drummers. It was that exact same symbiotic bond that existed between Yusuff Olatunji and his lead drummer, Kasumu Ishola Sanni; between Haruna Ishola and Raufu Ojubanire; between Lefty Salami and Nosiru Akanmu; and between the fiery Ayinla Omowura and Adewole Alao, famously known as Onílù Olà , the drummer of fortune. Plagues, like death itself, sever these human bonds without mercy. In Ọyọ-Ilé, Pẹhẹ claimed the lives of thousands of citizens in rapid succession. The pestilence was reported to be the devastating climax of a four-year cycle of recurrent epidemic outbreaks in the empire’s capital. It provoked a historic visit to Ọyọ-Ilé in 1827 by the famous Cornish explorer, Richard Lander. Lander had arrived in the Empire’s capital riding on the fame of his association with solving the mystery of the course and outlet of the River Niger, alongside the Scottish explorer Hugh Clapperton. After Clapperton and other members of the expedition succumbed to tropical illnesses, Lander was commissioned by the British government to return, sailing with his brother from Badagry to Bussa by canoe, where they were eventually captured and ransomed. When Lander arrived at Ọyọ-Ilé, he recorded his astonishment at the crude yet organised quarantine structures implemented by the empire’s authorities. The traditional council had taken victims of Pẹhẹ to an isolation centre, established inside a dense forest roughly half a mile outside the city walls. In his journal, Lander observed that the sick were placed systematically “underneath the branches of trees…” The strict customary law of the empire dictated that the next of kin of Pẹhẹ victims were solely responsible for bringing food and water to the perimeter of the forest isolation grounds. However, this outbreak severely crippled the empire because it arrived alongside a devastating combination of external and internal crises. A brutal drought had covertly walked into Ọyọ-Ilé that same year. Consequently, the metropolis suffered the double agony of severe famine and political instability, which had commenced a decade earlier due to internal rivalries. The Pẹhẹ pandemic was like rubbing coarse salt into an open, bleeding wound. Historical descriptions of Pẹhẹ paint it as a highly contagious respiratory illness that caused swift, terrifying fatalities across all social strata. Aláàfin Májòótú and Ọyọ-Ilé’s ancient political structures were completely overwhelmed. In his notes, Lander helped preserve the oral memory of this tragedy. He recorded that the combination of acute famine and political turmoil severely worsened the plight of those confined to the forest isolation center. Because the victims were largely drawn from poor backgrounds, many ended up dying of sheer starvation rather than the viral load of Pẹhẹ itself. It was recorded that although Pẹhẹ directly killed thousands in 1831, Ọyọ-Ilé was already suffocating from the loss of more than 100,000 of its inhabitants to famine, civil strife, and disease combined. This massive health disaster shattered Old Oyo’s demographic foundation and completely paralysed its military leadership. It dramatically accelerated the empire’s fall to Fulani invasions and internal rebellions, culminating in the total evacuation and permanent abandonment of Ọyọ-Ilé as the capital between 1835 and 1836. Plagues do not merely kill bodies; if mishandled, they topple empires. If pre-colonial Nigeria was naive in curtailing the spread of infectious pathogens, centuries later, it is outright criminal for modern authorities to follow suit. Long before modern medicine, diseases like chickenpox and smallpox attacked the rich and the poor with equal, indiscriminate fury. In response to their inability to comprehend or halt the ravages of smallpox, the ancient Yoruba deified the disease out of sheer terror. Smallpox was elevated to the pantheon of sacred deities as Ṣọnpọnná. Because of the mysterious way it struck from nowhere, the deity was given fearful, exalted appellations. One was Olóde, “The Owner of the Outside” or “Lord of the Open Space,” referencing how the contagion traveled invisibly through open air and wind; Ọbalúayé “The King Who is Lord of the World”; and Babalúayé “The Father Who is the Lord of the Earth.” Till this day in ancient Ilé-Ifẹ, the annual Ìtàpá festival is celebrated to memorialise those ancient pox outbreaks. When you observe the intricate lesions of white chalk painted across the bodies of Ọbàtálá priests during the sacred festival, you are looking at a living artistic ritual depicting the skin pustules suffered by their ancestors. Ṣọnpọnná priests were both deeply revered and terrifyingly feared as specialist medical practitioners. They presided over the containment of pox outbreaks, performing ritual sacrifices, administering botanical variolation (inoculation), caring for the afflicted, and executing strict, solitary burials for those killed by the disease to prevent further contamination. Until its global eradication in the 20th century, no disease struck deeper dread into the Yoruba psyche than smallpox, owing to its high transmission rate, swift lethality, and unpredictable seasonality. The disease routinely peaked between January and February, the dry, dusty harmattan months, proving itself to be an opportunistic killer that exploited seasonal vulnerability. Similarly, cholera has been an explosive, killer epidemic in Nigeria’s history. It struck water supplies and wiped out entire communities overnight. But no historical outbreak matched the terrifying speed of the 1918 Influenza Pandemic. Originating in March 1918 in Kansas, USA, and carried across oceans by returning World War I troops, the “Spanish Flu” quickly earned the grim distinction of killing more people than any other pandemic in human history. It became the first truly nationwide pandemic to sweep through Nigeria, imported directly by maritime passengers and crew arriving at coastal ports. Lagos was the epicentre of the tragedy. Public historian Oludamola Adebowale notes that passengers who contracted the virus in Accra, Gold Coast (modern Ghana), boarded ships bound for Lagos and seeded the contagion upon arrival. The spread was so violent that within the first two months, maritime quarantines completely collapsed. Lagos lost 1.5 per cent of its entire population of 81,941 people in a matter of weeks. Out of a national population estimated at 18 million in 1918, over 500,000 Nigerians died within six months, with between 50 per cent and 80 per cent of the entire population contracting the virus. From Lagos, the flu followed trade routes like wildfire. In 1918 October, Abeokuta was to get its first index patient. Ibadan got its on October 5, 1918 and gradually, Oyo, Ilorin, Minna, Bida, Jebba, Zaria, Kano, and Bauchi got theirs. Calabar and Onitsha got theirs on October 14, 1918 while it was spread farther by ships through Forcados port to Warri and Asaba, Port Harcourt and Bonny. Traveling through passengers on River Niger, the Spanish flu pandemic spread to Lokoja, Sokoto, Maiduguri, as well as to other parts of the Northern Nigeria, so much that, by December 1918, the whole of the country had completely bowed to the Spanish flu. Traveling via passengers along the River Niger, the Spanish flu penetrated Lokoja, Sokoto, and Maiduguri. By December 1918, the entire geographic entity of Nigeria had completely bowed to the devastating flu. With this mountain of historical tragedy, and our recent, painful experience during COVID-19, Nigeria’s current dilly-dallying on the reported Abuja Ebola case is utterly incomprehensible. Ebola is not an abstract threat. Since its discovery in September 1976 along the Ebola River in Yambuku, (in the Democratic Republic of Congo, then Zaire) where it claimed its first victim, a local school headmaster named Mabalo Lokela, the virus has exhibited one of the highest case-fatality rates known to science.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.title_zh: 埃博拉：疫情导致一名Aláàfin去世，Festus Adedayo撰文
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body_zh: 历史对公共卫生自满与行政懈怠相遇后会酿成何种后果发出了严厉警告。1827年至1831年间，在旧奥约帝国宏伟的都城Ọyọ-Ilé，人们试图忽视危险的细微征兆。但正如约鲁巴人所说，子弹终究会出膛，枪声终将轰鸣，蛇bite最终酿成了有案可查的灾难。一种名为Pẹhẹ的怪异致衰疾病突然凭空出现。这是一种传染病，传染性极强，对人体呼吸系统发动了致命而持续不断的战争。Pẹhẹ肆虐帝国都城；传奇历史学家Samuel Johnson在其不朽著作《History of the Yoruba》第254页详细记录了这幕悲剧篇章。由于人类只能预见战争的开端，却永远无法预见其最终结局，到1831年，Pẹhẹ已从局部健康警报演变为失控的瘟疫。在那个致命年份，它突破神圣的宫殿围墙，夺走了备受敬仰的帝国至高君主Aláàfin Májòótú的性命。当Májòótú屈服于这场夺走呼吸的瘟疫时，Aláàfin Amodo登上的王座所支撑的国家早已摇摇欲坠。Aláàfin Májòótú死于一场寻常大流行病，这一悲剧始终提醒人们，当瘟疫发动战争时，即使最神圣的树林和最尊贵的王室宫廷也难免遭到波及。瘟疫在死亡面前极其平等；它既不顾王冠，也不顾王座。这段悲惨的历史事实令人想起Kelani Yesufu最钟爱的音乐名句之一。他是出生于Egba的传奇约鲁巴Sakara音乐歌手和社会诗人。这句话出自他的一首杰作，那位歌匠将其题为“Ikú ò Mo Olówó”。这是一段深邃的哲学论述，断言死亡不尊重财富、王冠或社会地位。Yesufu创作这首歌，是为了悼念他的首席鼓手师父Shittu Shitta Alabi。1972年，Alabi在Abeokuta的Sokenu Village参加现场演出时，突然身体一软，倒在舞台上死去。Alabi终生献身艺业的感人象征，就在于他逝去时仍紧紧抱着自己的Sakara鼓。Kelani Yesufu的音乐造诣和文化影响力在20世纪中后期达到顶峰。他与S. Aka（Sanusi Ayinde Aka，又名Baba Wahidi及Omo Lawale）、传奇Sakara流派宗师Yusuff Olatunji、Haruna Ishola和Lefty Salami等同时代音乐人并肩而立，将传统约鲁巴乐器，尤其是庄重忧郁的goje小提琴和富有节奏感的Sakara手鼓结合起来，向社会腐化和恶习发起攻击。Kelani因其不循常规、尖锐犀利的诗作而闻名于世。他运用叙事才华参与打击广为人知的社会陋习，这体现在《Emu Ògùrò》（他在其中无情抨击鲁莽酗酒）和《April Fool》等作品中，后者同样是他尖锐而讽刺的社会评论。Yesufu是敢于率先打破围绕性病古老文化禁忌的勇敢歌匠，他以名曲《À tòsí》（Gonorrhea）作出突破。在Yesufu大胆介入之前，约鲁巴社会被灌输要用欺骗性、浪漫化的标签À rùn Gbajúmò来掩饰这种疾病——仿佛那是一种专属于名人和富人的感染。在歌曲中，Yesufu敦促社会正视残酷的流行病学事实，并揭穿社会固有的虚伪矛盾：人们仅仅因为一种可耻疾病会影响精英，便将其浪漫化。Kelani以被哀痛浸透的声音悼念师父首席鼓手之死，同时说教般讲述死亡绝对不可避免且一视同仁。这首歌最终成为文化史学家经常引用的神圣文献，痛切见证传统约鲁巴歌手与首席鼓手之间形成的深厚、终生精神纽带。Yusuff Olatunji与其首席鼓手Kasumu Ishola Sanni之间，Haruna Ishola与Raufu Ojubanire之间，Lefty Salami与Nosiru Akanmu之间，以及激情澎湃的Ayinla Omowura与Adewole Alao之间，都存在同样牢不可破的共生纽带；Adewole Alao以Onílù Olà之名广为人知，被称为“幸运鼓手”。瘟疫与死亡本身一样，会无情割断这些人间纽带。在Ọyọ-Ilé，Pẹhẹ接连夺去数千名市民的生命。据报道，这场瘟疫是帝国都城连续四年反复暴发流行病的灾难性高潮。它促使著名的Cornish探险家Richard Lander于1827年历史性地访问Ọyọ-Ilé。Lander因与苏格兰探险家Hugh Clapperton一道揭开尼日尔河流向及入海口之谜而声名鹊起，并因此来到帝国都城。Clapperton和探险队其他成员染上热带疾病去世后，英国政府委派Lander返回。他与兄弟乘独木舟从Badagry前往Bussa，最终遭到俘获并被赎回。Lander抵达Ọyọ-Ilé时，记录下自己对帝国当局所设置简陋却井然有序的隔离设施的惊讶。传统议事会把Pẹhẹ患者送往一个隔离中心，该中心设在城外约半英里的一片茂密森林中。Lander在日记中写道，病人被有系统地安置在“树枝之下……”帝国严格的 customary law 规定，Pẹhẹ患者的近亲须负责把食物和水送到森林隔离区外围。然而，此次疫情与 devastating combination of external and internal crises 同时到来，令帝国遭受重创。同年，一场残酷旱灾悄然降临Ọyọ-Ilé。因此，这座大都会同时遭受严重饥荒与政治动荡的双重煎熬，而政治动荡始于十年前的内部争斗。Pẹhẹ疫情犹如把粗盐撒进一道敞开的流血伤口。关于Pẹhẹ的历史描述将其描绘为一种传染性极强的呼吸系统疾病，在各个社会阶层都迅速造成可怕死亡。Aláàfin Májòótú和Ọyọ-Ilé古老的政治架构彻底不堪重负。Lander在笔记中帮助保存了这场悲剧的口述记忆。他记录道，严重饥荒与政治动荡叠加，使那些被隔离在森林收治中心的人的处境雪上加霜。由于患者大多出身贫困，许多人最终并非死于Pẹhẹ病毒本身，而是纯粹饿死。记录显示，尽管Pẹhẹ在1831年直接造成数千人死亡，但Ọyọ-Ilé早已因饥荒、内乱和疾病叠加而失去超过100,000名居民，几近窒息。这场惨重的健康灾难粉碎了旧奥约的人口根基，并令其军事领导层彻底瘫痪。它大幅加速了帝国在Fulani入侵和内部叛乱中走向衰亡，最终导致1835年至1836年间都城Ọyọ-Ilé被完全撤空并永久弃置。瘟疫夺走的不只是生命；一旦应对失当，它们还会推翻帝国。如果殖民前的尼日利亚在遏制传染病传播方面尚且称得上无知，那么数百年后，现代当局若效仿其做法便 outright criminal。在现代医学出现很久以前，水痘和天花等疾病便以同等、无差别的狂怒袭击富人与穷人。面对无法理解或制止天花肆虐的处境，古老约鲁巴人出于纯粹恐惧，将这种疾病神化。天花被奉入神圣神灵殿堂，成为Ṣọnpọnná。由于它会神秘地凭空袭击，这尊神祇被冠以令人畏惧的崇高称号。其中包括Olóde，即“外面之主”或“旷野之主”，意指这种传染病如何在空气与风中无形传播；Ọbalúayé，即“万物之主君王”；以及Babalúayé，即“大地之主父亲”。时至今日，古老的Ilé-Ifẹ仍每年举行Ìtàpá节，以纪念昔日那些天花疫情。当你在神圣节庆中看到Ọbàtálá祭司身上用白色粉笔绘制的精细皮损图案时，你看到的是一种仍在延续的艺术仪式，描绘其祖先所患的皮肤脓疱。Ṣọnpọnná祭司既是备受尊崇的专业医疗人员，也因掌握相关技艺而令人畏惧。他们主持控制天花疫情，举行仪式献祭、施行植物接种、照顾患者，并对病亡者执行严格的单独埋葬，以防止进一步污染。在20世纪全球根除天花以前，没有哪种疾病比天花更令约鲁巴人恐惧 owing to its high transmission rate, swift lethality, and unpredictable seasonality。这种疾病经常在1月至2月间达到高峰，即干燥多尘的harmattan季节，证明自己是一种利用季节性脆弱点的机会主义杀手。同样，霍乱在尼日利亚历史上也曾成为暴烈致命的流行病。它袭击供水，一夜之间摧毁整座社区。但没有任何历史疫情能与1918年流感大流行的可怕传播速度相比。这场疫情于1918年3月起源于美国堪萨斯州，并随第一次世界大战返乡士兵漂洋过海传播，“西班牙流感”很快以夺走的人数超过人类历史上任何其他大流行病的阴惨记录载入史册。它成为首场真正席卷全国的大流行病，由抵达沿海港口的海运乘客和船员直接传入尼日利亚。Lagos是这场悲剧的震中。公共历史学家Oludamola Adebowale指出，在Gold Coast（今加纳）Accra感染病毒的乘客登上了驶往Lagos的船只，并在抵达时播下传染源。疫情传播猛烈到头两个月内，海上隔离措施便彻底崩溃。数周之内，Lagos全部81,941名居民中损失了1.5 per cent，即1.5%。1918年全国人口估计为1,800万，半年内超过500,000名尼日利亚人死亡，全国50 per cent至80 per cent的人口感染病毒。流感从Lagos出发，沿贸易路线如野火般蔓延。1918年10月，Abeokuta出现首例指示病例；Ibadan于1918年10月5日出现首例，随后Oyo、Ilorin、Minna、Bida、Jebba、Zaria、Kano和Bauchi相继出现。Calabar和Onitsha于1918年10月14日出现疫情，病毒又乘船经Forcados港进一步传播至Warri、Asaba、Port Harcourt和Bonny。西班牙流感随尼日尔河上的旅客传播至Lokoja、Sokoto、Maiduguri以及尼日利亚北部其他地区，以至于到1918年12月，全境都已彻底屈服于西班牙流感。旅客沿尼日尔河出行，使西班牙流感深入Lokoja、Sokoto和Maiduguri；到1918年12月，尼日利亚整个地理实体都已彻底屈服于这场毁灭性流感。鉴于这堆积如山的历史悲剧，以及我们近期在COVID-19期间经历的痛苦，尼日利亚当局对阿布jareported Ebola病例目前拖拖拉拉的处理实在令人费解。埃博拉并非抽象威胁。自1976年9月在Ebola River沿岸的Yambuku（位于刚果民主共和国，当时称扎伊尔）首次被发现并夺去首位受害者Mabalo Lokela——一名当地学校校长——以来，这种病毒一直表现出科学界已知最高病例死亡率之一。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/northern-ash.body: Northern Ashanti Mines Limited Company has filed an injunction application seeking to stop a government takeover of its Konongo concession, warning that about $110 million in committed expenditure is at risk. The application, filed at the Commercial Division of the High Court in Accra, seeks to restrain the Minerals Commission and the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources from taking possession of the mine or reallocating it to third parties. The company wants the restrictions to remain in place until the court determines its challenge to the termination of its mining lease. The Attorney-General is also named as a respondent. In a supporting affidavit, Administrative Manager Jonathan Adongo alleges that Minerals Commission officials, accompanied by military personnel, visited the mine on October 22, 2026. He says they ordered the company, its staff and workers to vacate the mine, offices and residential accommodation by midday that day. The company argues that any takeover before the court determines the legality of the lease termination would threaten its investment, equipment and operations. “The threatened military takeover is imminent, and I humbly pray this Honourable Court to hear this application with urgency,” Mr Adongo states. According to the affidavit, Northern Ashanti Mines is wholly Ghanaian-owned and was formerly known as Owere Mines Limited. It is redeveloping the historic Konongo Gold Mine in the Ashanti Region. The company says it renewed its lease on February 2, 2023, for 13 years, covering about 125 square kilometres. It maintains that Parliament ratified the renewed lease, which runs until February 1, 2036. It says it has committed capital and incurred expenditure exceeding US$83.34 million on the concession. It also recently secured a facility of more than US$30 million to develop a gold processing plant, which it describes as more than 50% complete. The affidavit puts its committed expenditure at about US$110 million and says the company employs approximately 422 people directly and indirectly. The dispute follows a termination notice dated April 30, 2026, issued by the Minerals Commission on behalf of the minister. Northern Ashanti Mines disputes that position. It says no notice of any breach was served and that it was given no opportunity to remedy alleged breaches or explain why its mineral rights should not be cancelled. The company says it received no response to a letter from its lawyers dated May 4 and a petition dated May 20 seeking a review and reversal of the decision. Its injunction application also seeks to prevent security deployments intended to enforce the termination and to stop the granting or transfer of mineral rights over the concession. The company argues that a forcible takeover could endanger staff and surrounding communities, damage equipment and destroy exploration records and geological data. It is asking the court to preserve its possession of the concession pending the final determination of its judicial review application

https://www.myjoyonline.com/northern-ash.body_zh: Northern Ashanti Mines Limited Company已提交禁制令申请，请求阻止政府接管其科农戈采矿特许区，并警告约1.10亿美元的已承诺支出面临风险。该申请提交给阿克拉高等法院商事法庭，旨在限制矿产委员会和土地与自然资源部长接管该矿场，或将其重新分配给第三方。在法院就该公司针对终止采矿租约提出的异议作出裁决之前，该公司希望相关限制措施继续有效。总检察长也被列为答辩人。在一份支持性宣誓书中，行政经理Jonathan Adongo称，矿产委员会官员于2026年10月22日在军事人员陪同下前往该矿场。他表示，这些官员命令公司、其员工和工人在当日中午前搬离矿场、办公室和宿舍。公司认为，在法院裁定终止租约是否合法之前进行任何接管，都会危及公司的投资、设备和运营。Adongo先生表示：“军方接管迫在眉睫，我恳请尊敬的法院紧急审理本项申请。”据宣誓书称，Northern Ashanti Mines由加纳人全资拥有，原名Owere Mines Limited。该公司正在重新开发阿散蒂地区的历史悠久的科农戈金矿。公司表示，其于2023年2月2日续签租约，期限为13年，涉及约125平方公里。公司坚持认为，议会已批准续签的租约，该租约有效期至2036年2月1日。公司称，已在该特许区投入资本并发生超过8334万美元的支出。公司最近还获得了超过3000万美元的融资，用于开发一座黄金加工厂，并称该厂已完成50%以上。宣誓书称，其已承诺支出约为1.10亿美元，公司直接和间接雇用约422人。此次争端源于矿产委员会代表部长于2026年4月30日发出的终止通知。Northern Ashanti Mines对该立场提出异议。公司称，未收到任何违约通知，也未获机会纠正所指控的违约行为或说明为何不应取消其矿产权利。公司表示，对于其律师于5月4日发出的信函，以及5月20日提交、要求审查并推翻该决定的申诉，它均未收到任何回复。其禁制令申请还寻求阻止为执行终止决定而部署安全人员，并阻止就该特许区授予或转让矿产权利。公司认为，强行接管可能危及员工和周边社区、损坏设备，并毁坏勘探记录和地质数据。公司请求法院在其司法审查申请获得最终裁决期间，允许其继续占有该特许区

Unlock these with Subscription Education Minister Ashish Sood said on Sunday that the Delhi government will set up medical rooms in all 1,086 government schools at a cost of ₹48.87 crore to provide immediate first aid and care to students during school hours. The medical rooms will provide basic first aid, including wound dressing, administration of ORS and temporary rest under trained supervision. However, diagnostic services and prescription medicines will not be provided in schools. Mr. Sood said a trained health worker, such as an Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM) or a multipurpose health worker, will be engaged in each school to address immediate health needs and provide adolescent health support. “Every child in our government schools deserves a safe and caring environment. When a student falls sick or gets hurt during school hours, parents and teachers should have peace of mind knowing that immediate first aid and proper care are readily available right inside the school campus,” he said. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/b.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s remarks at a Patna event on Sunday (October 25, 2026), in which he dragged Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father, triggered a sharp reaction from senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders, who accused the principal Opposition, under Rahul Gandhi’s leadership, of increasingly resorting to personal attacks against Mr. Modi and his family. Criticising the “ Modi ka baap bhi jayega [even Modi’s father will go]” comment, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Mr. Kharge has “torn apart all norms of decorum”. “This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modi ji or his family,” he said, accusing the party of having hurled insults at the Prime Minister’s mother, calling him a “merchant of death”, and mocking his poverty by addressing him as a “chaiwala” in the past. “Under Rahul Gandhi’s leadership, the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day,” he said, alleging that repeated electoral defeats over the past 12 years had bred “desperation and frustration” within the party. “Only the politics of slander remains. Having lost its public base among the people, Congress is now steadily losing its base even among its own workers. Whenever they have made hateful comments against Modi ji or his family, the public has given Congress a resounding response every time,” said Mr. Shah on X . Terming Mr. Kharge’s language “indecent and unparliamentary”, BJP chief Nitin Nabin said: “There is a certain dignity to political opposition as well, but dragging the departed family members into speeches from public platforms has now become the real ‘culture’ of Rahul Gandhi and the whole Opposition. This is not Kharge ji’s personal statement, but a reflection of the entire Congress party’s lack of decorum in its thinking.” “Frustrated by repeated electoral defeats, the Congress party is venting its political spite against Prime Minister Modi ji and his family through baseless and irresponsible comments. The Opposition’s panic — stemming from Modi ji ’s rising popularity at home and abroad, and the public’s unwavering trust in him — is now plainly evident in its language and conduct,” said Union Minister J.P. Nadda. He said that in a democracy, opponents must not “cross the bounds of propriety”, and the people will respond to such politics. “The Congress must realise that the trust of the people cannot be won through a politics of hatred and humiliation. The people of the country will surely deliver their response to such petty politics through democratic means,” he said. Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/e.body: The Lagos State Government has intensified preparedness against Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) following the confirmation of an index case in Abuja, upgrading its isolation centre and targeting laboratory test results within 24 hours. The state Commissioner for Health, Prof. Akin Abayomi, disclosed this in a statement, saying Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu had directed relevant agencies to maintain a high level of alertness and preparedness. Abayomi said Lagos was treating the situation as a priority because of the constant movement of people between Lagos and Abuja. He said the state’s Emergency Operations Centre had been working ahead of the confirmed case, with teams conducting simulation exercises to ensure responders understood their roles. According to him, the state’s isolation centre has been upgraded, while additional capacity is being developed. Training for health workers in public and private facilities is also ongoing, with emphasis on infection prevention and control. The commissioner said the state was establishing a clear pathway for laboratory testing, targeting results within 24 hours. “Our isolation centre has been upgraded, and additional capacity is ongoing,” Abayomi said. “We are defining a clear pathway from sample to result, targeting results within 24 hours.” He added that a dedicated Ebola Research Committee was reviewing the latest evidence on treatments and vaccines to guide decisions. Abayomi said the state was also refining screening at airports and other points of entry in collaboration with federal partners. He noted that disease surveillance was being digitally enhanced on SHIP to improve the detection, tracing and real-time response to suspected cases. The commissioner urged residents to wash their hands regularly with soap and water and avoid contact with the blood and body fluids of anyone who was ill. He advised anyone experiencing fever, weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, or who suspected exposure to the virus, not to self-medicate but to call health authorities before visiting a health facility. Abayomi also urged health workers to maintain a high index of suspicion, ask patients about their travel history and use personal protective equipment. Residents were advised to report suspected cases or exposure through the Lagos State emergency numbers, 112 and 767, or the Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health on 0802 316 9485. He urged residents to remain calm, stay alert and rely on official information from the Lagos State Ministry of Health. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/e.title_zh: 埃博拉：拉各斯升级隔离中心，力争24小时内出具检测结果
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/e.body_zh: 拉各斯州政府在阿布贾确认首例病例后，加强了应对埃博拉病毒病（EVD）的准备工作，升级隔离中心，并力争在24小时内出具实验室检测结果。该州卫生专员Akin Abayomi教授在一份声明中透露了这一情况，并表示州长Babajide Sanwo-Olu已指示相关机构保持高度警觉和充分准备。Abayomi说，由于人员经常在拉各斯和阿布贾之间往来，拉各斯将应对局势列为优先事项。他说，该州应急行动中心在确诊病例得到确认前就已展开工作，各团队开展模拟演练，确保应急人员的职责得到明确。据他介绍，该州隔离中心已经升级，同时正在扩大收治能力。公立和私立医疗机构卫生人员的培训也仍在进行，重点是感染预防与控制。专员表示，该州正在建立明确的实验室检测流程，力争在24小时内得出结果。Abayomi说：“我们的隔离中心已经升级，额外capacity仍在建设中。我们正在明确从样本采集到结果出具的清晰流程，力争在24小时内得出结果。”他补充说，专设的埃博拉研究委员会正在审查有关治疗方法和疫苗的最新证据，以指导决策。Abayomi表示，该州还在与联邦层面合作伙伴协作，进一步完善机场和其他入境口岸的筛查工作。他指出，该州正在利用SHIP加强疾病监测的数字化能力，以改进对疑似病例的发现、追踪和实时响应。专员敦促居民经常使用肥皂和水洗手，并避免接触任何患病者的血液和体液。他建议，出现发热、乏力、呕吐、腹泻或原因不明的出血，或怀疑自己接触过病毒的人，不要自行用药，而应在前往医疗机构前致电卫生部门。Abayomi还敦促卫生人员保持高度警惕，询问患者的旅行史，并使用个人防护装备。居民如发现疑似病例或存在暴露情况，应通过拉各斯州紧急号码112和767，或拨打流行病学、生物安全和全球安全局电话0802 316 9485进行报告。他敦促居民保持冷静、提高警觉，并依赖拉各斯州卫生部发布的官方信息。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都领地以及世界各地设有办公室。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过各类平台面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级报道新闻，同时充当抱负者、千禧一代接触新思想、文化和技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相和理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直至探索人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

Unlock these with Subscription Theoretical physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal , becoming the first Indian laureate to receive the honour, awarded by Stockholm University and the Nobel Committee for Physics of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. The Medal recognises significant contributions to theoretical physics. Dr. Sen is the ICTS-Infosys Madhava Chair Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS), Bengaluru. He also delivered the memorial lecture accompanying the Medal in Stockholm on October 22, under the title ‘Gravity from Strings and Strings from Gravity’. In his career, Dr. Sen has focused on string theory, which is the name of an attempt by physicists to describe matter and nature’s fundamental forces, including gravity, within a single framework called quantum gravity. Currently, they are split across two frameworks, quantum physics and relativity. String theory offers ways to reconcile them, but while it is mathematically a highly evolved theory, it has been unable to make predictions that can be confirmed with experiments using today’s technologies. In the 1980s, Dr. Sen helped establish how the equations describing hypothetical strings moving through space could relate to the equations that describe the physical fields that surround it. In the 1990s, he helped show that two apparently different ways to describe physical forces were really equivalent, an idea called S-duality. He also proposed three related ideas, together called the Sen conjectures, in 1999 that gave physicists new ways to understand the behaviour of the strings of string theory. Dr. Sen graduated from Presidency College in Kolkata before going to IIT-Kanpur and thereon to earning his PhD from Stony Brook University, New York, in 1982. After working at institutions including the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) in Mumbai and the Harish-Chandra Research Institute (HRI) in Prayagraj, he moved to ICTS in 2021. For his work, he has won the S.S. Bhatnagar Prize (1994), the Infosys Prize (2009), the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics (2012), and the Dirac Medal (2014). He also received the Padma Shri in 2001 and the Padma Bhushan in 2013. The impact of Dr. Sen’s contributions has exceeded their own ambit. In one 2014 interview, U.S. theoretical physicist Edward Witten — widely considered to be the greatest living mathematical physicist — called one of Dr. Sen’s papers “short but brilliant” and that it “convinced me that the duality had to be right”. Dr. Witten also said Dr. Sen’s findings had inspired work that paved the way for more breakthroughs in understanding how subatomic particles interact with each other. He has also done important work on black holes. Physicists had long known that these enigmatic cosmic beasts had entropy but could not explain its origins in their physical theories. Dr. Sen developed mathematical methods to make sense of a black hole’s microscopic states in a way that could account for its observable, macroscopic characteristics. Together, many physicists agree, his contributions have considerably advanced the theories physicists use to understand quantum gravity. The Oskar Klein Medal and the accompanying Memorial Lectures were launched in 1988 to honour the Swedish physicist Oskar Klein (1894-1977). In 1926, Klein, building on the work of German mathematician Theodor Kaluza, explored whether electromagnetism and gravity could be described in a common framework by introducing an extra dimension of space. The result, known as Kaluza-Klein theory, exerted a significant influence on later attempts by physicists — including string theory — to unify these forces. India in particular has an influential community of string theorists, especially at TIFR Mumbai, ICTS Bengaluru, HRI Prayagraj, and the Indian Institute of Science Education Research in Pune. Aside from Dr. Sen, the community’s notable members include Nabamita Banerjee, Shiraz Minwalla, Sunil Mukhi, P. Ramadevi, and Spenta Wadia. Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 理论物理学家 Ashoke Sen 荣获2026年奥斯卡·克莱因奖章，成为首位获此殊荣的印度人。该奖章由斯德哥尔摩大学和瑞典皇家科学院诺贝尔物理学委员会颁发，旨在表彰对理论物理学的重大贡献。Sen 博士是位于班加罗尔的国际理论科学中心（ICTS）ICTS-Infosys Madhava 讲席教授。10月22日，他还在斯德哥尔摩发表了与奖章配套的纪念讲座，题为《来自弦的重力与来自重力的弦》。

在其职业生涯中，Sen 博士主要专注于弦理论。弦理论是物理学家试图在名为量子引力的单一框架内描述物质以及自然界基本作用力（包括引力）的一种理论。目前，这些基本作用力分属量子物理学和相对论两大理论框架。弦理论为协调二者提供了途径，但尽管从数学角度看它已经发展得十分成熟，却仍无法借助当今技术通过实验加以验证的预言。

20世纪80年代，Sen 博士帮助确立了描述假想弦在空间中运动的方程与描述其周围物理场的方程之间的联系。20世纪90年代，他帮助证明两种表面看来不同的物理作用力描述方式实际上是等价的，这一思想被称为 S 对偶性。1999年，他还提出了三个彼此相关的概念，合称 Sen 猜想，为物理学家理解弦理论中弦的行为提供了新途径。

Sen 博士毕业于加尔各答的 Presidency College，之后就读于 IIT-Kanpur，并于1982年在纽约州石溪大学取得博士学位。他曾在包括孟买 Tata Institute of Fundamental Research（TIFR）和普拉亚格拉杰 Harish-Chandra Research Institute（HRI）在内的多家机构任职，2021年转入 ICTS。

凭借其研究成果，他曾获得 S.S. Bhatnagar Prize（1994年）、Infosys Prize（2009年）、Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics（2012年）以及 Dirac Medal（2014年）。他还于2001年获得 Padma Shri 勋章，并于2013年获得 Padma Bhushan 勋章。

Sen 博士贡献所产生的影响已经超出了这些成果本身的范围。在2014年的一次采访中，美国理论物理学家 Edward Witten——他被广泛认为是当代最杰出的数学物理学家——称 Sen 博士的一篇论文“简短却精彩”，并表示这篇论文“使我确信这种对偶性必定是正确的”。Witten 博士还指出，Sen 博士的研究成果启发了一系列工作，为进一步突破人们理解亚原子粒子如何相互作用的认识铺平了道路。

他还就黑洞开展了重要研究。长期以来，物理学家一直知道这些神秘的天体具有熵，却无法在物理理论中解释熵的起源。Sen 博士发展出数学方法，以一种能够解释黑洞可观测的宏观特征的方式，理解黑洞的微观状态。许多物理学家一致认为，他的贡献极大推进了物理学家用于理解量子引力的理论。

奥斯卡·克莱因奖章及其配套纪念讲座于1988年设立，旨在纪念瑞典物理学家奥斯卡·克莱因（1894—1977）。1926年，克莱因在德国数学家 Theodor Kaluza 研究的基础上，通过引入一个额外的空间维度，探索电磁学和引力能否置于同一框架内描述。其成果称为 Kaluza-Klein 理论，对后来物理学家统一这些作用力的尝试产生了重要影响，其中包括弦理论。

印度尤其拥有一批颇具影响力的弦理论学家，主要分布在孟买 TIFR、班加罗尔 ICTS、普拉亚格拉杰 HRI 以及浦那的 Indian Institute of Science Education Research。除 Sen 博士外，该群体中值得关注的成员还包括 Nabamita Banerjee、Shiraz Minwalla、Sunil Mukhi、P. Ramadevi 和 Spenta Wadia。

Unlock these with Subscription A day after attempts were made to forcibly remove protesting students at Jamia Millia Islamia university, students gathered around the campus and tried to enter by climbing the gates on Sunday (October 25, 2026). With classes suspended, water facilities on the campus were cut off and no entry or exit was allowed. Amid heavy police deployment, students still gathered in large numbers and staged a protest. On Saturday (October 24), security personnel, teaching and non-teaching staff attempted to remove the students protesting since October 11 for restoration of their students’ union. The tent was uprooted from the lawn inside gate no. 7, campus electricity and water facilities suspended, gates and libraries closed and all classes announced to be conducted online until further notice. Following this, students gathered in large numbers and stayed through the night, singing songs, raising slogans and demanding the restoration of JMISU. On Sunday (October 25), a similar scenario was observed, with heavy CRPF and Delhi Police personnel guarding the entry gates and dispersing the students who were trying to enter. “We have been trying to go inside the campus but the security personnel are not allowing us. They have barricaded gate no. 7 and no entry is allowed from other gates as well. In the afternoon, some students from the hostel tried to access the health centre from gate no. 4 but were not allowed,” said Md. Zubair, a second year Bachelor’s student. With entry and exit banned, students inside the campus were unable to access filtered water, had to rely on friends to get water for them. Some students wanting to join the protest also climbed gates and entered. Delhi Police personnel stopped many students from entering by pulling and physically handling them. Some students were also detained. Around 1:00 p.m., the Vice-Chancellor, along with administration and other staff, visited the campus, inspected the gates and security arrangements and left without interacting with the students. “We have been demanding a dialogue with the V-C and the Chief Proctor on the restoration of JMISU that has been non-existent since 2006. After inviting students for a dialogue, the V-C used force to remove us and end our protest,” alleged Habeeba, one of the students removed from the hostel. An FIR has been registered under the charges of trespassing, defacement of property and confinement against political leaders and students following a complaint sent by Jamia administration, the police officials said. The complaint was sent by the Economics department mentioning trespassing and damage to public property. “The complaint contains names of MPs, leaders, students and ex-students who were trying to trespass on campus property. The FIR has been registered under the charges of criminal trespassing, wrongful confinement and voluntarily causing hurt under BNS. We have also added Sections from Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, as per the complaint,” Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police, South East, said. Three persons including two women were detained from outside the campus on Sunday. “The two women were not connected with Jamia at all. They were neither students, nor ex-students or associated with any student party or union. They were creating law and order problems and were detained. They were released before sunset,” the officer said. “Another person was held under Preventive Detention. The man works with a food delivery app and is educated only till class 10. We found his activities suspicious and are currently questioning him for his purpose of being at the site. We will present him before the SEM tomorrow,” the officer added. Students were informally being told to vacate the hostel on account of online classes and upcoming festivals. “The campus has moved online. There is no reason for anyone to stay on campus. They are also being asked to vacate informally as it is the festive season and parents like to see them at home,” an official from the Jamia administration said. “Dialogue has been happening since day one. On Saturday (October 24), the entire Jamia, including professors, the administration and even the non-teaching staff, went to meet the students, but they did not want to end their protest,” the official said. On being asked why the students were forcibly removed, the official said, “If they had been removed, they would not have been there still.” Responding to water facilities being suspended, the official said that since the campus was moved online, there was no question for students or anyone else to access these facilities. “The staff is not there. 在有人试图强行驱散抗议学生仅一天后，2026年10月25日（星期日），Jamia Millia Islamia大学的学生聚集在校园周围，试图攀爬大门进入校园。由于停课，校园供水设施被切断，任何人不得进出。在警方重兵部署的情况下，学生仍大批聚集并举行抗议。10月24日（星期六），安保人员以及教职员工和非教学人员试图驱散自10月11日起抗议、要求恢复学生会的学生。7号门内草坪上的帐篷被连根拔起，校园供电和供水设施被暂停，大门和图书馆关闭，并宣布所有课程在另行通知前改为在线进行。随后，学生大批聚集并彻夜留在校园内，唱歌、呼喊口号，要求恢复JMISU。

10月25日（星期日），类似情况再次出现，大量CRPF人员和德里警察在各个入口把守，驱散试图进入校园的学生。二年级学士生Md. Zubair说：“我们一直试图进入校园，但安保人员不允许。他们封锁了7号门，其他门也不准进入。下午，一些宿舍学生试图从4号门前往健康中心，但同样未获准。”

由于禁止进出，校园内的学生无法使用过滤水，只能请朋友替他们取水。一些想要参加抗议的学生也翻越大门进入校园。德里警察通过拉拽和强行控制等方式阻止许多学生进入，部分学生还遭到拘留。下午1点左右，校长与行政人员及其他教职员工到访校园，视察各处大门和安保安排，但没有与学生交谈，随后离开。

一名被赶出宿舍的学生Habeeba指称：“我们一直要求与校长和首席教务长对话，讨论恢复自2006年起便已停止运作的JMISU。校长在邀请学生对话后，却动用武力驱赶我们，企图结束抗议。”

警方官员表示，Jamia管理层提交投诉后，已针对政治人士和学生以非法侵入、破坏财物和非法拘禁等罪名立案。投诉由经济学系提交，内容涉及非法侵入和损坏公共财物。

东南区警察additional deputy commissioner表示：“投诉中列出了试图非法侵入校园财物的国会议员、领导人、学生和往届学生姓名。我们已依据BNS，以刑事非法侵入、非法拘禁和故意伤害等罪名立案。根据投诉内容，我们还加入了《德里防止破坏财物法》的相关条款。”

星期日，3人在校园外被拘留，其中包括2名女性。该官员说：“这两名女性与Jamia毫无关系。她们既不是学生，也不是往届学生，也未与任何学生政党或学生会有关。她们正在制造治安问题，因此遭到拘留。两名女性在日落前获释。”

该官员补充道：“另一人依据预防性拘留规定被拘留。这名男子为一家外卖平台工作，只读到10年级。我们发现其行动可疑，目前正在询问他出现在现场的目的。明天我们将把他带到SEM面前。”

由于课程改为在线进行且节庆将至，校方还在非正式地要求学生搬离宿舍。Jamia管理层的一名官员说：“校园已经转为在线模式，任何人都没有理由留在校园。正值节庆季节，家长也希望看到孩子回家，因此校方也在非正式地要求他们搬离。”

该官员说：“对话从第一天起就一直在进行。10月24日（星期六），包括教授、管理人员甚至非教学人员在内的整个Jamia都去见学生，但他们不愿结束抗议。”

当被问及为何强行驱赶学生时，该官员说：“如果他们已经被驱走，就不会再出现在那里了。”

针对供水设施暂停的问题，该官员表示，由于校园已经转为在线模式，学生和其他任何人都没有理由使用这些设施。他说：“教职员工不在，大门和图书馆都已关闭，课程在线进行。他们没有理由待在那里。”
