https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: Nigeria and six other countries under the High Ambition Coalition (HAC) for Nature and People have won $50,000 seed grants each under the Rapid Deployment Mechanism (RDM) to execute projects aimed at accelerating progress towards their 30×30 conservation targets. The grants were announced and awarded on the sidelines of the ongoing 17th session of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17) in Armenia. The beneficiary countries are Costa Rica, Mexico, Nigeria, Nepal, Zambia, Rwanda, and Kenya, each receiving a certificate confirming a $50,000 grant for its respective project. Nigeria received the grant for its project proposal titled “Strengthening Nigeria’s 30×30 Progress through Ecological Connectivity, Terrestrial and Marine OECMs, and Protected Area Management Effectiveness”. PREMIUM TIMES gathered that the project will be implemented by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF). Costa Rica’s project, titled “From 30×30 Coverage to Effective Conservation: Developing an Acceptable Visitation Load Tool for Cocos Island National Park”, seeks to improve conservation management at the national park. Mexico received the grant for its project, “Strengthening Mexico’s Marine 30×30 through Underwater Acoustic Baselines and Evidence-Based Protected Area Management”. Nepal’s project, “Operationalising Nepal’s National OECM Guideline: Recognising New OECMs to Advance the 30×30 Target”, focuses on recognising other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs) to advance its conservation target. Zambia’s project is titled “Strengthening Zambia’s 30×30 Progress through the Busanga Swamps Wetland Inventory and Management Effectiveness Assessment”. Rwanda’s project, “Advancing Rwanda’s 30×30 Commitments through Community-Based Terrestrial OECMs and Ecological Connectivity”, seeks to strengthen community-based conservation and ecological connectivity. Kenya’s project, “Advancing Kenya’s Marine 30×30 through Community-Led OECMs, Indigenous and Local Knowledge, and Effective Marine Protected Area Management”, focuses on marine conservation. Nigeria’s award was presented to Sikeade Egbuwalo, the country’s focal point to the Convention on Biological Diversity. Representatives of the other beneficiary countries also took turns receiving their awards, except Kenya, whose representative was unavoidably absent. In her remarks, Mrs Egbuwalo appreciated the HAC secretariat and the RDM for the recognition and support. “This support will not only help us to achieve the 30×30 targets but also help us to address the issue of fragmented habitat, which has been a big issue in Nigeria,” she said. The RDM is an initiative of the HAC for Nature and People designed to address funding gaps by providing small-scale financing to catalyse broader conservation impacts. “By providing fast, flexible seed grants, the RDM bridges the gap between early-stage requirements and larger funding sources, helping countries accelerate actions to achieve their 30×30 goals,” the organisers said. During the gala, some recipients of the 2025 RDM grants shared their experiences and highlighted the funding’s importance to biodiversity conservation efforts in their respective countries. In his closing remarks, Labaran Ahmed, Nigeria’s Chief Scientific Officer at the Federal Department of Forestry and HAC for Nature and People Co-Chair, expressed the Nigerian government’s appreciation to the HAC secretariat for its deliberations. “We look forward to seeing your projects move forward and contribute to your country’s effort to achieve the 30×30 targets,” he said. In his reaction to the award, Director-General of the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF), Joseph Onoja, said the award represents a significant milestone in Nigeria’s conservation journey and reinforces NCF’s leadership in advancing biodiversity conservation, ecological connectivity, and sustainable natural resource management. “Working in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Environment, NCF will provide scientific and technical support to the Federal Government of Nigeria in advancing the country’s commitment to the global 30×30 target of conserving at least 30% of land and sea by 2030,” he said. Mr Onoja explained that the project will identify, map, and profile priority terrestrial and marine Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs); assess protected area management effectiveness; and develop a national Management Effectiveness Framework. These interventions, he said, will generate critical evidence and recommendations to strengthen Nigeria’s protected and conserved area network, improve conservation governance, and support the implementation of Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. He said the award underscores the importance of strategic partnerships between government and conservation organisations in translating global biodiversity commitments into measurable national outcomes. “NCF remains committed to working closely with the Federal Ministry of Environment, relevant government agencies, research institutions, conservation partners, and local communities to strengthen ecological connectivity, improve protected area management, and advance Nigeria’s 30×30 ambition,” he said. Mr Onoja said the initiative represents an important investment in Nigeria’s ecological future, safeguarding biodiversity, strengthening ecosystem resilience, and ensuring that nature continues to support the wellbeing and livelihoods of present and future generations
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title_zh: CBD COP17：尼日利亚等7个国家各获得5万美元拨款，用于开展生物多样性项目
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: 尼日利亚和另外6个加入“自然与人民雄心联盟”（HAC）的国家，在“快速部署机制”（RDM）下各获得了5万美元的种子拨款，用于实施旨在加快实现30×30保护目标的项目。这些拨款是在亚美尼亚举行的《联合国生物多样性公约》第17次缔约方大会（CBD COP17）会议期间宣布并授予的。受益国家包括哥斯达黎加、墨西哥、尼日利亚、尼泊尔、赞比亚、卢旺达和肯尼亚，各国均收到一份证书，确认其各自项目获得5万美元拨款。尼日利亚的项目提案题为《通过生态连通性、陆地和海洋其他有效区域保护措施以及保护区管理效能，加强尼日利亚30×30进展》，并获得了这笔拨款。PREMIUM TIMES获悉，该项目将由尼日利亚自然保护基金会（NCF）实施。哥斯达黎加的项目题为《从30×30覆盖到有效保护：为科科斯岛国家公园开发可接受的游客承载量工具》，旨在改善该国家公园的保护管理。墨西哥凭借《通过水下声学基线和循证保护区管理加强墨西哥海洋30×30》项目获得了拨款。尼泊尔的项目《落实尼泊尔国家其他有效区域保护措施指南：确认新的其他有效区域保护措施以推进30×30目标》，重点确认其他有效区域保护措施（OECMs），以推进其保护目标。赞比亚的项目题为《通过Busanga沼泽湿地资源清查和管理效能评估，加强赞比亚30×30进展》。卢旺达的项目《通过社区主导的陆地其他有效区域保护措施和生态连通性，推进卢旺达30×30承诺》旨在加强社区保护及生态连通性。肯尼亚的项目《通过社区主导的其他有效区域保护措施、原住民和地方知识以及有效的海洋保护区管理，推进肯尼亚海洋30×30》侧重于海洋保护。尼日利亚的奖项授予了该国在《生物多样性公约》框架下的联络点Sikeade Egbuwalo。其他受益国家的代表也轮流领取了各自奖项，但肯尼亚代表因不可避免的原因缺席。Egbuwalo女士在致辞中感谢HAC秘书处和RDM的认可与支持。她说：“这项支持不仅将帮助我们实现30×30目标，也将帮助我们应对栖息地碎片化这一在尼日利亚一直非常突出的问题。”RDM是“自然与人民雄心联盟”的一项倡议，旨在通过提供小规模融资弥合资金缺口，从而推动更广泛的保护影响。组织方表示：“通过提供快速、灵活的种子拨款，RDM弥合了早期项目需求与较大规模资金来源之间的差距，帮助各国加快行动，实现其30×30目标。”在晚宴上，部分2025年RDM拨款获得者分享了自身经历，并强调这笔资金对各自国家生物多样性保护工作的重要性。尼日利亚联邦林业部首席科学官兼“自然与人民雄心联盟”共同主席Labaran Ahmed在闭幕致辞中，对HAC秘书处的审议工作表示了尼日利亚政府的感谢。他说：“我们期待看到你们的项目顺利推进，并为各自国家实现30×30目标作出贡献。”尼日利亚自然保护基金会（NCF）总干事Joseph Onoja在谈及获奖时表示，这一奖项是尼日利亚保护进程中的重要里程碑，也进一步体现了NCF在推进生物多样性保护、生态连通性和自然资源可持续管理方面的领导作用。他说：“NCF将与联邦环境部合作，为尼日利亚联邦政府推进本国对全球30×30目标的承诺提供科学和技术支持，即到2030年至少保护30%的陆地和海洋。”Onoja先生表示，该项目将识别、绘制并重点分析优先开展的其他有效区域保护措施（OECMs）；评估保护区管理效能；并制定国家管理效能框架。他说，这些干预措施将产生关键证据和建议，以加强尼日利亚受保护区域和保育区域网络、改善保护治理，并支持落实《昆明—蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架》第3项目标。他表示，这项奖励凸显了政府与保护组织之间建立战略伙伴关系的重要性，有助于把全球生物多样性承诺转化为可衡量的国家成果。他说：“NCF仍致力于与联邦环境部、相关政府机构、研究机构、保护伙伴和当地社区密切合作，加强生态连通性、改善保护区管理，并推进尼日利亚的30×30愿景。”Onoja先生表示，该倡议代表了对尼日利亚生态未来的重要投入，有助于保护生物多样性、增强生态系统韧性，并确保自然持续为当代和子孙后代的福祉与生计提供支持

https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/lead/ja.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Over the past few months, three distinct streams of dissent have emerged in India: the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) -led agitation , actions by left-wing student organisations, and campaigns spearheaded by the Congress and the INDIA bloc . Although these streams have largely evolved independently, their paths have increasingly converged around shared concerns about democracy, dissent, citizens’ rights and the fairness of the political and electoral process. Their significance lies in their capacity to bring disparate grievances and constituencies together in a broader challenge to the government. The first phase of the agitation unfolded at Jantar Mantar in June and July, focusing on education reform, the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) paper leaks and demands for the (then) Education Minister’s resignation . The CJP played a pivotal role in galvanising public discontent, drawing large numbers of young people into the streets, where they articulated their grievances through a distinctive blend of humour, creativity and youthful energy. This indicated that dissatisfaction with the ruling establishment extended well beyond the established Opposition parties, with the political disaffection of this constituency having been seriously underestimated. The Minister’s eventual resignation gave the movement fresh impetus, demonstrating that sustained public pressure could secure political concessions. On Gandhi Jayanti, Opposition parties, student groups and civil society activists took to the streets, demanding the Chief Election Commissioner’s (CEC) resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Mobile Internet services were suspended around Jantar Mantar, gates at a number of Metro stations were closed, and more than 700 protesters were detained in the vicinity by the police. The CJP’s call for a protest at Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 met with an even heavier crackdown. A massive deployment of police and paramilitary forces brought much of the capital to a near standstill, effectively preventing the gathering from taking place. Two days later, thousands gathered in central Delhi for the unprecedented ‘Dilli Chalo’ march, led by Leader of the Opposition (Lok Sabha) Rahul Gandhi, Congress and prominent INDIA bloc leaders. ALSO WATCH “Losing faith in elections”: Ground zero at Jantar Mantar’s massive Oct 2 protest The contrast was telling. While the ‘Dilli Chalo’ march showed the Congress’s capacity to draw large crowds onto the streets, the CJP’s calls brought youth discontent into sharper public focus. For Mr. Gandhi, this offered an opportunity to unite various concerns and channel them towards a more focused political agenda. The Jantar Mantar uprising created new political space outside parties. Its most significant contribution was to break the climate of fear. The mass protest demonstrated the ability of established Opposition parties, particularly the Congress, to consolidate concerns over electoral integrity, institutional accountability and the right to protest into a broader political challenge to the government. While movements can mobilise people and articulate dissent, parties provide the organisational means to sustain it and translate it into political action. Neither form of collective action is sufficient on its own. Ultimately, political change depends on parties being able to turn mass mobilisation into a sustained challenge to those in power. At the heart of this public upsurge is a widening struggle over the sanctity of the vote, a cornerstone of democracy. By early September 2026, the exercise had resulted in the exclusion of 13.37 crore names from draft electoral rolls across 30 States and Union Territories — equivalent to 14.1% of the pre-SIR electorate — raising concerns about the possible disenfranchisement of eligible voters. The central question is whether the revision is transparent, verifiable and subject to adequate safeguards against arbitrary exclusion, particularly given concerns about the reliability of the procedures and centralised software used to remove names. The protest, accompanied by a petition to the Supreme Court of India seeking an investigation, an audit of voter deletions, safeguards against arbitrary exclusion and suspension of the process, underscored the political force of a convergence between mass participation, Opposition mobilisation and legal action. The petition also put the judiciary to the test, challenging it to protect constitutional rights through judicial review rather than allow executive decisions to evade scrutiny. The ECI’s independence had already been questioned following the enactment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which excluded the Chief Justice of India from the panel appointing Election Commissioners (ECs) and provided immunity from civil and criminal proceedings for acts undertaken in the discharge of official duties. Reports of disagreements among the ECs over unilateral decisions taken by the CEC further fuelled questions about the ECI’s functioning. These doubts intensified opposition to SIR, adding a new dimension to the challenge by linking electoral administration to democratic accountability. Thousands have taken to the streets, protesting the voter-list overhaul and raising concerns over the ECI’s constitutional obligation to act impartially. Gathering momentum since early October, the protests signal a significant shift in Opposition politics. The demand for scrapping SIR and the CEC’s resignation, once unthinkable, has emerged as a rallying point of protests. It has also brought the contest over electoral fairness beyond the institutional arenas of Parliament and the courts and onto the streets. When eligible citizens are excluded from voter rolls without adequate safeguards or effective remedies, the conduct of elections alone cannot guarantee democratic legitimacy. These concerns have raised the spectre of a shift from electoral democracy towards electoral autocracy, underscoring the extent of democratic backsliding in the country. The current political moment exposes the vulnerabilities beneath the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)’s dominance, as growing public resentment begins to test its hold on power. The BJP’s failure to secure a parliamentary majority in the 2024 general election had already dented its aura of invincibility. Meanwhile, the government’s efforts to reshape the electoral architecture through multiple mechanisms have fuelled concerns that it seeks to institutionalise a permanent majority and forestall a recurrence of its electoral setback. Unable to offer political solutions, the government has instead deployed its coercive powers to quell dissent, particularly among the youth. Such measures, however, cannot obscure deeper concerns over the erosion of the constitutionally guaranteed right to vote. Nor can the government deflect scrutiny by accusing the Opposition, the CJP or left-wing groups of fomenting anarchy or conspiring to bring down the regime. Such allegations of regime change — which simply means transition of power through elections — are especially unconvincing given the BJP’s own record of pursuing regime change of governments whose policies, programmes and practices it opposed. By resorting to repression, the government has exposed the limits of its political dominance and sharpened the disconnect between the young and the ruling party, as well as eroded trust in the institutions it controls. In short, it is losing the plot. The larger democratic stakes are clear: this is ultimately a fight over the foundation of democracy itself — the right to vote. Although these developments have yet to produce a new political alignment, they have widened the space for dissent and intensified scrutiny of the concentration of executive power. Most strikingly, the ECI has come to be seen as a proxy for the executive, with doubts about its impartiality sharpening broader concerns about executive overreach and the erosion of institutional autonomy. The challenge now is to convert this heightened public scrutiny into a sustained political check on right-wing dominance. The central question is whether this wave of public dissent over the electoral process can connect with wider popular resentments over the education system, unemployment and rising prices, and translate them into political change. Mantar周边暂停移动互联网服务，多座地铁站关闭入口，警方在附近拘留了700多名抗议者。CJP号召于10月10日在Jantar Mantar举行“Jantar Mantar 2.0”抗议，却遭到更严厉的镇压。警方和准军事部队大规模部署，几乎令首都陷入停顿，实际上阻止了集会举行。两天后，数千人在德里市中心参加史无前例的“Dilli Chalo”游行，由反对党领袖（人民院）拉胡尔·甘地、国大党以及INDIA联盟重要领导人率领。另请观看“对选举失去信心”：Jantar Mantar大规模10月2日抗议的震中。这一对比颇具意味。“Dilli Chalo”游行展现了国大党动员大批人群上街的能力，而CJP的号召则使青年不满更鲜明地进入公众视野。对甘地先生而言，这提供了整合各种诉求并将其引向更聚焦政治议程的机会。Jantar Mantar起义在政党之外创造了新的政治空间。其最重要的贡献是打破了恐惧氛围。大规模抗议证明，既有反对党，尤其是国大党，能够将对选举诚信、机构问责和抗议权利的关注整合起来，对政府形成更广泛的政治挑战。社会运动可以动员民众、表达异议，而政党则提供维持运动并将其转化为政治行动的组织手段。两者单独都不足以实现目标。最终，政治变革能否实现，取决于政党能否将大规模动员转化为对执政者持续而有力的挑战。这场公众情绪高涨的核心，是围绕投票神圣性展开的日益扩大的斗争，而投票权正是民主的基石。截至2026年9月初，这项工作已导致30个邦和联邦属地的选民名册草案中删除了13.37 crore个名字，相当于SIR修订前选民的14.1%，引发了合格选民可能遭不当剥夺选举权的担忧。核心问题在于，这项修订是否透明、可核查，并设置了充分保障，防止任意排除选民，尤其是在用于删除姓名的程序及集中式软件可靠性受到质疑的情况下。此次抗议还伴随着向印度最高法院提交的请愿书，要求展开调查、审计删除选民记录的情况、设置防止任意排除的保障措施并暂停修订进程，凸显了大规模参与、反对党动员与法律行动相互汇合所形成的政治力量。请愿书也给司法系统带来考验，要求其通过司法审查保护宪法权利，而非让行政决定逃避监督。自《首席选举专员及其他选举专员（任命、服务条件及任期）法》2023年颁布后，选举委员会（ECI）的独立性已受到质疑。该法将印度首席大法官排除在任命选举专员的委员会之外，并规定选举专员履行公务时享有免受民事和刑事诉讼追究的豁免权。有关各选举专员就CEC单方面决定存在分歧的报道，又进一步引发了对ECI运作方式的质疑。这些疑虑加剧了反对SIR的声音，为挑战政府增添了新的维度，将选举管理与民主问责联系起来。数千人走上街头，抗议重做选民名单，并质疑ECI是否履行了公正履职的宪法义务。抗议自10月初以来不断增强，标志着反对党政治发生重大转变。要求取消SIR并让CEC辞职一度被认为难以想象，如今已成为抗议活动的凝聚点。这场斗争也把围绕选举公平的较量从议会和法院等机构场所推向街头。如果合格公民在没有充分保障或有效救济的情况下被排除在选民名册之外，那么仅靠选举活动的举行，无法保证民主的合法性。这些担忧令electoral民主转向选举专制的幽灵再次浮现，凸显该国民主倒退的严重程度。当前的政治时刻暴露出印度人民党（BJP）主导地位之下的脆弱之处，不断增长的公众不满开始考验其执政根基。BJP在2024年大选中未能取得议会多数，已经削弱了其不可战胜的光环。与此同时，政府通过多种机制重塑选举架构的努力，加剧了人们的担忧：政府试图将永久多数制度化，并阻止其选举失利再次发生。政府无法提供政治解决方案，转而动用强制权力压制异议，尤其是针对青年群体。然而，这些措施无法掩盖更深层的问题，即宪法保障的投票权正在遭到侵蚀。政府也不能通过指责反对党、CJP或左翼团体煽动混乱或密谋推翻政权来回避监督。此类关于颠覆政权的指控——其含义不过是通过选举实现政权更替——尤其缺乏说服力，因为BJP自身也有追查并推动那些政策、纲领和做法遭其反对的政府更迭的记录。政府采取镇压手段，暴露了其政治影响力的局限，加深了青年与执政党之间的隔阂，也侵蚀了公众对其掌控的机构的信任。简言之，它正在失去对局势的掌控。更大的民主利益攸关之处十分明确：这归根结底是一场围绕民主根基——投票权——的斗争。尽管这些 developments 尚未促成新的政治阵营组合，却拓宽了表达异议的空间，并加剧了对行政权力集中的审视。最引人注目的是，ECI如今被视为行政部门的代理机构，对其公正性的怀疑加剧了人们对行政越权和机构自主性遭侵蚀的广泛担忧。当前的挑战，是将这种不断增强的公众监督转化为对右翼主导地位的持续政治制衡。核心问题在于，这股针对选举进程的公众不满浪潮，能否与民众对教育体系、失业和物价上涨的更广泛不满相连接，并将其转化为政治变革。对此仍有待观察。评论须以英语撰写，并使用完整句子。评论不得含有辱骂性内容或针对个人的攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果您已经注册The https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/u.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription In its second term, the Donald Trump administration has been active in restricting legal immigration to the United States. The administration’s attempt to impose a $100,000 payment requirement on certain new H-1B petitions, changes to visa renewal procedures, the introduction of a wage-weighted selection system, and the latest suspensions of the Program Electronic Review Management (PERM) process are cases in point, disproportionately impacting Indian immigrants and firms. It is tempting to read these developments as a product of the Trump administration alone, but they reflect deeper political interests that are likely to survive post-Trump. Indian nationals account for 70% of H-1B visa approvals, with one-fifth of the visas going to employees of Indian-origin companies. This means that, as the bipartisan focus on immigration reform continues, the issue is likely to sustain as a friction point in India-U.S. relations. Democrats are expected to dominate the upcoming midterm elections in November. They view immigration through a rights-based lens, and their voters remain supportive of both legal immigration and increased legalisation of undocumented immigrants. Some 75% of Democrats see skilled immigration as good for the U.S., compared with 54% of Republicans. Even under the current administration, Democrats have pushed for easing F-1 student visa requirements and have traditionally enjoyed the support of diaspora communities in the U.S., including the Indian diaspora. Immigrants seeking U.S. citizenship targeted in Trump administration's illegal voting crackdown U.S. proposes new rule to scrap 60-day grace period for H-1B workers after job loss However, prominent Democratic Senators such as Dick Durbin and Richard Blumenthal, as well as progressive Independents such as Bernie Sanders, have also pushed for bills seeking H-1B reforms. Democrats view alleged fraud in the H-1B visa system as a serious challenge that needs to be addressed. Similarly, the labour wing of the Democratic Party views the H-1B visa programme as a potential threat to domestic labour protections and workers’ rights. The Democrats’ immigrant voter base, their open opposition to the H-1B visa fee hikes, and resistance to these restrictions from businesses and unions suggest that a Democratic-controlled Congress may soften the harshest executive measures and tone down the rhetoric. However, concerns about visa fraud and worker protections mean that Democrats are likely to keep up the pressure on the outsourcing model and continue pushing for H-1B reforms. While a plurality of Republicans support restrictions on legal immigration, this number has declined considerably since 2025. Among the Republican leadership, there is a visible split between anti-immigration nationalists and pro-immigration business interests. The Trump administration’s hikes in the H-1B visa fee is an example of this conflict. While the administration was openly critical of the programme and aggressively pushed for the fee increase, it subsequently diluted the measure by including exemptions for graduates of U.S. universities and existing visa holders, following pressure from businesses and universities. The debate over wage-weighted entries versus the lottery system for H-1B visas has dominated discussions on immigration within the U.S. business community. There are three broad categories in this debate. The first is the random lottery system that was in place until 2026, which benefited outsourcing firms and start-ups. The second is the wage-weighted lottery system (February 2026), which infers wage levels based on experience, job role and location, dividing visa quotas into four categories. On the surface, this system might benefit big-tech firms, but it could also benefit outsourcing firms that hire highly experienced workers for lower wages. The third is the actual wage weighted lottery model, which is supported by U.S.-based industries. This approach could dilute the advantages enjoyed by outsourcing firms while benefiting American hires and also F1 student hires. If India plays its cards right, suspension of PERM may be an opportunity: Priyank Kharge Trump’s move to suspend PERM programme for Indian IT majors raises talent-retention concerns MEA says U.S. green card suspension measures do not advance shared India-U.S. ambitions For the artificial intelligence (AI) and big-tech business community, this reform could be beneficial in two ways. First, AI graduate programmes and advanced research roles in the U.S. rely heavily on international talent, with demand for AI skills growing faster than the supply of domestic graduates. The reform could therefore help AI firms secure top international talent for higher wages. Second, the AI sector is expanding into market segments traditionally occupied by start-ups and outsourcing companies, which often perform low technology maintenance and communication roles. The AI sector could therefore benefit if these start-ups and outsourcing firms were compelled to hire fewer workers. With the AI sector playing a prominent role in campaign contributions for the 2026 midterm elections, these policies to counter outsourcing firms are likely to continue. With over 54% of India’s software services exports going to the U.S., which remains the top market for Indian information technology (IT) outsourcing, this represents a major challenge for India. However, these developments could also be viewed as positive news for Indian students at U.S. universities. The U.S. Department of Labor’s suspension of eight firms, including not only Indian outsourcing companies such as Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro but also major technology firms such as Microsoft and Adobe, from green card sponsorship reinforces this trend. It raises the cost of hiring foreign workers for businesses as a whole, creating pressure that remains largely beyond partisan control. With Mr. Trump’s political power potentially diminished after November, anti-immigration rhetoric could decline. However, with both parties committed to immigration reform, India should continue to expect an unfavourable and unpredictable immigration landscape. 特朗普政府进入第二个任期以来，积极限制合法移民赴美国。该政府试图对某些新的H-1B申请施加10万美元缴费要求、改变签证续签程序、推出工资加权筛选系统，以及最近暂停项目电子审查管理（PERM）流程，这些都是其典型做法，对印度移民和企业造成了不成比例的影响。人们很容易将这些 developments 解读为特朗普政府单独推出的产物，但它们实际上反映了更深层次的政治利益，而这种利益很可能在特朗普卸任后继续存在。

印度公民占H-1B签证批准人数的70%，其中五分之一的签证发放给了印度裔公司的员工。这意味着，随着两党继续关注移民改革，该问题很可能持续成为印美关系中的摩擦点。预计民主党将在11月即将举行的中期选举中占据优势。他们从权利视角看待移民，其选民仍然支持合法移民以及增加无证移民合法化。约75%的民主党人士认为技术移民有利于美国，而共和党人士的这一比例为54%。即便在现任政府执政期间，民主党也一直主张放宽F-1学生签证要求，并且历来得到美国侨民社群的支持，其中包括印度侨民。

特朗普政府打击非法投票行动所针对的、寻求美国公民身份的移民

美国提议制定新规，取消H-1B工人在失业后的60天宽限期

不过，Dick Durbin和Richard Blumenthal等资深民主党参议员，以及Bernie Sanders等进步派独立人士，也一直在推动旨在改革H-1B的法案。民主党认为，有关H-1B签证系统存在欺诈的指控是一项必须解决的严重挑战。同样，民主党内的劳工派将H-1B签证项目视为对国内劳工保护和工人权利的潜在威胁。

民主党所拥有的移民选民基础、他们对提高H-1B签证费率的公开反对，以及企业和工会对这些限制的抵制，都表明由民主党控制的国会可能会软化最严厉的行政措施，并降低相关言论的强硬程度。

不过，对签证欺诈和劳工保护的担忧意味着，民主党很可能继续向外包模式施压，并继续推动H-1B改革。

虽然多数共和党人士支持限制合法移民，但这一比例自2025年以来已大幅下降。在共和党领导层中，反移民民族主义者与支持移民的商业利益之间出现了明显分化。特朗普政府提高H-1B签证费就是这种冲突的一个例子。该政府公开批评这一项目，并积极推动提高费用，但在企业和大学施加压力后，随后通过为美国大学毕业生和现有签证持有者设置豁免，削弱了该措施的影响。

围绕H-1B签证采用工资加权录取还是抽签制度展开的争论，一直主导着美国商业界的移民讨论。这场争论大致分为三类。第一类是截至2026年一直采用的随机抽签制度，它有利于外包企业和初创公司。第二类是工资加权抽签制度（2026年2月推出），该制度根据工作经验、职位和所在地推定工资水平，将签证配额划分为四个类别。表面上，这套制度可能有利于大型科技公司，但也可能让那些以较低工资聘用经验丰富的员工的外包企业受益。第三类是真正的工资加权抽签模式，得到美国本土行业的支持。这一做法可能削弱外包企业的优势，同时让美国本土招聘和F1学生招聘受益。

如果印度审慎应对，暂停PERM可能是一个机会：Priyank Kharge

特朗普暂停面向印度IT专业人士的PERM项目，引发人才留任担忧

印度外交部表示，美国暂停绿卡措施无助于推进印美共同目标

对于人工智能（AI）和大型科技商业群体而言，这项改革可能带来两方面好处。第一，美国的人工智能研究生项目和高水平研究岗位高度依赖国际人才，而对人工智能技能的需求增长快于本土毕业生供给。因此，这项改革可能帮助人工智能企业以更高薪酬留住顶尖国际人才。第二，人工智能行业正在向传统上由初创公司和外包企业占据的市场领域扩张，而这些企业通常承担低技术维护和沟通工作。因此，如果这些初创公司和外包企业被迫减少招聘，人工智能行业可能从中受益。

鉴于人工智能行业在2026年中期选举的竞选捐款中占据重要地位，这些制衡外包企业的政策很可能会延续下去。印度超过54%的软件服务出口流向美国，而美国仍是印度信息技术（IT）外包的首大市场，因此上述趋势对印度构成重大挑战。

不过，这些 developments 也可以被视为印度学生在美国大学就读的利好消息。美国劳工部暂停八家企业为外籍员工提供绿卡担保，其中包括Infosys、Tata Consultancy Services和Wipro等印度外包企业，也包括Microsoft和Adobe等大型科技企业，这进一步强化了这一趋势。它提高了整个企业群体聘用外国劳工的成本，从而形成一种基本不受党派控制的压力。

如果特朗普先生的政治权力在11月之后可能减弱，反移民言论或许会减少。然而，由于两党都致力于移民改革，印度应继续预期移民环境将处于不利且难以预测的状态。

Unlock these with Subscription Sixteen years after his visit as Poland’s Prime Minister, Donald Tusk’s travel to Delhi and Bengaluru last week was to signal a renewed desire to work closely with India. Mr. Tusk’s visit, two months ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s trip to Brussels to sign the India-European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement , indicated one part of his agenda. Both sides agreed that it was time to develop trade, currently worth just $6 billion, to double its size by 2030. Mr. Tusk’s last visit to India was in 2017, as President of the European Council for the EU-India summit, and it is fitting that his trip was just as the FTA is finalised and ratified after years of delays. Another area of increased India-Poland collaboration is in technology, AI and defence hardware, critical minerals, renewable and nuclear energy given Poland’s expertise in the last few decades and India’s capacity for scale. As the EU’s sixth largest economy, Poland has officially crossed the $1 trillion GDP (nominal terms) milestone. Its $120-billion-dollar tech economy is also gaining global interest. A large part of Polish machinery and parts is exported to Germany, which in turn has a growing share of Indian imports, and India could consider more trilateral collaborations for manufacturing and mining technology. The two sides agreed to establish a “Defence Industry Dialogue” and explore a dialogue on counter-terrorism cooperation. Finally, the Modi-Tusk talks focused on geopolitics, particularly the ongoing war in Ukraine. The war’s impact, especially on the Global South, has been a concern for India, and the Modi government’s initiative to work on an agreement acceptable to Kyiv and Moscow on grain exports and seafarers’ safety was discussed. The four-pronged plan, announced by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar during his September visit to Warsaw, won Mr. Tusk’s support. At the India-Poland Business Forum in Bengaluru, Mr. Tusk, who was accompanied by a Polish business delegation, said the challenge now was in “translating” the talks and MoUs signed into actual joint ventures between businesses. Apart from the distance and geographies, there is the matter of trust, given India’s defence engagement with Russia and Poland’s defence ties with Pakistan. Poland is credited with training Pakistan’s Air Force in its early years; a mutual defence cooperation agreement was signed in 2018. India has a unique and enduring partnership with Russia, and New Delhi is unlikely to accept Warsaw’s strictures over its military engagement and exercises with Russia that caused a controversy earlier this year during the Polish Foreign Minister’s visit. It is essential for Delhi and Warsaw to complete the confidentiality of classified information that is still being negotiated and draw up the parameters of future cooperation based on realities. Mr. Tusk’s statement that India and Poland today have no “conflicts of interest” is a significant aspiration, for two countries that share old values, and new avenues of partnership. 唐纳德·图斯克担任波兰总理16年后，他上周访问新德里和班加罗尔，旨在表明与印度加强合作的愿望。图斯克先生此次访问是在印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪赴布鲁塞尔签署印度—欧洲联盟（EU）自由贸易协定前两个月进行的，这显示了其议程的一部分。双方一致认为，应推动目前价值仅60亿美元的双边贸易发展，到2030年将其规模翻一番。图斯克先生上次访问印度是在2017年，当时他以欧洲理事会主席身份出席欧盟—印度峰会。如今，在自由贸易协定历经多年延迟后即将敲定并获批准之际出访印度，恰当不过。

印度与波兰加强合作的另一个领域涉及技术、人工智能和国防装备、关键矿产、可再生能源及核能。鉴于波兰在过去几十年积累的相关专长以及印度具备规模化能力，这些领域具有重要意义。作为欧盟第六大经济体，波兰已正式跨越1万亿美元国内生产总值（按名义价值计算）里程碑。其价值1200亿美元的科技经济也正日益受到全球关注。波兰大量机械及零部件出口至德国，而德国在印度进口中的占比不断上升。印度可考虑在制造和采矿技术方面扩大三方合作。双方同意建立“国防工业对话”，并探讨就反恐合作启动对话。

最后，莫迪与图斯克的会谈聚焦于地缘政治，尤其是乌克兰持续战争。这场战争的影响，尤其是对全球南方的影响，一直是印度关切的问题。双方还讨论了莫迪政府提出的倡议，即着手制定一项能够为基辅和莫斯科双方接受的协议，以处理粮食出口和海员安全问题。外交部长S. 贾伊尚卡尔9月访问华沙期间宣布了四点计划，图斯克先生对此表示支持。

在班加罗尔举行的印度—波兰商业论坛上，图斯克先生表示当前的挑战在于将会谈和已签署的合作备忘录“转化”为企业之间的实际合资项目。波兰商业代表团陪同图斯克先生出席论坛。除距离和地理因素外，信任问题同样值得关注，因为印度与俄罗斯有防务合作，而波兰与巴基斯坦保持防务关系。波兰曾帮助培训巴基斯坦空军早年力量，双方于2018年签署了共同防务合作协议。印度与俄罗斯拥有独特而持久的关系。新德里不太可能接受华沙对其与俄罗斯开展军事接触和军演的批评。今年早些时候波兰外长访问期间，这些接触和军演曾引发争议。德黑兰和华沙必须完成仍在谈判中的涉密信息保密安排，并依据实际情况制定未来合作的参数。

图斯克先生表示，如今印度与波兰之间不存在“利益冲突”，这一愿望意义重大，因为这两个国家拥有共同的历史价值观，也正在开辟新的合作途径。

Unlock these with Subscription A 48-year-old man with uncontrolled diabetes developed persistent swelling in his left lower limb, followed by high fever and breathlessness. An ankle-joint sample was initially misidentified as Acinetobacter baumannii complex, while findings in his lungs raised suspicion of tuberculosis. Cultures from his blood and joint pus eventually identified Burkholderia pseudomallei -- the bacterium that causes melioidosis. His blood cultures cleared around the 21st day of treatment, and he recovered, according to a case report described by Atish Mohapatra, Assistant Professor, Department of Microbiology, Kalinga Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar. In another report published in 2026, Dr.Mohapatra and colleagues described a 25-year-old patient living with sickle cell disease and type 1 diabetes who developed disseminated melioidosis involving the bones and lungs, with a splenic abscess and pulmonary embolism. Neha Rastogi Panda, senior consultant, Infectious Diseases, Fortis Hospital, described a case involving a 54-year-old man living with diabetes and chronic liver disease. He had low-grade fever for about six weeks, followed by high fever over 15 days, and a persistent cough for three weeks. He also had swelling and pus discharge from his left foot. A CT scan showed extensive consolidation in the right lower lobe of his lung. Blood cultures and samples collected during bronchoscopy grew B. pseudomallei , confirming pulmonary melioidosis with bloodstream infection. A study published in The Lancet Global Health , led by Nitin Gupta, Department of Infectious Diseases, Kasturba Medical College, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, assessed high-risk hospitalised adults at 15 Indian tertiary-care centres between January 2023 and December 2025. Culture-confirmed melioidosis was found in 262 of 2,953 patients (8.9%). Of those diagnosed, 50 (19.1%) died in hospital. B. pseudomallei is found in soil and water in tropical and subtropical regions. Infection usually occurs when contaminated soil or water enters the body through cuts or wounds. Inhalation of contaminated dust or water droplets and, less commonly, ingestion of contaminated water can also transmit the bacterium. Human-to-human transmission is exceptionally rare. Melioidosis can cause pneumonia, bloodstream infection, skin and soft-tissue infections, abscesses in organs such as the liver and spleen, septic arthritis and bone infections. It can also affect the kidneys, muscles and prostate. Rarely, infection involves the nervous system. Severe disease can progress to septic shock and multiorgan dysfunction. Symptoms vary according to the organs affected. Patients may have persistent fever, cough, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, painful joint swelling, abdominal pain or localised skin infections. Some develop a slowly progressive illness resembling tuberculosis, while others deteriorate rapidly. The infection can also relapse if treatment is inadequate. Diabetes is a major risk factor. Chronic kidney, lung and liver diseases, heavy alcohol use and reduced immunity can also increase vulnerability. Dr. Mohapatra says clinicians usually consider melioidosis in high-risk patients with unexplained sepsis, severe pneumonia, deep-seated abscesses or bone and joint infections, particularly when environmental exposure is plausible. When it comes to diagnosis there are challenges at both the clinical and laboratory levels. Symptoms are often nonspecific, the disease can present in different ways and the incubation period can vary. Clinicians may not suspect melioidosis or send appropriate samples for culture, while microbiologists may struggle to identify the organism correctly. Automated identification systems can help, but they are not infallible. Like in the above case, the bacterium was initially misidentified as A. baumannii complex. Dr.Mohapatra notes that even systems such as VITEK 2 can misidentify B. pseudomallei . MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry can aid identification, but its cost and limited availability can be barriers. Validated molecular tests, including PCR, can support confirmation where accessible. Culture of blood, pus, abscess aspirates, respiratory specimens or affected tissue remains central to diagnosis. Depending on the presentation, urine and other clinical samples may also be tested. Multiple specimens may be necessary because infection can involve several organs, and prior antibiotic use can make confirmation difficult. Imaging with ultrasound, CT or MRI can help locate deep-seated abscesses and identify organ involvement. Madhumitha R., senior consultant, Infectious Diseases and Infection Control at MGM Healthcare, Chennai, says clinicians should consider blood cultures in patients with persistent fever, ideally before antibiotics when clinically appropriate. If melioidosis is suspected, the laboratory should be informed so that appropriate identification procedures can be followed. A history of contact with contaminated soil or water can also help guide testing. Experts call for better communication between clinicians and microbiologists, training for laboratory personnel to recognise suspicious organisms, and referral pathways to facilities that can confirm difficult isolates. Standardised laboratory procedures and quality assurance are important, particularly where advanced identification methods are unavailable. India’s National Centre for Disease Control provides technical guidance for melioidosis treatment in its 2025 manual on zoonotic diseases of public health importance. Treatment has two phases: an initial intensive phase with intravenous antibiotics, followed by prolonged oral eradication therapy to reduce the risk of relapse. Ceftazidime is an established option for the intensive phase, while meropenem is preferred in severe illness, including septic shock and neurological involvement. Intravenous treatment may last two to eight weeks or longer, depending on severity and the organs affected. Bone and joint infections, neurological disease and deep-seated abscesses may require prolonged treatment. The oral eradication phase commonly uses trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for several months, with longer courses sometimes required for complicated infections. Dr.Panda stresses that treatment must be individualised according to organ involvement, drug susceptibility, kidney and liver function, tolerability and clinical response. Drainage of accessible abscesses, control of underlying conditions such as diabetes, monitoring for adverse effects and follow-up after discharge are also important. Incomplete treatment can lead to relapse even after symptoms improve. There is currently no licensed vaccine. The multicentre study found variation across participating centres, with the highest proportions in Odisha (26%), Madhya Pradesh (22.7%) and Karnataka (19.3%) – figures describe the selected hospital populations, not State-wide prevalence. The study also found associations with monsoon admission, outdoor high-risk occupations and groundwater as the main drinking-water source. These associations do not establish causation. Earlier reviews have found confirmed cases in several Indian States, but differences in diagnosis, awareness and reporting may affect how many cases are recorded. Dr. Mohapatra says India should move beyond identifying melioidosis only when an unusual case appears. Experts recommend a phased surveillance system, beginning with hospitals and laboratories equipped to confirm infection and expanding as diagnostic capacity improves. Such a system could track confirmed cases, geographical and environmental exposures, antimicrobial susceptibility, treatment regimens, deaths, complications and relapse. Better surveillance, alongside improved diagnostic access and clinical awareness, would help establish the disease burden and guide public-health responses. Prevention is important especially for people who often come into contact with soil or water. Farmers and others at higher risk should use protective footwear, cover cuts and abrasions, and clean contaminated wounds promptly. Avoiding untreated surface water and informing a doctor about possible environmental exposure may also help reduce risk and guide timely testing. Improving clinical awareness, access to reliable diagnostic testing and systematic surveillance will be essential to identifying more cases of melioidosis in India and reducing deaths from this potentially life-threatening infection. Unlock these with Subscription The Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR) on Sunday sought an inquiry report within two weeks from the Directorate of Education over the death of a 17-year-old Class 12 student who was found with severe burns at a government school in east Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday. The girl was found behind the school’s guard room after school authorities heard cries from the area. She was taken to Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan, where she was declared dead on arrival. According to police, a water bottle used to carry petrol was recovered from the spot. Taking cognisance of media reports, the commission raised concerns about student safety, questioning how the girl managed to bring an inflammable substance into the school without being noticed. “The content of the news report, if true, are disturbing and raise serious concern on the safety of children inside the school premises. The incident as a whole has resulted in violation of child rights on account of negligence of public servants,” the commission stated in its notice. The commission issued notices to the Directorate of Education, the school principal and the police, seeking action-taken reports within two weeks. DCPCR member Kundan Kanskar said the commission would take action after receiving the reports. “Such incidents hint at a lack of accessible, quality mental health services for students in schools,” he said. Police have seized the school’s CCTV digital video recorder and are examining the footage to reconstruct the sequence of events. They are questioning the security guard, teachers and family members to ascertain how the incident went unnoticed. The school’s attendance register has also been examined. Officers on Saturday said a three-page purported suicide note recovered from the student’s bag referred to “relationship issues and parental disappointment”. Sources said one page contained an apology to her family, while another requested that a friend not be harassed. “We are investigating the matter. The circumstances leading to the incident are being examined,” a senior police officer said. Police said they are also examining the family’s allegation that the girl could have been the victim of a conspiracy. Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 德里儿童权利保护委员会（DCPCR）周日向教育局提出要求，要求其在两周内就一名17岁的高中二年级学生之死提交调查报告。该学生于周六在德里东部克里希纳纳加尔的一所政府学校被发现全身严重烧伤。学校方面听到附近传来呼救声后，在学校门卫室后方发现了这名女孩。她被送往 Hedgewar 医院，并在抵达时被宣布死亡。据警方称，现场发现一个曾用于携带汽油的水瓶。委员会在关注媒体报道后，对学生安全表示担忧，质疑女孩是如何在无人察觉的情况下将易燃物品带进学校的。委员会在通知中表示：“如果新闻报道内容属实，令人不安，并引发了对校园内儿童安全的严重关切。整起事件因公职人员失职而造成了对儿童权利的侵犯。”委员会向教育局、学校校长和警方发出通知，要求在两周内提交已采取措施的报告。DCPCR 成员 Kundan Kanskar 表示，委员会将在收到报告后采取行动。他说：“此类事件表明，学校可能缺乏学生能够获得的高质量心理健康服务。”

警方已扣押学校的监控数字录像机，并正在查看录像，以还原事件发生的经过。警方正在询问保安、教师和家属，以查清这起事件为何未被发现。学校的考勤登记簿也已接受检查。警方人员周六表示，从该学生书包中起获的一份据称为遗书的三页文件提到了“感情问题和父母失望”。消息人士称，其中一页内容是向家人道歉，另一页则请求不要骚扰她的一名朋友。一名高级警官说：“我们正在调查此事，目前正在审查导致该事件发生的各种情况。”警方表示，他们也在核查家属提出的指控，即该女孩可能是阴谋的受害者。

The collapse occurred in Milan Garden as an additional floor was being built on an old, single-storey house on a 200-square-yard plot, said an officer. No casualties had been reported till the time the report went to the press. “Their family members suspect that they are trapped as their mobile phones are not reachable,” the officer said. https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori.summary: Unlock these with Subscription As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori.summary_zh: 订阅后解锁这些内容 印度从一个季风降雨不足的年份中恢复之际，对于所谓“另一个季风”，即“东北季风”的前景，人们既怀希望又感忧虑。印度气象局（IMD）表示，今年10月至12月的东北季风降雨量可能处于“正常”水平，即与50年平均值一致，并处于12%的误差范围内。
https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . While contributing only around a quarter of India’s annual rainfall, it is largely focused on the south-east peninsula regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Keralam. The southwest monsoon, influenced by a strengthening El Niño , has already left its desiccating mark. Rainfall from June-September was 759.4 mm against 868.6 mm, a 12.6% deficit, the driest in 11 years. This has impacted kharif sowing and is reflected in food inflation. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that this year, the northeast monsoon rainfall, spanning October to December, would likely be ‘normal’ , meaning in line with a 50-year average and within a 12% error window. Most parts of the country, it said, are expected to receive below-normal rainfall, except some areas of northwest India and southern parts of peninsular India, where rainfall is likely to be normal to above-normal. The wide error window, however, is far less precise than its forecasts for the southwest monsoon with its margin of 5%, and can sometimes make the northeast monsoon the bearer of nasty surprises. For instance, December 1, 2015, saw the city of Chennai deluged by its heaviest rainfall in 24-hours in over a century ; at least 500 lives were lost and 18 lakh people displaced in the State. That year and the present are linked by a common thread: a powerful El Niño. Associated with the heating up of the Central Pacific, the El Niño is linked to the drying up of the southwest monsoon rains but also yoked — not always — with a vigorous northeast monsoon. Other than in 2015, several El Niño years, such as 1997 and 2009, have been associated with above-normal rainfall between October and December in Tamil Nadu though El Niño years, such as 2002 and 1982, saw a poor northeast monsoon (and a predictably bad southwest monsoon). While the climate mechanisms linking a vigorous northeast monsoon and El Niño are still to be fully understood, it appears the warming patterns of the El Niño tend to deflect rain-bearing cyclonic circulations in unpredictable ways. Therefore, the Centre and the southern States ought to take enough precautions: from clearing up stormwater drains, fortifying shelters, making provisions for infrastructure damage and tightening weather warning forecasts to prepare for torrents. https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori.title_zh: 东北季风带来意外之变
https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori.body_zh: 订阅可享受更多权益，包括独家报道、社论、观点等。订阅即可解锁这些内容。随着印度从季风降雨不足的一年逐渐恢复，对于“另一个季风”，即“东北季风”的前景，既有人乐观，也有人担忧。东北季风贡献了印度年降雨量的约四分之一，但主要集中在泰米尔纳德邦、本地治里、安得拉邦沿海、拉亚拉西马、卡纳塔克邦南部内陆和喀拉拉邦等东南半岛地区。受不断增强的厄尔尼诺现象影响，西南季风已经留下干旱的印记。6月至9月的降雨量为759.4毫米，而同期为868.6毫米，降雨量缺口达到12.6%，是11年来最干旱的一次。这影响了卡里夫作物的播种，也反映在食品通胀之中。印度气象局（IMD）表示，今年10月至12月的东北季风降雨量可能处于“正常”水平，即与50年平均值一致，并处于12%的误差范围内。该局称，除印度西北部部分地区和印度半岛南部部分地区外，全国大部分地区预计将获得低于正常水平的降雨；这些地区的降雨量则可能正常或高于正常水平。然而，这一较宽的误差范围远不如西南季风预测精确，后者采用的误差幅度为5%，因此东北季风有时可能带来令人不愉快的意外。例如，2015年12月1日，金奈市遭遇了一个多世纪以来24小时内最猛烈的降雨，至少500人死亡，该邦180万人流离失所。那一年与今年有一个共同点：强大的厄尔尼诺现象。厄尔尼诺与中太平洋海域升温有关，它不仅与西南季风降雨减少有关，也与强劲的东北季风存在联系，尽管这种联系并非始终存在。除2015年外，1997年和2009年等多个厄尔尼诺年份，泰米尔纳德邦10月至12月的降雨量都高于正常水平；而2002年和1982年等厄尔尼诺年份则遭遇了较差的东北季风，以及可以预见的糟糕西南季风。尽管将强劲东北季风与厄尔尼诺现象联系起来的气候机制仍未被完全理解，但厄尔尼诺现象的增温模式似乎会以不可预测的方式改变携雨气旋的路径。因此，中央政府和南部各邦应采取充分预防措施，包括清理雨水排水渠、加固避难所、为基础设施受损做好准备，以及加强天气预报预警，以应对暴雨洪灾。评论必须使用英语，并以完整句子表达。评论不得包含辱骂或人身攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你是《The Hindu》的注册用户且已登录，可以继续参与我们的文章讨论。如果你还没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录自己的账户后，可以在Vuukle上查看过去的评论。

The Bengaluru police have cracked the case of the recent blast at an under-construction building on Jeremiah Road, injuring two, and arrested a 27-year-old bakery salesman, who allegedly conspired with two childhood friends to murder his uncle by assembling an improvised explosive device (IED) concealed inside a parcel. According to the police, the prime accused held a grudge against his uncle, Allauddin M., over property and financial disputes, as well as a personal issue involving the breakdown of his sister’s marriage. The incident occurred on October 20 when workers were at the building. A loud explosion was heard on the fifth floor, and an investigation revealed that an IED concealed inside a torch had exploded. The IED was assembled in Raichur by one of the conspirators, who learned from YouTube. Material obtained from firecrackers was used as the explosive material in the IED, rigged inside a battery using an electrical circuit and pellets. Investigators said the accused had prepared a parcel containing the device and left it at a petty shop near the building where Allauddin was working. The accused allegedly contacted him over the phone and pressured him to open the parcel. Allauddin, who was having lunch, asked his colleague to open it and the device exploded when the parcel was opened. Allauddin and his colleague, Suraj Kumar, a security guard from Uttar Pradesh, sustained severe injuries. The case had led to speculations of terrorism owing to the involvement of an IED, even as sleuths from the National Investigation Agency (NIA) also joined the probe. https://leadership.ng/2027-yiaga-africa-.summary: Itodo observed that the 2026 figures show that the voter register has increased to 103,428,715 registered voters, representing an increase of 9,959,707 voters, representing 10.66% compared with 11.27% increase recorded in 2023. While the overall voter register figure for 2026 increased by 10.66%, the number of registered voters aged 18–34 declined by 7,282,821, representing a 19.65% reduction in this age category.
https://leadership.ng/2027-yiaga-africa-.summary_zh: 伊托多表示，2026年的数据显示，选民登记册已增至103,428,715名登记选民，新增9,959,707名选民，增幅为10.66%，低于2023年录得的11.27%。虽然2026年选民登记册总数增长了10.66%，但18至34岁登记选民人数减少了7,282,821人，降幅达19.65%。
https://leadership.ng/2027-yiaga-africa-.body: “According to INEC, Nigeria had 93,469,008 registered voters in 2023, distributed across four age categories: Youth: 18–34 years: 37,060,399 (39.6%); •Middle age: 35–49 years: 33,413,591 (35.8%); Elderly: 50–69 years: 17,700,270 (18.9%), 70 years and above: 5,294,748 (5.7%),” he stated. Itodo observed that the 2026 figures show that the voter register has increased to 103,428,715 registered voters, representing an increase of 9,959,707 voters, representing 10.66% compared with 11.27% increase recorded in 2023. “The 2026 age distribution is as follows: Youth: 18–34 years: 29,777,578 (28.79%); Middle age: 35–49 years: 43,265,946 (41.83%); Elderly: 50–69 years: 22,982,900 (22.22%); 70 years and above: 7,402,291 (7.16%). “What do these figures tell us? While the overall voter register figure for 2026 increased by 10.66%, the number of registered voters aged 18–34 declined by 7,282,821, representing a 19.65% reduction in this age category. Their share of the register also declined from 39.6% in 2023 to 28.79% in 2026, a decrease of approximately 10.9 percentage points. “The number of registered voters aged 35–49 increased by 9,852,355, representing an increase of approximately 29.5%. Does this mean young people were removed from the register? Not necessarily,” he noted. Itodo said between 2023 and 2026, three years elapsed, hence voters who were aged 32, 33, and 34 in 2023 would have transitioned into the 35–49 age category by 2026. “This demographic shift could partially explain the decline in the youth category and the increase in the older age category. However, ageing alone does not fully account for these changes. “It is also necessary to examine new additions to the register, particularly the rate of youth registration, and any administrative adjustments. “This raises a critical question: Are young Nigerians registering to vote at a rate sufficient to replace those who are ageing out of the youth category? “For historical perspective, Nigeria’s voter register increased from 68,833,476 in 2015 to 84,004,084 in 2019, representing a 22.04% increase. Between 2019 and 2023, the register grew to 93,469,008, an increase of 9,464,924 voters (11.27%). By 2026, it had risen further to 103,428,715, representing an additional 9,959,707 voters (10.66%). “Although the absolute increase between 2023 and 2026 was slightly higher than that recorded between 2019 and 2023, the percentage growth was marginally lower. These figures demonstrate a declining rate of growth in Nigeria’s voter register: 22.04% in 2015–2019, 11.27% in 2019–2023, and 10.66% in 2023–2026. The most recent period, however, covers three years rather than four. “The critical issue, therefore, is not simply whether the voter register is growing, but who is entering the register, how voters are transitioning between age categories, and what these demographic changes mean,” he added. Itodo called on INEC to publish a detailed age-cohort analysis explaining changes between the 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2026 registers, including new registrations, age transitions, removal of dead and unqualified persons on the register and other adjustments. He said: “if the decline shows inadequate registration among newly eligible young voters, it must prompt increased investment in youth mobilization for voter registration. If it reflects administrative adjustments, those changes must be clearly documented and explained.” We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/2027-yiaga-africa-.body_zh: 据独立国家选举委员会（INEC）表示，尼日利亚2023年共有93,469,008名登记选民，分为四个年龄类别：青年：18–34岁：37,060,399人（39.6%）；•中年：35–49岁：33,413,591人（35.8%）；老年人：50–69岁：17,700,270人（18.9%），70岁及以上：5,294,748人（5.7%），”他表示。伊托多指出，2026年的数据表明，选民登记册已增至103,428,715名登记选民，新增9,959,707名选民，增幅为10.66%，低于2023年录得的11.27%增幅。“2026年的年龄分布如下：青年：18–34岁：29,777,578人（28.79%）；中年：35–49岁：43,265,946人（41.83%）；老年人：50–69岁：22,982,900人（22.22%）；70岁及以上：7,402,291人（7.16%）。“这些数字说明了什么？尽管2026年选民登记总数增长了10.66%，但18–34岁登记选民人数减少了7,282,821人，降幅为19.65%。这一年龄类别在登记册中的占比也从2023年的39.6%降至2026年的28.79%，下降约10.9个百分点。“35–49岁登记选民人数增加了9,852,355人，增幅约为29.5%。这是否意味着年轻选民被从登记册中移除了？未必如此，”他指出。伊托多说，2023年至2026年间过去了三年，因此2023年32岁、33岁和34岁的选民到2026年时已进入35–49岁年龄类别。“这种人口结构变化可以部分解释青年类别人数减少和较高年龄类别人数增加的现象。然而，仅凭年龄增长无法完全说明这些变化。“还需要考察新加入登记册的人员，尤其是青年登记率，以及可能存在的行政调整。“这提出了一个关键问题：尼日利亚年轻选民登记投票的速度，是否足以补充那些因年龄增长而退出青年类别的选民？“从历史数据看，尼日利亚选民登记册从2015年的68,833,476人增至2019年的84,004,084人，增幅为22.04%。2019年至2023年间，登记册增至93,469,008人，新增9,464,924名选民（11.27%）。到2026年，登记册进一步增至103,428,715人，又新增9,959,707名选民（10.66%）。“尽管2023年至2026年的绝对增量略高于2019年至2023年，但百分比增幅略低。这些数据表明，尼日利亚选民登记册的增长率正在下降：2015–2019年为22.04%，2019–2023年为11.27%，2023–2026年为10.66%。不过，最近这一统计期涵盖三年，而非四年。“因此，关键问题不只是选民登记册是否在增长，还包括谁正在加入登记册、选民如何在各年龄类别之间转换，以及这些人口结构变化意味着什么，”他补充说。伊托多呼吁独立国家选举委员会（INEC）公布详细的年龄群组分析，解释2015年、2019年、2023年和2026年登记册之间的变化，包括新登记、年龄类别转换、移除登记册中已故及不符合资格的人员，以及其他调整。他说：“如果下降趋势表明新获得投票资格的年轻选民登记不足，就必须推动加大针对青年群体的选民登记动员投入。如果这反映了行政调整，就必须对这些变化作出明确记录和解释。”掌握先机。实时报道、突发独家消息和独家视角将直接推送到您的手机上。不要满足于过时新闻。加入 LEADERSHIP NEWS 的 WhatsApp，随时随地获取全天候最新消息 →

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: At least two people were feared to be trapped under debris after an under-construction house collapsed in the Milan Garden area of north east Delhi’s Harsh Vihar on Sunday evening. A Delhi Fire Service (DFS) official said that call regarding the collapse was received at 6.46pm, following which six fire tenders were pressed into service. Police personnel and rescue teams, including the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), rushed to the spot and began efforts to search for anyone who may have been trapped beneath the rubble. The operation was ongoing at the time of going to print. Among the two people who are reported to be missing are the contractor and his father, said the DFS official. “When the teams reached the location, they found that the building’s ground floor was an old structure, while the owners were carrying out construction on the first floor,” a senior police officer said. However, the circumstances that led to the collapse were not immediately clear, he said. The owner of the structure has been identified and traced, and legal proceedings have been initiated, the police official said, without giving further details. The incident comes amid a string of building collapses that have shined a spotlight on weak enforcement of building safety laws and lack of proper oversight. On October 7, at least four people died when a building collapsed in New Seemapuri with demolition work in an adjacent building, involving vibrating machines, suspected to have triggered the collapse. On September 6, a multi-storey boy's hostel collapsed, killing seven people, including five Delhi University students and two labourers. Prior to that, On May 30, a building collapsed in south Delhi’s Saidulajab, killing six people, including five doctors and engineers and one eatery owner. Unauthorised construction was suspected to be the cause in both the incidents
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.title_zh: 德里Harsh Vihar一栋在建建筑坍塌，至少2人恐被困
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 周日晚，一栋在建房屋在德里东北部Harsh Vihar的Milan Garden地区倒塌，至少有两人疑似被困在废墟下。德里消防局（DFS）一名官员表示，下午6时46分接到建筑倒塌报警，随后出动6辆消防车。警方人员和包括国家灾害响应部队（NDRF）在内的救援队赶赴现场，开始搜寻可能被困在废墟下的人员。截至付印时，搜寻工作仍在进行。DFS官员称，据报失踪的两人中包括承包商及其父亲。一名高级警官说：“救援队抵达现场时，发现该建筑底层是一处旧有结构，而业主正在一层进行施工。”不过，他表示，导致建筑倒塌的具体原因尚不清楚。该建筑业主已被确认并找到，警方已启动法律程序，但未透露进一步详情。这起事件发生在此前一系列建筑倒塌事故之中，这些事故暴露出建筑安全法律执法不力以及监管缺失等问题。10月7日，新西马普里一栋建筑在邻近建筑进行拆除作业时倒塌，至少造成4人死亡；此次拆除使用了振动机，被怀疑是引发倒塌的原因。9月6日，一栋多层男生宿舍楼倒塌，造成7人死亡，其中包括5名德里大学学生和2名劳工。此前，5月30日，德里南部Saidulajab一栋建筑倒塌，造成6人死亡，其中包括5名医生和工程师以及1名餐馆老板。这两起事故均疑似由未经许可的施工所致

Unlock these with Subscription What happens when the rhythms of Korean culture meet the beats of Telangana’s traditional drums? At Shilpakala Vedika here on Sunday, the answer unfolded through a lively mix of music, dance, martial arts and cultural exchange, as Korea Culture Day 2026 brought the traditions of two countries together on one stage. From afternoon, stalls selling Korean products drew curious visitors, with crowds gathering around them to explore a slice of Korean culture. As the evening approached, the buzz moved towards the auditorium, where hundreds of people began assembling from 5 p.m., eager to witness the performances lined up for the occasion. Inside, the anticipation gave way to a celebration that travelled between two cultures, from the precision and power of Korean martial arts to the vigorous movements of Telangana’s traditional dances. The programme began around 5.30 p.m. with an address by Lee Seong-ho, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India, who welcomed the audience to Hyderabad and spoke of the cultural ties that the event hoped to strengthen. Drawing a connection between Diwali, India’s festival of lights, and Chuseok, Korea’s harvest festival, Mr. Lee spoke about the shared values underlying celebrations in both countries: family, togetherness, gratitude and hope for the future. Though the traditions may differ, he said, the emotions they evoke are remarkably similar. Cultural exchanges, he added, help people discover just how much they have in common. Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, who addressed the gathering, spoke about Korea’s transformation into a global economic and cultural force. He noted how Korean music, cinema and television had found audiences across the world, demonstrating that a country’s influence extended beyond its economic and military strength to the power of its cultural imagination. He also highlighted the historical connections between India and Korea and Hyderabad’s long-standing identity as a meeting point of cultures, languages and traditions. "Telangana’s festivals, arts and heritage were an important part of its identity as a state looking towards a globally connected future," he added. Beyond culture, Mr. Vikramarka pointed to opportunities for closer cooperation between Telangana and Korean enterprises in areas such as electronics, electric vehicles, advanced manufacturing, renewable energy and emerging technologies. The Daekyung Taekwondo Demonstration was among the evening’s most energetic acts. The performers combined agility, strength and precision in a series of martial arts displays, breaking tiles and executing impressive stunts that drew loud cheers from the crowd. Each demonstration was met with excitement, turning the auditorium into a space of applause and animated reactions. The programme then shifted to the vigorous rhythms of Telangana’s Perini Shiva Tandavam. The traditional dance, known for its powerful movements and historical association with warriors, brought a distinctly local flavour to the evening. The Telangana Dappulu performance followed, filling the programme with the forceful beats of traditional drums. The audience was then introduced to Korean traditional performance through Eolssigu, before a violin duo offered another musical dimension to the evening. The Atti Classic Vocal Crossover Performance further broadened the programme’s musical range, leading into an instrumental performance by a Korean band that brought the cultural showcase to a close. Unlock these with Subscription The Delhi government is set to introduce Individual Aftercare Plans (IAPs) for teenagers exiting Child Care Institutions (CCIs) at 18, based on their specific circumstances, requirements and rehabilitation needs, under the proposed ‘Aftercare Scheme for Young Persons’, a senior government official said on Sunday. Under the scheme, the eligible beneficiaries will receive up to ₹2 lakh for higher education and ₹60,000 for vocational training. The scheme is likely to be approved by the Delhi Cabinet soon, according to a senior government official. In May, the Women and Child Development Department proposed a budget of ₹3.50 crore for the implementation of the scheme for the current financial year. The government also plans to allocate ₹5 crore from the Chief Minister’s Development Fund to strengthen the juvenile justice system, including the aftercare scheme, the official said. The government is also seeking Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partnerships to provide mentorship, additional financial resources, and other forms of support. The scheme will be implemented under a two-tier structure where the District Aftercare Committees will assess eligibility, map out individual plans, and track beneficiary progress, and the State Aftercare Committees will oversee the implementation, fund disbursement and policy reforms. “There will also be a provision for financial assistance, subject to the recommendation of the District Aftercare Committee, for eligible young people who have no income or insufficient income,” the official said. “A database of individuals eligible for aftercare will be maintained and these individuals will be recommended to various Delhi government departments for internships, contractual roles, or outsourced employment opportunities, provided they meet the prescribed eligibility criteria,” the official added. Under the scheme, the government will start preparations when a child in a CCI is 15 years old, with focus on acquiring the skills necessary for living independently. By the time they turn 17, officials will evaluate their readiness and specific support needs. “Post 18 years, the aftercare support will cover education, training, housing, financial assistance, mentorship and employment, based on an individualised aftercare plan,” the official said. Delhi currently has around 88 CCIs operated jointly by the government and various non-governmental organisations. These homes provide care, protection, education and rehabilitation to children up to the age of 18. Every year, between 150 and 200 young adults exit these institutions after turning 18, according to officials. As per the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, support is generally provided up to the age of 21. However, in exceptional circumstances, and upon the recommendation of competent bodies, it may be extended up to the age of 23, the official added. https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.title: Nigeria Customs Tests New Cargo Scanners, Tracking Systems in China
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.summary: The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and Trade Modernisation Project Limited (TMPL) have completed factory acceptance tests for newly acquired cargo scanners and electronic tracking systems in China ahead of their deployment in Nigeria. The new scanners are designed to examine cargo without requiring routine physical opening of containers, while the electronic tracking system will enable Customs officers to monitor consignments in real time as they move from ports to their final destinations.
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.summary_zh: 尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）与贸易现代化项目有限公司（TMPL）在中国完成了新购置货物扫描仪和电子追踪系统的工厂验收测试，随后这些设备将部署到尼日利亚。新扫描仪能够在无需例行打开集装箱的情况下检查货物，电子追踪系统则将使海关官员能够实时监控货物从港口运往最终目的地的全过程。
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.body: The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and Trade Modernisation Project Limited (TMPL) have completed factory acceptance tests for newly acquired cargo scanners and electronic tracking systems in China ahead of their deployment in Nigeria. The equipment is expected to strengthen cargo examination, improve revenue collection, curb cargo diversion and enhance the detection of concealed and prohibited items at the country’s entry and exit points. The two-week Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), conducted from October 9 to 20, 2026, took place at the facilities of Nuctech Company Limited, the Chinese manufacturer of the equipment. The exercise was led by the Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of the Information Communication and Technology/Modernisation Department, Oluyomi Adebakin, and involved technical experts from the NCS and TMPL. The team conducted technical verification of the newly acquired Non-Intrusive Inspection (NII) equipment and Electronic Cargo Tracking System (ECTS) to ensure they met contractual specifications and international operational standards before shipment to Nigeria. Speaking during the exercise, Adebakin reaffirmed Comptroller-General of Customs Adewale Adeniyi’s commitment to deploying modern technology to facilitate legitimate trade, optimise revenue generation and strengthen national security. She described the factory acceptance test as a critical quality-assurance process that would ensure the equipment was fit for purpose before deployment. The new scanners are designed to examine cargo without requiring routine physical opening of containers, while the electronic tracking system will enable Customs officers to monitor consignments in real time as they move from ports to their final destinations. The integration of both technologies is expected to improve cargo visibility, strengthen risk management and reduce opportunities for diversion and other irregularities along the supply chain. Also speaking, the Acting Comptroller of Non-Intrusive Inspection, Deputy Comptroller of Customs Umar Madugu, said the deployment of the equipment would significantly reduce the need for 100 per cent physical examination of cargo. According to him, the systems would minimise human contact in cargo inspection, curb diversion and improve operational efficiency across Customs formations. Madugu added that the technology would support more targeted inspections, allowing officers to concentrate on high-risk consignments while facilitating faster clearance for compliant traders. Speaking on behalf of TMPL, the company’s General Manager, Bamidele Chinedu, described the factory acceptance test as a significant milestone in the implementation of the Trade Modernisation Project. He said the integration of NII scanners and the Electronic Cargo Tracking System was central to establishing a transparent, efficient and technology-driven Customs administration. Chinedu noted that combining modern scanning technology with electronic cargo monitoring would strengthen operational controls and support the Service’s broader modernisation agenda. In his remarks, Niu Chao, Project Manager at Nuctech Company Limited, expressed the company’s commitment to delivering world-class equipment and providing the technical support required for effective implementation. He also assured the Nigerian delegation of continued assistance through capacity building, equipment maintenance and after-sales services to support the systems’ long-term performance. Beyond the equipment verification, technical experts from the NCS and TMPL received training during the exercise on the operation, handling and maintenance of the scanners and electronic tracking systems. The training is expected to equip Nigerian personnel with the technical skills required for the equipment’s deployment, routine operation and maintenance, while reducing potential disruptions after installation. The factory acceptance test marks a key stage in preparations for introducing the new technology into Nigeria’s Customs operations. Once deployed, the systems are expected to support faster cargo processing, improve compliance monitoring, strengthen revenue assurance and enhance the Service’s capacity to detect illicit goods. The initiative forms part of the NCS’s broader modernisation drive to use digital technology and automation to improve trade facilitation, operational transparency and border security
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.title_zh: 尼日利亚海关在中国测试新货物扫描仪和追踪系统
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.body_zh: 尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）和贸易现代化项目有限公司（TMPL）在中国对新购置的货物扫描仪和电子追踪系统完成了出厂验收测试，随后这些设备将部署到尼日利亚。这些设备有望加强货物查验、提高税收征管效率、遏制货物转移，并增强该国口岸发现藏匿物品和违禁品的能力。此次为期两周的出厂验收测试（FAT）于2026年10月9日至20日进行，地点是设备中国制造商Nuctech Company Limited的厂区。测试由负责信息通信技术及现代化部门的海关副总监长Oluyomi Adebakin主持，尼日利亚海关总署和TMPL的技术专家参与。测试团队对新购置的非侵入式检查（NII）设备和电子货物追踪系统（ECTS）进行了技术核验，以确保其符合合同规格和国际运行标准后再运往尼日利亚。Adebakin在测试期间表示，海关总监长Adewale Adeniyi重申了部署现代技术的决心，以促进合法贸易、优化收入增长并加强国家安全。她称，出厂验收测试是一项关键的质量保证流程，可确保设备在部署前适合其预期用途。新扫描仪能够在无需例行拆开集装箱的情况下检查货物，电子追踪系统则将使海关官员能够实时监控货物从港口运往最终目的地的全过程。两项技术的整合有望提高货物可视性、强化风险管理，并减少供应链中出现货物转移及其他违规行为的机会。代理非侵入式检查总监长、海关副总监长Umar Madugu也表示，部署这些设备将显著减少对货物进行100%人工实物查验的需要。他说，这些系统将尽量减少货物查验中的人为接触，遏制货物转移，并提高海关各部门的运行效率。Madugu补充称，这项技术将支持更有针对性的查验，使官员能够集中处理高风险货物，同时为合规贸易商提供更快捷的通关服务。TMPL总经理Bamidele Chinedu代表公司发言时，将此次出厂验收测试描述为贸易现代化项目实施过程中的一个重要里程碑。他说，整合非侵入式检查扫描仪与电子货物追踪系统，是建立透明、高效且以技术驱动的海关管理体系的核心。Chinedu指出，将现代扫描技术与电子货物监控相结合，将强化运营管控，并支持海关总署更广泛的现代化议程。Nuctech Company Limited项目经理Niu Chao在发言中表示，该公司致力于提供世界一流的设备，并为设备的有效实施提供所需的技术支持。他还承诺，通过能力建设、设备维护和售后服务，继续向尼日利亚代表团提供协助，以支持这些系统的长期运行。除核验设备外，尼日利亚海关总署和TMPL的技术专家还在此次活动中接受了有关扫描仪和电子追踪系统操作、使用与维护的培训。此次培训将使尼日利亚人员掌握设备部署、日常运行和维护所需的技术技能，同时降低安装后可能出现的运行中断。出厂验收测试标志着将该新技术引入尼日利亚海关业务准备工作的一个关键阶段。系统部署后，有望加快货物处理、改善合规监管、强化税收保障，并增强海关总署发现非法商品的能力。该举措是尼日利亚海关总署更广泛现代化计划的一部分，旨在利用数字技术和自动化手段促进贸易便利化、提高运营透明度并加强边境安全

It focused on grassroots mobilization and the consolidation of support for President Tinubu across the South-South and South-East geopolitical zones. He added the campaign trail will ensure that the message of the Renewed Hope reaches every doorstep, emphasizing that an alliance with Tompolo as Convener of the Movement is strategic. He also expressed profound gratitude to the President for assenting to the South-East Development Commission Act, which he said was an important step towards addressing reconstruction, infrastructure and development priorities in the South-East. “As a representative of Bende Federal Constituency, I particularly appreciate President Tinubu’s assent to the South-East Development Commission Act, an important step towards addressing reconstruction, infrastructure and development priorities in our region”, Kalu said. He also urged the Movement to embody the highest standards of democratic participation by listening to citizens’ concerns. “Nigeria benefits when citizens can exchange ideas peacefully and participate in public life with confidence and dignity,” Kalu said. https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/h.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Picture this. Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma scored centuries to power India to a big win. Now ask yourself: which of the two blazed her way to triple figures? If your gut said Harmanpreet, it failed you. On a sweltering Sunday at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi, the second ODI against Zimbabwe turned the script on its head. A restrained Harmanpreet played the artisan while Deepti played destroyer, with their record-breaking 153-run fifth-wicket stand laying the foundation of India’s 121-run win and unassailable 2-0 lead. India was stuttering at 19 for two in the third over — Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma both undone by Nomvelo Sibanda’s short-ball ploy — when Harmanpreet joined Pratika Rawal. Pratika, fresh from a hundred in the first ODI, and Harmanpreet added 124 off 118 balls. The former looked set for another ton when Nyasha Gwanzura deceived her with a change of pace. Tejal Hasabnis followed soon after. But Harmanpreet remained unfazed, aided by a fearless Deepti who arrived as if stepping in for a net session. As many as 32 of the pair’s first 47 runs came through Deepti’s audacious shots on the leg-side while Harmanpreet whipped out a catalogue of puritanical drives and cuts on the off-side. When the century came, celebrations oddly didn’t. Neither did tears, like the 91 she scored in the third T20I had drawn out of her. Deepti, too, eventually braved a slowdown to reach her second ODI century in the final over — nine years after her first — helping India set an intimidating 329-run target. Modester Mupachikwa’s sprightly start, despite losing Loryn Phiri early, gave Zimbabwe hope. With support from Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano, the Lady Chevrons got to 100 in just 19 overs, helped by India’s worrying inability to take wickets, especially the seamers. Sayali Satghare finally succeeded in breaching Mugeri-Tiripano’s defence. Left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma’s guile and persistence then took centrestage. She removed Mupachikwa for her maiden ODI wicket before dismissing Beloved Biza, Michelle Mavunga and skipper Josephine Nkomo in a cluster. Deepti ran through the tail before Jintimani Kalita opened her account in the format. While Zimbabwe ticked one box by crossing 200, its bid to last the full 50 overs was yet to be achieved. The scores: India 328/6 in 50 overs (Pratika Rawal 61, Harmanpreet Kaur 126, Deepti Sharma 106 n.o.) bt Zimbabwe 207 in 48.5 overs (Modester Mupachikwa 49, Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano 46, Beloved Biza 34, Deepti 3/32, Vaishnavi Sharma 4/39). https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/h.body_zh: 订阅可享受《The Hindu》深度报道、评论、社论等更多内容。订阅即可解锁。请看这张图片。哈曼普里特·考尔和迪普蒂·夏尔马双双攻入百分世纪 innings，帮助印度取得一场大胜。现在问问自己：两人中是谁一路狂奔，打出了三位数得分？如果你的直觉认为是哈曼普里特，那它可让你失望了。在科坦比BCA体育场举行的这个炎热星期天，对津巴布韦的第二场ODI比赛彻底逆转了局势。哈曼普里特稳守反击，迪普蒂则火力全开；两人创纪录的第五wicket搭档贡献153分，为印度以121分取胜和无可撼动的2比0领先奠定基础。第三轮时，印度仅得19分便已失去2个门球——斯姆里蒂·曼达娜和沙法莉·维尔马都被诺姆韦洛·西班达利用短球战术击败。哈曼普里特此时与普拉蒂卡·拉瓦尔搭档。普拉蒂卡刚刚在首场ODI中攻入百分球，哈曼普里特与她合力用118个球得到124分。普拉蒂卡一度有望再次攻入百分球，但尼亚莎·瓜祖拉通过变速球骗过了她。特哈尔·哈萨布尼斯随后也遭到淘汰。不过，哈曼普里特始终不为所动，无畏的迪普蒂也前来助阵，她仿佛直接进入了球网训练状态。两人开局47分中的多达32分来自迪普蒂在腿侧的大胆击球，而哈曼普里特则在偏侧打出一系列教科书般端正的推球和切球。哈曼普里特攻入百分球时，庆祝场面却出人意料地平静。她也没有落泪——此前她在第三场T20I中得到的91分曾让她泪流满面。迪普蒂最终也顶住放缓的攻势，在最后一轮攻入个人第二个ODI百分世纪——距离她首次达成这一成绩已有9年——帮助印度设下极具压力的329分目标。莫德斯泰·穆帕奇克瓦开局灵动，虽然早些时候失去洛琳·菲里，仍给津巴布韦带来希望。在奇波·穆杰里-蒂里帕诺的支持下，女雪佛龙车队仅用19轮便得到100分；印度令人担忧的无力取particularly，尤其是缺乏来自速度型投球手的牵制，帮了对手大忙。萨亚莉·萨特加雷终于成功突破穆杰里-蒂里帕诺的防守。左手旋球手瓦伊什纳维·夏尔马随即凭借变化与韧劲成为焦点。她先以个人首个ODI wickets淘汰穆帕奇克瓦，随后又接连击败贝洛韦德·比扎、米歇尔·马温加和队长约瑟芬·恩科莫。迪普蒂清扫了尾部阵容，之后金蒂马尼·卡利塔也在这一赛制中收获首个 wickets。津巴布韦虽然跨过200分大关，却未能坚持打满全部50轮。比分：印度在50轮中得328/6分（普拉蒂卡·拉瓦尔61分，哈曼普里特·考尔126分，迪普蒂·夏尔马106分未出局）击败津巴布韦，后者在48.5轮中得207分（莫德斯泰·穆帕奇克瓦49分，奇波·穆杰里-蒂里帕诺46分，贝洛韦德·比扎34分，迪普蒂3/32，瓦伊什纳维·夏尔马4/39）。评论必须使用英文，并以完整句子表达。评论不得包含辱骂或针对个人的攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已经是《The Hindu》注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与我们的文章互动。如果你没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录自己的账户后，可以访问以前的评论。
