Unlock these with Subscription The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) is in the process of retrofitting 250 old diesel buses into electric vehicles in the first phase as part of its efforts to reduce emissions. Speaking on Saturday (October 24, 2026) at the foundation-laying ceremony for a new bus terminal at Uppal Zonal Workshop, with an estimated cost of ₹3.22 crore, Mr. Ponnam Parbhakar, Minister of Transport and BC Welfare, said that the move was part of a larger push toward clean mobility. He added that 3,000 electric buses have already been added to the RTC fleet, and another 2,200 are expected to be inducted under the PM e-Drive initiative. Touching upon the principal demand of TGSRTC workers and unions to merge the corporation with the government, he said that efforts toward this are underway. Following the recently held trade union elections after a gap of 10 years, a committee would be constituted with the elected recognised union to initiate the process, he added. The Minister said the government was also in the process of addressing the issue of pensions of retired employees and clearing pending contributions relating to the CCS and provident fund in phases. Pay Revision Commission (PRC) recommendations had been implemented, and no DA was outstanding, he said. Referring to the flagship Mahalakshmi scheme, Mr. Prabhakar said women had made several crore journeys free of cost under the scheme, resulting in substantial savings on travel expenses. The RTC was being developed with a focus on passenger convenience, employee welfare and the protection of the organisation, he said. The proposed bus terminal at Uppal would have modern facilities to serve nearly one lakh passengers a day. About 1,053 bus trips originate from the location, with services connecting places such as Bhongir, Yadagirigutta, Hanamkonda and Warangal. The terminal would serve the Peerzadiguda and Boduppal areas and be named accordingly, Mr Prabhakar said. The project is expected to be completed within 100 days. Mr. Prabhakar also said the government was promoting electric vehicles through its EV policy, under which zero tax was applicable to eligible vehicles. An allocation of ₹200 crore has been earmarked for electric vehicles, including autos, in the Core Urban Region. Automated testing stations were also being established, while reflectors and a vehicle scrapping policy had been introduced to improve road safety. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/kadu.body: The Kaduna State Government has dismissed as fabricated a viral letter alleging that Gov. Uba Sani approved and released N2.3 trillion for the APC presidential campaign flag-off. The government described the purported letter as fraudulent and misleading, accusing its authors of attempting to damage the governor’s reputation for fiscal discipline and responsible governance. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki, stated this in a statement on Saturday in Kaduna. Maiyaki said the letter, dated Oct. 18, 2026, and titled “Notification for Preparations for the Grand Rally Flag Off”, contained inconsistencies that questioned its authenticity. He said the purported letter, allegedly addressed to Sen. Abdulazeez Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, falsely claimed that N2.3 trillion was released for the campaign flag-off. The commissioner noted that Kaduna’s 2026 budget stood at N985.92 billion, making the alleged expenditure more than twice the state’s annual budget. He said the claim was financially implausible and unsupported by any authentic appropriation, approval or expenditure records. Maiyaki also identified irregularities, including the misspelling of the governor’s surname as “Uba Sai” and the apparent unauthorised reproduction of his signature. “The Kaduna State Government categorically disowns this document. Gov. Uba Sani neither authored nor authorised the purported letter, and no N2.3 trillion was budgeted, approved or released,” he said. He described the allegation as fictitious and a deliberate attempt to mislead the public. Maiyaki said that since assuming office on May 29, 2023, Sani had prioritised fiscal discipline, transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources. He listed investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection among the administration’s priorities. The commissioner expressed concern over what he described as coordinated misinformation aimed at discrediting the governor and his administration ahead of the 2027 general elections. He warned that fabricating official correspondence and circulating false financial claims could constitute criminal offences. “Political competition must be conducted within the bounds of truth, decency and the law,” Maiyaki said, urging critics to rely on credible evidence when questioning government expenditure. He disclosed that steps were being taken to establish the origin of the purported letter. Maiyaki also called on security and investigative agencies to examine the document and ensure that anyone found culpable faced appropriate legal action. He urged media organisations and members of the public to verify documents before circulating or publishing allegations concerning public expenditure. The commissioner reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to peace, institutional strengthening, infrastructure development, citizens’ welfare and sustainable governance. He said the government would remain focused on prudent financial management and would not be distracted by what it described as deliberate misinformation. Unlock these with Subscription North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appears to have arrived on an unannounced visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong, a government source in Seoul and South Korean media said on Saturday (October 24, 2026). Mr. Kim crossed via a major border bridge that only officially opened last week -- 12 years after its completion -- deepening economic ties between China and diplomatically isolated, nuclear-armed North Korea. Neither North Korea nor China disclosed Kim’s visit in advance. South Korean lawmaker Youn Kun-young said Kim was “understood” to have met Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Saturday (October 24). South Korea’s ruling Democratic Party said Mr. Youn had been briefed that Kim was likely to return home later the same day. China is North Korea’s largest trading partner and a vital source of diplomatic, economic and political support for Pyongyang, although ties have not always been smooth. The Yonhap news agency first reported Kim’s arrival, citing an unidentified South Korean government source. A separate government source told AFP that the North Korean leader appeared to have crossed into China via the recently opened New Yalu River Bridge. Lawmaker Youn said he had been briefed on Friday (October 23) about the likely visit. World leaders are preparing for November’s APEC summit in China’s Shenzhen, where it has been speculated that Kim may meet U.S. President Donald Trump. Neither the Chinese foreign ministry nor the North Korean embassy in Beijing immediately responded to AFP’s requests for comment on Saturday (October 23). South Korea’s government said it could not confirm Kim’s itinerary in China. The New Yalu River Bridge was completed in 2014 but its opening was delayed due to a lack of connecting roads and customs facilities on the North Korean side, according to South Korean news reports. Its opening came a little more than a month after North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge. By meeting Mr. Li in Dandong, Mr. Kim “may have sought to reaffirm the economic cooperation agreed during Xi Jinping’s visit to North Korea” earlier this year, and “press China to move more quickly on those commitments”, Yang Moo-jin, former president of the South’s University of North Korean Studies, told AFP . “He may also have sought Beijing’s active support and cooperation ahead of a possible summit with Trump in Shenzhen.” Hours before Yonhap’s report, North Korea’s state media said he had urged his military at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang to train to become the strongest in the world. Mr. Kim’s call for what he dubbed a “Korean-style military revolution” came the same week Seoul’s military proposed talks to clarify the border after an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) further strained inter-Korean ties. Seoul’s military proposed the talks on Friday (October 23) after it blamed the blast, which injured South Korean soldiers, on North Korean landmines. Pyongyang strongly rejects the claim. North Korea has not responded to the proposal and previously rejected the South’s demand for an apology over the explosion. The countries remain technically at war as their 1950-53 conflict ended in an armistice, not a peace treaty. Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung -- who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions -- suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of its nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief. Critics say such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal. Analysts say China has also appeared to move towards implicit acceptance. Mr. Kim hosted Xi Jinping in Pyongyang in June, soon after Xi held back-to-back summits in Beijing with Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin. Neither Pyongyang nor Beijing mentioned North Korean denuclearisation in their official statements -- an omission experts saw as a sign of China’s tacit consent. 据首尔一名政府消息人士和韩国媒体周六（2026年10月24日）报道，朝鲜领导人金正恩似乎已对中国边境城市丹东进行了一次未事先公布的访问。金正恩经由一座主要边境大桥过境，该桥直到上周才正式启用，而其建设早在12年前就已竣工；此举进一步深化了中国与外交孤立的核武装朝鲜之间的经济关系。朝鲜和中国均未提前披露金正恩此次访问。

韩国议员尹根镛表示，朝鲜领导人“据称”已于周六（10月24日）会见中国国务院总理李强。韩国执政党民主党称，尹根镛接到简报称，金正恩可能于当天较晚时候回国。中国是朝鲜最大的贸易伙伴，也是平壤在外交、经济和政治上的重要支持来源，尽管双方关系并非一直顺畅。

韩联社最先报道金正恩抵达的消息，并援引一名身份未公开的韩国政府消息人士。另一名政府消息人士告诉法新社，这名朝鲜领导人似乎是经由最近启用的新鸭绿江大桥进入中国。尹根镛议员说，他已于周五（10月23日）接到简报，得知金正恩很可能进行了此次访问。

各国领导人正在为11月于中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织峰会做准备，外界猜测金正恩可能会在那里会见美国总统唐纳德·特朗普。中国外交部和中国驻北京朝鲜使馆均未立即回应法新社周六（10月23日）的置评请求。韩国政府表示，无法确认金正恩在中国的行程。

据韩国新闻报道，新鸭绿江大桥于2014年竣工，但由于朝鲜一侧缺乏连接道路和海关设施，其启用被推迟。该桥启用前不久，朝鲜和俄罗斯也开通了首座公路桥。

韩国延北大学前校长杨慕真对法新社表示，金正恩在丹东会见李强总理，“可能是想重申今年早些时候习近平访问朝鲜期间达成的经济合作协议”，并“敦促中国更快履行这些承诺”。他说：“他也可能是在寻求北京的积极支持与合作，为可能在深圳与特朗普举行的峰会作准备。”

韩联社报道前数小时，朝鲜国家媒体称，金正恩在平壤举行的两天连长会议上要求军方加强训练，成为世界上最强大的军队。金正恩将他所称的“朝鲜式军事革命”提上日程之际，首尔军方提议举行会谈，以澄清非军事区（DMZ）内发生爆炸后边境局势；这场爆炸使韩朝关系进一步紧张。

首尔军方于周五（10月23日）提出会谈，称这起爆炸造成韩国士兵受伤，应归咎于朝鲜地雷。平壤强烈否认这一说法。朝鲜尚未回应这一提议，此前也拒绝了韩方就爆炸事件提出的道歉要求。两国在技术上仍处于战争状态，因为1950年至1953年的冲突最终以停战协定告终，而非和平条约。

尽管联合国制裁长期存在，朝鲜已通过法律确认其核武装国家地位，政权多次宣称其核武库是永久且不可逆转的。韩国鸽派总统李在明曾多次提出无条件与平壤对话。他于9月建议，华盛顿应以冻结朝鲜核计划、而非立即消除该计划，作为换取解除制裁的筹码。批评者称，这种做法可能默认朝鲜作为核武装国家的地位，同时让平壤在不放弃核武库的情况下获得制裁解除。分析人士称，中国似乎也正转向默认接受这一现实。

金正恩于6月在平壤接待习近平，此前习近平刚刚在北京接连与特朗普和普京举行峰会。平壤和北京在官方声明中均未提及朝鲜无核化问题，而专家认为，这种省略被视为中国默许的信号。

https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/u.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription With about 10 days left for the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, talk of a Democratic wave has shifted from opinion polls to voting reality. Every major forecast now predicts the Democrats will win the House of Representatives. Statistician Nate Silver gives them a 75% chance of winning the Senate, which Republicans held strongly just a month ago. The Grand Old Party faces five main problems: a President who is a liability, weak candidates, money not swaying voters, fissures in their heartland, and a party base turning against its own. Let us begin with the President. Midterms are often a verdict on the White House. Donald Trump has made this election about himself, telling crowds to “pretend I’m on the ballot”. His approval rating is below 40%. In September, he told Republicans in tight races that he would visit “every one of those 35 places”. But he has campaigned in fewer than a third. Most stops have been in States he won easily, such as Oklahoma, Alabama, Tennessee, and Montana, which he said was his way “to thank them”. When a President rallies supporters in States that he won by huge margins two years earlier instead of margin seats, it conveys a hint of desperation. The next issue is candidate quality. Texas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988. This year, the Republican nominee is Ken Paxton, who was impeached by the Texas House in 2023 and later acquitted by the State Senate. He was also observed partying in 2025 in Dubai with two Pakistani-American federal fugitives who were also his donors. His Democratic opponent, James Talarico, a former teacher and State legislator, was leading by two points in a Fox News poll (but the latest Fox News poll listed for October 15-19 showed a 49%-49% tie); and by three points in a University of Texas poll (September 25-October 5). The third problem is in the heartland. Kansas has sent only Republicans to this Senate seat since 1919, the longest streak for any party in U.S. history. Republican incumbent Roger Marshall is tied in the polls with Adam Hamilton, a Methodist pastor who started one of the country’s largest churches. In Nebraska — a State Mr. Trump won by over 20 points — Democrats have stepped aside for Dan Osborn, a former union leader running as an independent. He is about three points behind Senator Pete Ricketts. When a party spends the last two weeks defending strongholds of Kansas and Nebraska, it is on the back foot. The fourth issue is money. Elon Musk, who split from Mr. Trump last year, is now the biggest known donor in this election, having given over $276 million to Republican groups since July. Recent filings show that Mr. Musk gave $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund and a separate $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, which supports Mr. Paxton’s Senate campaign. Even so, Mr. Talarico, the Democratic candidate, is still ahead. Money can buy TV advertisements, but it cannot easily overcome a national mood shaped by high prices, an unpopular war with Iran, and immigration raids. Ohio combines these issues, making it the most revealing race. Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate backed by Mr. Trump, seemed confirmed for Governor in a State that the President has won three times. His opponent, Amy Acton, looked like an easy target. As Ohio’s highly unpopular health director during the COVID-19 pandemic, she ordered lockdowns, faced armed protesters at her home, and had Republicans try to strip her powers before she resigned in 2020. Mr. Ramaswamy and his supporters have spent about $101 million on advertisements, including $36 million of his own money, about three times what Ms. Acton has spent. Still, he was trailing her recently by about three points on average. Among independent voters, his net rating is minus 25, the lowest for a Republican candidate for Governor in Ohio this century. This week, his campaign announced plans to spend $4 million promoting an advertisement featuring Ms. Acton’s estranged mother calling her a liar, drawing criticism from Republicans, including Governor Mike DeWine and Senator Jon Husted. Much of this can be explained by the national mood, since the party’s Senate candidate in Ohio is also behind by a similar amount. But some of Mr. Ramaswamy’s problems come from within his own party. His rival in the Republican primary, Casey Putsch, posted a video of himself with a rifle inviting him to play “cowboys versus Indians”. He called Mr. Ramaswamy an “anchor baby” and said that there was “nothing remotely American” about him. Still, nearly one in five Republican primary voters picked Mr. Putsch. Far-right commentator Nick Fuentes told his followers to oppose Mr. Ramaswamy, while students at a conservative youth event questioned whether a Hindu could represent a Christian State. The anger goes back to the H-1B controversy in December 2024, when Mr. Ramaswamy said American culture undervalued excellence, which angered ‘Make America Great Again’ (MAGA) voters. Now, the same party that once questioned who belongs in America is asking the same question about its own candidate. Ohio is an apt lesson for the Republicans. A party can get through having an unpopular President, a weak candidate, or a tough electoral map in any given year. But it is much harder when all these problems happen at once and the party’s base starts judging its own candidates by their race, background and religion. If Democrats win Texas, Kansas, Nebraska, or Ohio on November 3, it will be a wave, and the Republicans will have helped make it. Perhaps they deserve that loss. https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/u.body_zh: 订阅还可享受 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。距离美国11月3日中期选举还有约10天，关于“民主党浪潮”的讨论已从民意调查转向实际投票结果。如今，所有主要预测都认为民主党将赢得众议院。统计学家内特·银估计民主党赢得参议院的概率为75%，而共和党一个月前还稳稳控制着参议院。共和党面临五大主要问题：一位成为拖累的总统、软弱的候选人、无法左右选民的资金、其腹地内部的裂痕，以及开始反对本党的党派基础。先从总统说起。中期选举往往是对白宫执政表现的一次裁决。唐纳德·特朗普把这场选举变成了围绕自己的竞选活动，告诉支持者要“假装我也在选票上”。他的支持率低于40%。今年9月，他告诉身处胶着选区的共和党人，自己会拜访“那35个地方中的每一个”。但他实际 campaigned 的选区不到三分之一。大多数行程都安排在他轻松获胜的州，例如俄克拉何马州、阿拉巴马州、田纳西州和蒙大拿州；他说，这是为了“感谢他们”。当一位总统在两年前以巨大优势获胜的州拉票，而不是在势均力敌的选区助选时，这多少透露出他的绝望。第二个问题是候选人质量。得克萨斯州自1988年以来就没有选出过民主党参议员。今年，共和党候选人是肯·帕克斯顿，他于2023年被得克萨斯州众议院弹劾，随后又获州参议院判无罪。2025年，还有人看到他在迪拜与两名巴基斯坦裔美国联邦逃犯一起聚会，那两人也是他的捐助者。他的民主党对手詹姆斯·塔拉里科曾是一名教师和州议员，在福克斯新闻的一项民调中领先2个百分点（但福克斯新闻10月15日至19日发布的最新民调显示双方以49%对49%持平）；在得克萨斯大学9月25日至10月5日的一项民调中领先3个百分点。第三个问题出在腹地。堪萨斯州自1919年以来一直把该参议院席位交给共和党，这是美国历史上任何政党保持同一席位控制时间最长的纪录。共和党现任参议员罗杰·马歇尔在民调中与亚当·汉密尔顿持平。后者是一名卫理公会牧师，创建了美国最大的教会之一。内布拉斯加州——特朗普先生以超过20个百分点优势赢得的州——民主党没有推举候选人，转而支持以独立人士身份参选的丹·奥斯本。他是一名前工会领袖，目前落后参议员皮特·里凯茨约3个百分点。当一个政党在最后两周忙于捍卫堪萨斯州和内布拉斯加州的票仓时，它就处于被动挨打的状态。第四个问题是资金。埃隆·马斯克去年与特朗普先生分道扬镳，如今已成为本次选举中已知最大的捐助者，自7月以来向共和党团体捐赠了超过2.76亿美元。近期申报文件显示，马斯克先生向参议院领导基金捐赠了1.58亿美元，还另行向支持帕克斯顿先生参议员竞选的 Lone Star Liberty PAC 捐赠了1,000万美元。即便如此，民主党候选人塔拉里科先生仍然领先。资金可以买到电视广告，但难以轻易扭转一种全国性情绪，而这种情绪受到高物价、对伊朗战争的不满以及移民突袭的影响。俄亥俄州集这些问题于一体，因此成为最能揭示趋势的选区。特朗普先生支持的总统候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米，似乎已锁定在这个由总统三次赢得的州担任州长。他的对手艾米·阿克顿看上去是一个容易对付的目标。她在新冠疫情期间担任俄亥俄州颇不受欢迎的卫生主管时，下令实施封锁，在家中面对武装抗议者，还曾遭到共和党人试图剥夺其权力，最终她于2020年辞职。拉马斯瓦米先生及其支持者在广告上投入了约1.01亿美元，其中3,600万美元来自他本人，约为阿克顿女士支出的三倍。但截至近日，他平均仍落后她约3个百分点。在独立选民中，他的净支持率为负25，是本世纪俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人中最低的。本周，他的竞选团队宣布计划投入400万美元推广一则广告，广告中阿克顿女士关系疏远的母亲指责她撒谎，招来共和党人的批评，其中包括州长迈克·德怀恩和参议员乔恩·赫斯特德。其中很大一部分可以用全国性情绪来解释，因为该党的俄亥俄州参议员候选人也落后相近的幅度。但拉马斯瓦米先生的一些问题来自本党内部。他在共和党初选中的对手凯西·普奇发布了一段自己持步枪的视频，邀请拉马斯瓦米来玩“牛仔对印第安人”。他称拉马斯瓦米先生是“锚定婴儿”，并说他身上“没有任何 remotely American 的东西”。即便如此，近五分之一的共和党初选选民仍选择了普奇先生。极右翼评论员尼克·富恩特斯告诉追随者要反对拉马斯瓦米先生，而参加保守派青年活动的学生则质疑一名印度教徒能否代表一个基督教州。这种愤怒可以追溯到2024年12月的H-1B争议。当时，拉马斯瓦米先生说美国文化低估卓越，激怒了“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）选民。如今，这个曾质疑谁才属于美国的政党，也开始对自己的候选人提出同样的问题。俄亥俄州给共和党上了一堂合适的课。一个政党在某个特定年份即使面临不受欢迎的总统、软弱的候选人或艰难的选区版图，也有可能过关。但当所有这些问题同时出现，党派基础开始根据候选人的族裔、背景和宗教信仰评判本党候选人时，政党过关就要困难得多。如果民主党在11月3日赢得得克萨斯州、堪萨斯州、内布拉斯加州或俄亥俄州，那就会形成浪潮，而共和党将助长这一浪潮。或许他们正是咎由自取。评论必须使用英语，并且必须是完整句子。评论不得带有辱骂性或人身攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已经是《The Unlock these with Subscription Haryana Police is working with the CBI to finalise modalities for the deportation of fugitive gangster Himanshu Bhau, who has been detained by the U.S. authorities and is currently in the custody of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), officials said on Saturday (October 24, 2026). Bhau, wanted in India in multiple murder and extortion cases, was initially detained for misrepresentation of facts after Haryana Police flagged that he had fled the country using a forged surname in his passport, they said. The Special Task Force (STF) of Haryana Police is in close coordination with the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's nodal agency for Interpol, to expedite his deportation from the United States, officials said. Bhau's criminal career began at the age of 17, when he allegedly attempted to murder an adversary. Although he was arrested, he escaped from a juvenile correctional facility in Hisar in 2020. Since then, he has been involved in a series of organised criminal activities, emerging as one of the most wanted criminals, they said. Investigators allege that Bhau initially fled India to Portugal using forged documents and has since operated his criminal syndicate from overseas. His gang maintains close ties with groups that are rivals of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. The gang came under the spotlight in September after claiming responsibility on social media for the daylight murder of gym trainer and owner Vijay Kumar in South Delhi's Aya Nagar area. Kumar was shot dead on September 14 after being lured outside, where two motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire. Police said Kumar was the third person killed in an ongoing local family rivalry. The gang was also linked to a high-profile shootout at a Burger King outlet in Rajouri Garden in 2024, in which a 26-year-old man was killed. Unlock these with Subscription The Tamil Nadu Health Department has initiated efforts to establish a telemedicine programme based on a hub-and-spoke model, with five super speciality hubs being planned. This was one of the announcements made in the Budget earlier this year by Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson. According to the announcement, to ensure access to specialised medical care for people in remote and rural areas, the government will establish a telemedicine system based on a hub-and-spoke hospital model. Five hubs staffed by specialist doctors will be linked to 200 spokes at primary health centres and government hospitals through an online network. Over the next five years, this network will be progressively expanded to a total of 1,000 hubs and spokes. The government allocated ₹18.5 crore to establish the telemedicine network. Last week, the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu, in a communication to the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) and Research, said that a proposal has been submitted to the government for the establishment of a State Hub-and-Spoke Telemedicine Programme in Tamil Nadu, with five super speciality hubs at Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital, Chennai; Government Omandurar Medical College Hospital, Chennai; Government Rajaji Hospital, Madurai Medical College, Madurai; Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital, K.A.P.V. Government Medical College, Tiruchi; and Coimbatore Medical College Hospital. It said that the space and infrastructure required for each hub was discussed during a meeting, and a type design was prepared for the super speciality hub. It went on to outline the salient features, the need for the identification of space, and the preparation of estimates through the Public Works Department (Buildings). The DME was requested to instruct the deans of the five medical college hospitals to identify existing built-up space of about 1,700 sq. ft. in the institution for their conversion into the telemedicine hub. 泰米尔纳德邦卫生部门已着手建立一套基于“中心—辐射”模式的远程医疗计划，计划设立5个超级专科中心。这是财政部长N. Marie Wilson在今年早些时候公布的预算案中宣布的举措之一。根据公布的安排，为确保偏远和农村地区民众能够获得专科医疗服务，政府将建立一套基于“中心—辐射”医院模式的远程医疗体系。5个配备专科医生的中心将通过在线网络与基层卫生中心和政府医院的200个辐射点相连。未来5年，这一网络将逐步扩展至总计1,000个中心和辐射点。政府拨款₹18.5 crore用于建立远程医疗网络。

上周，泰米尔纳德邦国家卫生使命局在发给医学教育与研究局（DME）的一份通知中表示，已向政府提交了在泰米尔纳德邦设立“邦级中心—辐射式远程医疗计划”的提案。该计划将在以下医院设立5个超级专科中心：金奈Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital；金奈Government Omandurar Medical College Hospital；马杜赖Government Rajaji Hospital、Madurai Medical College；蒂鲁吉Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital、K.A.P.V. Government Medical College；以及Coimbatore Medical College Hospital。

通知称，相关会议已讨论每个中心所需的场地和基础设施，并为超级专科中心制定了类型设计方案。通知还概述了主要事项、确定场地的必要性，以及通过公共工程部门（建筑物）编制估算的要求。DME获指示要求这5家医学院医院的院长，在各自机构内确定约1,700平方英尺的现有建成空间，用于改建远程医疗中心。计划设置8个问诊隔间和2个用于敏感问诊的私密隔间。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary: Yet when he turned his formidable historical lens on a subject that has long fascinated me, namely political Islam, I found his latest book, Boko Haram: The Past of the Present Upheaval , quite unputdownable. Too often, our understanding of the North is mediated by the fragments that break into national consciousness as headlines: Boko Haram’s insurgency, the scourge of banditry, the politics of Sharia, anxieties over political Islam, and the seemingly interminable cycle of religious tension and bloodshed.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary_zh: 然而，当他将其非凡的历史视角转向一个长期令我着迷的议题，即政治伊斯兰主义时，我发现他的最新著作《博科圣地：当下动荡的过去》令人爱不释手。我们对北方的理解往往受到那些以头条新闻形式闯入全国意识的碎片所影响：博科圣地的叛乱、匪徒活动的祸害、伊斯兰教法的政治、对政治伊斯兰主义的焦虑，以及宗教紧张与流血冲突 seemingly 无休止的循环。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body: Having read much of Mo’s work and listened to enough of his arguments, I sometimes feel I have reached that curious point at which eating, regurgitating, and eating again begin to resemble one continuous meal. Yet when he turned his formidable historical lens on a subject that has long fascinated me, namely political Islam, I found his latest book, Boko Haram: The Past of the Present Upheaval , quite unputdownable. I make this disclosure not to stake a claim to objectivity, but to establish the context in which I approach the work under review. Neither Moses nor Farooq has been a mentor to me in the conventional sense. Rather, they have been interlocutors and intellectual companions whose scholarship, arguments, and dissenting perspectives have enriched my thinking in ways that are difficult to quantify. As a Christian Southerner, I have long been struck by the ease with which those of us in the South presume to understand Northern Nigeria, while remaining only dimly acquainted with the historical currents, religious traditions, and intellectual ferment that have shaped its complex evolution. Too often, our understanding of the North is mediated by the fragments that break into national consciousness as headlines: Boko Haram’s insurgency, the scourge of banditry, the politics of Sharia, anxieties over political Islam, and the seemingly interminable cycle of religious tension and bloodshed. We encounter the North principally through the spectacle of its crises, while remaining largely estranged from the deeper histories, ideas, and traditions that have given the region its distinctive character. Within this narrow framing, we become familiar with the region’s wounds without fully understanding the history behind them. Societies cannot be understood solely through their tragedies. They must also be understood through the histories, ideas, institutions, religious traditions, and political struggles that precede those tragedies. This is where Ochonu’s book proves particularly valuable. Ostensibly a study of Boko Haram, the book derives its deeper significance from its insistence that the insurgency cannot be adequately understood as an isolated contemporary phenomenon. Boko Haram emerged from a historical landscape marked by Islamic reform, religious contestation, struggles over authority, political transformation, and competing interpretations of legitimate governance. Such historical depth is often missing from public discourse. Boko Haram has been variously explained through poverty, unemployment, political exclusion, corruption, state failure, climate pressures, religious extremism, and international jihadist networks. Each explanation illuminates part of the problem, but none, standing alone, is sufficient. Ochonu’s contribution is to situate these contemporary realities within a much longer historical continuum while resisting the temptation to treat historical antecedents as inevitable causes. That distinction is crucial. To explain is not to excuse. Understanding the intellectual and historical origins of violence does not diminish the culpability of those who murder civilians, abduct children, or terrorise communities. Condemnation is morally indispensable, but it cannot substitute for explanation. A society that understands only the symptoms of its crises will repeatedly find itself surprised by their recurrence. One of the most compelling dimensions of Ochonu’s analysis is his treatment of the political uses of history. Boko Haram has invoked Usman dan Fodio, the nineteenth-century Islamic reformer whose jihad profoundly altered the political and religious architecture of much of what is now Northern Nigeria. Such invocations matter because history is not merely a record of what happened. It can become a reservoir of legitimacy, identity, grievance, and political aspiration. But invocation does not establish inheritance. The fact that Boko Haram appeals to dan Fodio does not, by itself, establish a direct theological or ideological descent from him. Nor does the history of Islamic reform in Northern Nigeria lead inexorably to contemporary jihadism. The intellectual task is more exacting: to determine what connects these historical moments, what separates them, and how contemporary actors selectively appropriate the past to legitimise present ambitions. Here, the politics of history becomes inseparable from the history of politics. The past is not inert. It is remembered, interpreted, contested, reconstructed, and sometimes weaponised. Ochonu also helps preserve a distinction frequently lost in polemical discussions: religious reform is not synonymous with religious extremism. Similarities in language, symbolism, or doctrine may suggest intellectual affinities, but resemblance alone cannot establish causation or direct descent. This distinction is particularly important in understanding Boko Haram’s hostility toward Western education and aspects of modern political life. Movements that denounce modernity can simultaneously exploit its technologies, communications systems, organisational structures, and political mechanisms. The more illuminating question, therefore, is not simply what Boko Haram rejects, but what it selectively appropriates, how its ideology has evolved, and why particular ideas resonate under specific political and social conditions. This is precisely where history must engage with political economy, state conduct, local grievances, and international influences. Poverty does not automatically produce insurgency. Religious conviction does not inevitably lead to violence. Political exclusion does not mechanically generate radicalization. The challenge is to understand how these forces interact and the circumstances under which they become combustible. Ochonu does not pretend to settle every question, nor should he. A single volume cannot exhaust the theological, historical, political, economic, and sociological dimensions of an insurgency whose roots and consequences span generations and national boundaries. Questions will inevitably remain about the precise relationship between earlier religious traditions and contemporary militancy, the role of state violence and international jihadism, the nature of local grievances, and the experiences of communities caught between insurgents and security forces. But a book need not answer every question to change the quality of the questions we ask. That, ultimately, is Ochonu’s achievement. He restores historical depth to a conversation too often dominated by immediate security concerns. He reminds us that Boko Haram is not merely a security problem, but also an intellectual, historical, political, and cultural phenomenon. For me, however, the significance of the book extends beyond Boko Haram. As someone from southern Nigeria, I consider it a valuable resource for anyone who wishes to understand Northern Nigeria beyond stereotype and political caricature. More importantly, it complicates assumptions about a region too often encountered through the shorthand of violence, religion, and political crisis. It invites readers to engage with the religious traditions, intellectual struggles, political formations, and historical experiences that have shaped a region whose destiny remains inseparable from that of the rest of Nigeria. Ultimately, Boko Haram: The Past of the Present Upheaval reminds us that history is neither a mausoleum of dead events nor a deterministic script for the future. It is a contested inheritance from which contemporary actors draw symbols, identities, grievances, ideas, and claims to legitimacy. For a country perpetually confronted by the consequences of an insufficiently examined past, that is an important lesson. A nation does itself a profound disservice when it buries its history rather than confronts it. History does not disappear because a society chooses not to speak about it. It persists in fractured identities, unresolved grievances, political suspicions, and the enduring consequences of decisions made in the past. I know this not merely as an abstraction, but as a matter of personal experience. I am an Igbo man born during the Nigerian Civil War, a conflict that formally ended decades ago but whose consequences remain woven into the lives of people from my part of Nigeria. For many of us, the war is not a distant episode confined to textbooks and archives. Its effects remain visible in our families and communities, as does the enduring sense that an essential chapter of our national story remains incompletely told. This is one of the deeper lessons of Ochonu’s book. His willingness to excavate the historical foundations of Boko Haram demonstrates what becomes possible when we resist the temptation to treat history as an inconvenience. Nigeria needs that same intellectual courage in confronting its own unresolved past. A nation cannot fully understand its present, much less build a more honest and cohesive future, while suppressing the difficult chapters that helped shape it. We do not heal historical wounds by refusing to name them; we merely allow their consequences to persist. For anyone who wishes to understand Northern Nigeria, its culture, religious traditions, intellectual evolution, political formations, and historical encounters, Moses Ochonu’s book is an indispensable place to begin. Mo has been generous enough to make the book universally available. Read it. Engage with it. Allow it to complicate what you thought you already knew. Osmund Agbo is a medical doctor, author, and the 2026 recipient of the Thabo Mbeki Prize for Scholarship and Public Service

读过莫的大部分著作，也听过足够多的他的论点后，我有时会觉得自己已经到达了一个奇特的境界：进食、反刍，再度进食，开始像是一顿连绵不断的餐食。然而，当他把自己强大的历史视角投向一个长期令我着迷的主题，即政治伊斯兰主义时，我发现他的最新著作《博科哈拉姆：当下动荡的往昔》令人爱不释手。我这样说明，并不是要宣称自己持客观立场，而是要交代我评介这部作品所处的语境。无论莫西姆斯还是法鲁克，都不是传统意义上的我的导师。更确切地说，他们是与我对话的人和思想同行者；他们的研究、论辩和异议视角以难以量化，丰富了我的思考。作为一名来自南方的基督徒，我早就注意到，我们这些南方人很容易自以为了解尼日利亚北部，却对塑造该地区复杂演变历程的历史潮流、宗教传统和思想激荡其实所知甚浅。我们对北方的理解往往由那些作为头条闯入全国意识的碎片所中介：博科哈拉姆的叛乱、匪患的灾难、伊斯兰教法的政治、对政治伊斯兰主义的焦虑，以及宗教紧张与流血似乎永无止境的恶性循环。我们主要通过其危机的spectacle认识北方，却仍与那些赋予这一地区独特特征，更深层的历史、观念和传统大体疏离。在这种狭窄的框架中，我们熟悉了该地区的创伤，却未能充分理解其背后的历史。社会不能仅凭悲剧来理解。还必须通过悲剧之前的历史、观念、制度、宗教传统和政治斗争来理解它们。奥乔努的书正是在这一点上显得格外有价值。这本书表面上研究博科哈拉姆，但它更深的意义在于坚持认为：这场叛乱无法被充分理解为一种孤立的当代现象。博科哈拉姆出现于一片充满伊斯兰改革、宗教争辩、权力斗争、政治转型以及对合法治理的各种相互竞争性解读的历史图景之中。公共讨论往往缺少这种历史纵深。博科哈拉姆先后被归因于贫困、失业、政治排斥、腐败、国家失灵、气候压力、宗教极端主义和国际圣战网络。每一种解释都揭示了问题的一部分，但没有任何一种单独来看是充分的。奥乔努的贡献，在于把这些当代现实置于长得多的一段历史连续体中，同时避免把历史先例当作不可避免的起因。这种区分至关重要。解释不等于开脱。理解暴力的思想和历史起源，并不会减轻那些杀害平民、绑架儿童或恐吓社区之人的罪责。道德谴责不可或缺，但它不能取代解释。一个只理解自身危机症状的社会，会一再对危机再次出现感到意外。奥乔努分析中最引人注目的维度之一，是他探讨了历史的政治用途。博科哈拉姆援引了乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥，这位19世纪的伊斯兰改革者，其圣战深刻改变了如今尼日利亚北部大片地区的政治与宗教格局。此类援引之所以重要，是因为历史并非仅仅是已发生之事的记录。它可以成为合法性、认同、不满和政治抱负的储备库。然而，援引并不能证明继承关系。博科哈拉姆诉诸丹·福迪奥，这一事实本身并不能证明两者之间存在直接或神学、意识形态上的谱系联系。尼日利亚北部伊斯兰改革的历史，也不会不可避免地导向当代圣战主义。思想任务要求更高：必须确定这些历史时刻之间有何联系、有何区别，以及当代行动者如何有选择地挪用过去，以使当下的抱负获得正当性。在这里，历史的政治与政治的历史变得不可分割。过去并非惰性不变。它会被记忆、解释、争议、重构，有时还会被武器化。奥乔努还帮助保留了辩论中经常被混淆的一项区别：宗教改革并不等同于宗教极端主义。语言、象征或教义上的相似性可能提示思想上的亲缘关系，但仅凭相似之处无法确立因果关系或直接谱系。在理解博科哈拉姆对西方教育和现代政治生活某些方面的敌意时，这一区分尤为重要。谴责现代性的运动，同时也可以利用现代性的技术、通信系统、组织结构和政治机制。因此，更具启发性的问题不只是博科哈拉姆拒绝什么，而是它有选择地挪用了什么，其意识形态如何演变，以及为什么某些观念会在特定政治和社会条件下引起共鸣。历史正是在这里必须同政治经济学、国家行为、地方不满和国际影响展开对话。贫困不会自动催生叛乱。宗教信仰不会必然导致暴力。政治排斥不会机械地产生激进化。真正的挑战是理解这些力量如何相互作用，以及在何种情况下它们会变得易燃。奥乔努并未假装能够解决每一个问题，他也不应当如此。一卷书不可能穷尽一场叛乱的全部神学、历史、政治、经济和社会学维度；这场叛乱的根源和后果跨越数代人与国界。关于早期宗教传统与当代武装活动之间的确切关系、国家暴力和国际圣战主义所起的作用、地方不满的性质，以及夹在叛乱分子与安全部队之间的社区所经历的一切，问题无疑仍将存在。但一本书不必回答所有问题，也能改变我们提出问题的质量。归根结底，这正是奥乔努的成就。他把历史纵深还原给一场往往被眼前安全考虑主导的讨论。他提醒我们，博科哈拉姆不仅是一个安全问题，也是一种思想、历史、政治和文化现象。然而，对我而言，这本书的意义超出了博科哈拉姆本身。作为一名来自尼日利亚南部的人，我认为，对于任何希望超越刻板印象和政治漫画化认识尼日利亚北部的人而言，它都是一部宝贵的资源。更重要的是，它使人们对这个常常只通过暴力、宗教和政治危机等简略标签来认识的地区的种种假设变得更加复杂。它邀请读者深入接触那些塑造了一个地区的宗教传统、思想斗争、政治形态和历史经历，而这个地区的命运至今仍与尼日利亚其他地区密不可分Ultimately，《博科哈拉姆：当下动荡的往昔》提醒我们，历史既不是死寂事件的陵墓，也不是决定未来的宿命脚本。它是一份有争议的遗产，当代行动者从中汲取符号、身份、不满、观念和正当性主张。对一个永远面对过去遭充分审视所遗留后果的国家来说，这是一堂重要的课。一个国家若掩埋自己的历史，而不是正视它，就是在严重地伤害自身。社会不会因为选择不谈论历史，历史便消失。它会继续存在于支离破碎的身份中、未解决的不满中、政治猜疑中，以及过去所作决定的长久后果之中。我知道这一点，不只是把它当作抽象概念，而是作为切身体验。我是一名伊博人，出生于尼日利亚内战期间；这场冲突在数十年前正式结束，但其后果至今仍编织在来自我所在地区 peoples 的生活之中。对我们许多人来说，战争并非只存在于教科书和档案中的遥远往事。它在我们家庭和社区中留下的影响依然可见，那种认为国家叙事中一个关键章节仍未被完整讲述的 enduring 感觉也依然存在。这是奥乔努之书更深层的教训之一。他愿意发掘博科哈拉姆的历史基础，展示了当我们抵制把历史视为麻烦的诱惑时，能够实现什么。尼日利亚在面对自身尚未解决的过去时，也需要同样的思想勇气。一个国家若压制塑造自己的艰难篇章，就不可能充分理解自己的现在，更谈不上建设更诚实、更凝聚的未来。拒绝说出历史创伤，并不能疗愈它们；我们只是任其后果延续下去。对于任何希望了解尼日利亚北部、其文化、宗教传统、思想演变、政治形态和历史际遇的人而言，莫西姆斯·奥乔努的书都是不可或缺的起点。莫已慷慨地让这本书向所有人开放。请读它。与它对话。让它使你以为自己早已了解的事情变得复杂。奥斯蒙德·阿博是一名医学博士、作家，也是2026年塔博·姆贝基学术与公共服务奖得主

https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.summary: Teodoro was responding to a report by a Manila-based Chinese language newspaper that China was considering removing the warship from Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal as one of 10 possible “countermeasures” against the Philippines following increasingly strained bilateral ties over the maritime conflict between the two countries.
https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.summary_zh: 特奥多罗是在回应马尼拉一家中文报纸的报道。该报称，在两国围绕海上冲突的双边关系日益紧张之际，中国正考虑将军舰撤出阿永金（第二托马斯）浅滩，作为针对菲律宾的10项可能“反制措施”之一。
https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.body: Teodoro was responding to a report by a Manila-based Chinese language newspaper that China was considering removing the warship from Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal as one of 10 possible “countermeasures” against the Philippines following increasingly strained bilateral ties over the maritime conflict between the two countries. “Any threat against BRP Sierra Madre will be taken very seriously because it will be an act against a military vessel of the Republic of the Philippines,” Teodoro said in an online interview with reporters. READ: Teodoro: China’s attempt to tow BRP Sierra Madre by force an act of war The ship, now rusted and decrepit, was intentionally run aground at Ayungin to serve as a military outpost in the West Philippine Sea in 1999, four years after China occupied Panganiban (Mischief) Reef, which, like Ayungin, is within the exclusive economic zone of the Philippines. Another reported countermeasure was to halt the resupply of the troops on the Sierra Madre, who rely on fuel, food, water, medicines and other resources delivered by sea. It added that if the Philippines “forcibly breaks through Chinese blockades, China will take strong measures to block them.” The 10 measures were outlined in a report on Friday by the Chinese Commercial News, which noted that there was no official confirmation that these “potential options” were being considered or had been approved by Beijing. It quoted “well-informed sources” saying that the “Chinese side” was “gradually losing patience with recent Philippine actions and related statements concerning China,” a reference to strident exchanges between Philippine officials and Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan and his embassy related to the maritime dispute between the two countries. The possible countermeasures include banning “anti-China” Filipino politicians and their immediate families from entering any Chinese territory, freezing their assets in China and prohibiting Chinese entities from conducting business with them; and publicly disclosing their commercial and financial dealings with China. The others are restricting Chinese citizens from traveling to the Philippines; tightening labor policies on Filipino workers in Hong Kong and Macao; arresting more Filipinos illegally working in China; closing certain consulates in China, including in Hong Kong, if Manila approves the establishment of an additional Taiwan office in Cebu. The proposed economic sanctions include cutting off fuel and fertilizer supply and restricting exports of urgently needed and essential goods to the Philippines. “It’s not a state of war … but an act of war because it is an offensive act against a Philippine warship,” he said. Only the President and Congress could declare a state of war, he said. Under the Constitution, Congress has the power to declare the existence of a state of war by a two-thirds vote of both houses in joint session, voting separately. Asked whether an attempt by China to board the Sierra Madre could trigger the Philippines’ Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) with the United States, Teodoro said the possibility remained open, although the decision would ultimately rest with President Marcos. He emphasized that such an incident could, rather than necessarily would, lead to the invocation of the 1951 treaty, which commits the Philippines and the United States to act in accordance with their respective constitutional processes to respond to an armed attack against either party in the Pacific. Several US officials, including secretaries of state and defense, and American diplomats have said that Washington would stand by its “ironclad” commitments under the treaty. Washington has affirmed that the treaty covers armed attacks against Philippine armed forces, public vessels and aircraft, including those of the Philippine Coast Guard, anywhere in the South China Sea. Asked to comment on the two proposed economic sanctions, Teodoro said the country’s dependence on China could be used against it. “It just goes to show you that whatever supposed goodwill that they are doing is a weapon and they are weaponizing it,” he said. Teodoro urged the government and private sector to strengthen domestic industries and diversify supply chains, particularly for critical infrastructure. “We cannot place complete trust in a country that claims our territory,” he said. Teodoro said the Philippines needed to reduce its dependence on Chinese products and suppliers, warning that economic relationships could be used as leverage during disputes over sovereignty and territorial rights. The defense chief also urged companies to diversify their sources of raw materials and finished products instead of relying heavily on a single country. “We are constantly being threatened subtly and now more overtly,” he said. Amid the continuing tensions, Teodoro renewed his call to overhaul the country’s military modernization law, warning that the existing framework was hampering efforts to secure sufficient funding for the Armed Forces of the Philippines. The defense establishment had been “stuck” to receiving the relatively small P50 billion allocation for military upgrades because of the modernization law, Teodoro said. He said the current spending system was “restrictive and no longer suited to present realities.” Teodoro called for a stronger domestic defense industry, saying the Philippines needed to develop basic industries that could support the local production of military equipment, citing South Korea and India as examples. The recent angry exchanges between Filipino officials and Chinese diplomats followed Jing’s remarks on Oct. 15. He was responding to reporters’ questions about a statement by Teodoro who said that China was the “lone troublemaker” in Southeast Asia. Jing said this was “nonsense” as the region was peaceful and that it was fortunate to have a neighbor like China. Jing added, however, that China “may easily win” against the Philippines but chose not to use force because it was peace-loving. The President regarded what he said as a threat and an undiplomatic statement. On Monday, Foreign Secretary Teresa Lazaro summoned Jing to protest against his remarks. Some Philippine lawmakers saw Jing’s remarks as a threat and several sought to declare him as persona non grata and to have him expelled. The Chinese embassy retaliated in a series of social media posts, saying that Filipino politicians with personal political ambitions were undermining Philippine-China relations. https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.title_zh: 吉博·特奥多罗：若中国试图拖走Sierra Madre，就等于“宣战”
https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.body_zh: Teodoro是在回应马尼拉一家中文报纸的报道。该报称，在两国围绕海上冲突的双边关系日益紧张之际，中国正考虑将军舰撤出Ayungin（Second Thomas）浅滩，并将其列为针对菲律宾的10项可能“反制措施”之一。Teodoro在线接受记者采访时说：“任何针对BRP Sierra Madre的威胁都会受到极为严肃的对待，因为这将构成针对菲律宾共和国军舰的行为。”阅读：Teodoro：中国试图强行拖走BRP Sierra Madre属于战争行为。这艘如今已经锈蚀破败的军舰于1999年被故意搁浅在Ayungin，作为菲律宾西海的一个军事前哨。那是在中国占领Panganiban（Mischief）礁4年后；Panganiban与Ayungin一样，均位于菲律宾专属经济区内。另一项被报道的反制措施是停止向Sierra Madre上的部队补给。这些部队依赖海运获得燃料、食物、饮用水、药品和其他物资。报道还称，如果菲律宾“强行突破中国的封锁，中国将采取有力措施予以阻止”。这10项措施是中国商业新闻周五发布的一份报告所列。报告指出，没有官方消息证实这些“潜在选项”正在考虑之中或已获北京批准。报告援引“消息灵通人士”的话说，中方“正逐渐失去对菲律宾近期涉华行动及相关言论的耐心”，这是指菲律宾官员与中国大使景泉及其使馆就两国海上争端进行的激烈交锋。可能采取的反制措施包括：禁止“反华”的菲律宾政治人物及其直系亲属进入任何中国领土，冻结他们在中国的资产，禁止中国实体与其开展业务，并公开披露他们与中国的商业和金融往来。其他措施包括限制中国公民赴菲律宾旅行；收紧针对在香港和澳门工作的菲律宾人的劳工政策；逮捕更多在中国非法工作的菲律宾人；如果马尼拉批准在宿务增设台湾办事处，就关闭中国境内的某些领事馆，包括香港的领事馆。建议实施的经济制裁包括切断对菲律宾的燃料和化肥供应，并限制向菲律宾出口急需品和基本物资。他说：“这不是战争状态……但属于战争行为，因为这是针对菲律宾军舰的进攻性行为。”他说，只有总统和国会才能宣布进入战争状态。根据《宪法》，国会可在两院联席会议中分别表决，以三分之二多数决定是否进入战争状态。被问及中国试图登上Sierra Madre是否会触发菲律宾与美国签订的《共同防御条约》（MDT）时，Teodoro表示这种可能性仍然存在，尽管最终决定权将掌握在Marcos总统手中。他强调，此类事件可能、但不一定必然导致援引1951年条约。该条约承诺，菲律宾和美国将依照各自宪法程序，共同应对任何一方在太平洋地区遭受的武装攻击。包括国务卿、国防部长在内的多名美国官员以及美国外交官都表示，华盛顿将恪守条约规定的“铁定”承诺。华盛顿确认，该条约涵盖针对菲律宾武装部队、公共船舶和飞机的武装攻击，包括菲律宾海岸警卫队任何位于南海的船舶和飞机。被要求评论拟议中的两项经济制裁时，Teodoro说，该国对中国的依赖可能被用来对付菲律宾。他说：“这恰恰说明，无论他们所谓的善意是什么，那都是一种武器，而且他们正把这种善意武器化。”Teodoro敦促政府和私营部门加强国内产业并推动供应链多元化，尤其是关键基础设施领域。他说：“我们不能完全信任一个声称觊觎我们领土的国家。”Teodoro表示，菲律宾需要减少对中国产品和供应商的依赖，并警告称，在主权和领土权利争端中，经济关系可能被用作施压杠杆。这名国防部长还敦促企业多元化采购原材料和制成品的来源，而不是严重依赖单一国家。他说：“我们不断受到隐性威胁，如今还面临更加公开的威胁。”在紧张局势持续之际，Teodoro再次呼吁全面改革该国的军事现代化法，并警告称，现有框架妨碍了为菲律宾武装部队争取充足资金。Teodoro说，受现代化法限制，国防体系一直“受困于”只能获得相对较小的500亿比索军备升级拨款。他说，现行支出制度“限制性太强，已不再符合当前现实”。Teodoro呼吁建立更强大的国内国防工业，称菲律宾需要发展能够支持本地生产军事装备的基础工业，并列举韩国和印度为例。菲律宾官员与中国外交官近期激烈交锋，源于景泉10月15日发表的言论。当时记者就Teodoro关于中国是东南亚“唯一麻烦制造者”的说法向他提问。景泉称这种说法“荒谬”，因为该地区是和平的，而能有中国这样的邻国是幸运的。不过，景泉补充说，中国“很容易战胜”菲律宾，但选择不使用武力，因为中国热爱和平。总统认为他的言论是一种威胁，也是不符合外交礼节的言论。周一，外交部长Teresa Lazaro召见景泉，就其言论提出抗议。一些菲律宾议员将景泉的言论视为威胁，数名议员试图宣布其为不受欢迎人物并将其驱逐。中国使馆在一系列社交媒体帖子中反击称，怀有个人政治野心的菲律宾政治人物正在破坏菲中关系。无法保存您的订阅。请重试。您的订阅已成功。该使馆向议员发出挑战，要求他们“停止虚张声势”，宣布景泉为不受欢迎人物。中国使馆说：“就这么做。”INQ https://leadership.ng/msmes-analysts-say.summary_zh: 尼日利亚小微企业主协会（ASBON）主席Femi Egbesola博士表示，降息尚未转化为中小微型企业（MSMEs）能够负担且便捷获得的信贷。他说：“许多中小微企业的现实情况是，尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）的降息尚未转化为价格可负担、获取便捷的信贷。
https://leadership.ng/msmes-analysts-say.body: The president of the Association of Small Business Owners of Nigeria (ASBON), Dr. Femi Egbesola, said the rate cut had not yet translated into affordable and accessible credit for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). He described the fall in private sector credit as a worrying signal. “The reality for many MSMEs is that the CBN’s rate cut has not yet translated into affordable, accessible credit. This is a worrying signal, although the aggregate figures alone do not explain why lending declined,” he said. He said small businesses still face high borrowing costs, stringent collateral requirements and short repayment periods that make bank loans inaccessible. “For small businesses, high borrowing costs, stringent collateral requirements and short repayment periods remain major barriers. Banks must also consider credit risks, but viable businesses should not be excluded simply because they lack landed property or other conventional collateral,” he said. According to him, the credit squeeze is crippling MSMEs’ ability to operate and expand. “The credit squeeze means businesses struggle to purchase raw materials, maintain production, invest in equipment and employ more workers,” Egbesola noted. He said fintechs are filling the gap with quick loans, but their model is not suitable for long-term industrial growth. “Fintech loans offer speed and convenience, but their short tenures and potentially high costs may not be suitable for financing factories or long-term expansion,” he said. Egbesola urged the CBN to go beyond rate cuts and adopt structural measures. “I urge the CBN to strengthen credit-guarantee schemes, expand cash-flow-based lending and movable-asset financing, and introduce measurable targets and incentives for bank lending to viable MSMEs,” he said. He also called for transparency in bank lending to small businesses. “Banks should be required to report transparently on their MSME lending performance, with appropriate regulatory consequences for persistent non-compliance. The objective is not to compel reckless lending, but to make productive businesses bankable and ensure that monetary easing translates into investment, jobs and economic growth,” Egbesola added. The chief operating officer of InvestData Consulting Limited, Mr. Ambrose Omordion, said banks appear not to be aligned with the CBN’s strategy of making funds cheaper to boost Gross Domestic Product. “Anywhere in the world, banks are the engine of any economy. Nigerian banks are sitting on liquid funds that should be lent to the public, but they are yet to understand how to do that lending because they have not been doing enough lending as before,” Omordion said. He said fintech banks have taken over the retail lending space, offering quick loans without demanding high collateral, a model traditional banks are struggling to replicate. Omordion said many deposit money banks prefer investing in risk-free treasury bills and remain cautious because of past experience with high non-performing loans, especially from exposure to the oil and gas and telecommunications sectors. “The CBN cut rates to boost the economy and push banks to lend to the real sector, but banks are dragging their feet in implementing the rate cut. The CBN has the hammer and can sanction any bank that defaults,” he said. He said increased lending would drive GDP growth, as no government can drive growth alone without the private sector. “Banks have the money and can drive new sectors. We want lending to expand so that industries and enterprises can produce more when they have access to cheaper funds,” he said. Omordion added that the entry of foreign banks, such as J.P. Morgan setting up a merchant bank in Nigeria, shows the potential in the economy and should push local banks to develop better lending strategies. Data from the CBN show that private sector credit dropped to N83.93 trillion in September from N84.47 trillion in August, a decline of 0.64 per cent. The figure is still about 15.7 per cent higher than the N72.53 trillion recorded a year earlier. The decline followed the decision of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in September to cut the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) by 350 basis points to 23 per cent, the largest reduction in the benchmark rate since December 2006. The MPC retained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for commercial banks at 45 per cent. The CBN data do not explain whether the fall reflects weaker loan demand, tighter lending conditions, repayments or other factors. A lower benchmark rate can also take time to filter through, as actual lending depends on banks’ funding costs, risk assessments and borrowers’ ability to repay. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/msmes-analysts-say.body_zh: 尼日利亚小企业主协会（ASBON）主席费米·埃格贝索拉博士表示，降息尚未转化为微型企业、小型和中型企业（MSME）负担得起且易于获得的信贷。他形容私营部门信贷下降是一个令人担忧的信号。埃格贝索拉说：“对许多微型企业、小型和中型企业而言，现实情况是，尼日利亚中央银行降息尚未转化为负担得起、容易获得的信贷。这是一个令人担忧的信号，尽管仅凭汇总数据无法解释贷款为何减少。”他说，小企业仍面临高借贷成本、严格抵押品要求和短期还款期限等问题，使银行贷款难以获得。埃格贝索拉说：“对小企业而言，高借贷成本、严格抵押品要求和短期还款期限仍是主要障碍。银行也必须考虑信贷风险，但 viable 企业不应仅仅因为没有房地产或其他传统抵押品就被排除在外。”据他称，信贷紧缩正严重削弱微型企业、小型和中型企业的运营和扩张能力。埃格贝索拉指出：“信贷紧缩意味着企业难以购买原材料、维持生产、投资设备以及雇用更多员工。”他说，金融科技公司正通过快速贷款填补这一缺口，但这种模式不适合长期工业增长。埃格贝索拉说：“金融科技贷款具有速度和便利性，但其期限短且成本可能较高，未必适合为工厂建设或长期扩张提供融资。”埃格贝索拉敦促尼日利亚中央银行超越降息措施，采取结构性措施。他说：“我敦促尼日利亚中央银行加强信贷担保计划，扩大基于现金流的贷款和动产融资，并为银行向 viable 微型企业、小型和中型企业发放贷款设定可衡量的目标和激励措施。”他还呼吁提高银行向小企业放贷的透明度。埃格贝索拉补充说：“应要求银行透明报告其向微型企业、小型和中型企业放贷的表现，并对持续不遵守规定的行为采取适当的监管措施。目标不是迫使银行进行鲁莽放贷，而是让富有成效的企业能够获得银行融资，并确保货币宽松转化为投资、就业和经济增长。”InvestData Consulting Limited首席运营官安布罗斯·奥莫尔迪恩先生表示，银行似乎尚未与尼日利亚中央银行降低资金成本、推动国内生产总值增长的战略保持一致。奥莫尔迪恩说：“在世界上任何地方，银行都是经济的引擎。尼日利亚银行手中握有本应贷给公众的流动资金，但它们仍未学会如何开展这类放贷，因为此前没有充分开展放贷业务。”他说，金融科技银行已经占据零售贷款市场，在不要求高额抵押品的情况下提供快速贷款，而传统银行难以复制这种模式。奥莫尔迪恩表示，许多存款货币银行更愿意投资于无风险的国库券，并且因过去高不良贷款经历而保持谨慎，尤其是涉及石油、天然气和电信行业的贷款。“尼日利亚中央银行降息是为了提振经济，并推动银行向实体经济放贷，但银行在落实降息方面行动迟缓。尼日利亚中央银行握有重拳，可以制裁任何违规银行。”他说，增加放贷将推动国内生产总值增长，因为没有私营部门参与，任何政府都无法独自推动增长。奥莫尔迪恩说：“银行拥有资金，可以推动新兴产业发展。我们希望扩大放贷，使各行业和企业在获得更低成本资金后能够扩大生产。”奥莫尔迪恩补充说，J.P. Morgan等外国银行进入尼日利亚并设立商人银行， shows 了该经济体的潜力，也应促使本地银行制定更好的放贷策略。尼日利亚中央银行数据显示，私营部门信贷从8月的84.47万亿奈拉降至9月的83.93万亿奈拉，降幅为0.64%。这一数字仍比一年前记录的72.53万亿奈拉高约15.7%。此次下降发生在货币政策委员会（MPC）于9月决定将货币政策利率（MPR）下调350个基点至23%之后，这是自2006年12月以来基准利率的最大幅度下调。货币政策委员会将商业银行的现金准备金率（CRR）维持在45%。尼日利亚中央银行的数据未能说明，信贷下降究竟反映了贷款需求减弱、放贷条件收紧、还款增加还是其他因素。较低的基准利率也可能需要时间才能逐步传导，因为实际放贷取决于银行的资金成本、风险评估以及借款人的偿还能力。我们掌握独家优势。获取实时报道、最新消息和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp频道，随时随地获取全天候更新 → 加入我们的WhatsApp频道 --> --> 奥卢绍拉·贝洛 奥卢绍拉·贝洛是《Leadership Newspaper》高级记者，报道尼日利亚资本市场、产业部门及更广泛的经济问题。她以影响力强的报道、对商业发展和金融市场的深入分析而闻名，其工作以严谨的编辑判断以及对准确和公平的承诺为基础

https://www.thehindu.com/news/internatio.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Ukraine's top negotiator involved in a humanitarian mission led by U.S. first lady Melania Trump told The Associated Press that a local ceasefire with Russia will start Tuesday (October 27, 2026) — two days before the mission begins — and last several days. Ukrainian, Russian and U.S. negotiators reached a deal on Friday (October 23, 2026) to provide humanitarian assistance in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, in the war-divided region of Kherson in southern Ukraine. Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian ombudsman and his country's chief negotiator in the talks, said the ceasefire would take effect across the Kherson region and neighbouring areas essential to the operation. He added that the initiative could act as a model for future humanitarian missions. The White House said Melania Trump had initiated discussions after learning about the situation during an event she hosted during last month's UN General Assembly session. It said she and a representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the ceasefire. Russian officials also confirmed the arrangement. Mr. Lubinets earlier on Friday (October 23, 2026) thanked Melania Trump for her involvement and said the deal would be tough to accomplish. He said the agreement calls for a ceasefire, followed by the delivery of much-needed humanitarian aid. Lastly, civilians will be allowed to leave Oleshky, he said in a video message posted online. "The operation will be carried out gradually and is extremely challenging to implement," Mr. Lubinets said. Mr. Lubinets said the operation would involve removing mines on the way to Oleshky before the physical delivery of humanitarian aid and the arranging of evacuations. He gave no further details on how the ceasefire or the aid mission would be monitored or implemented, citing the sensitivity of the negotiations. He declined to comment when asked if Melania Trump would travel to Ukraine but described her involvement as invaluable. "When Melania Trump learned about the situation in Oleshky, the negotiation process began under her coordination," he said. "For several weeks, we discussed many questions, initiatives and ideas. We established new approaches, mechanisms and tools to do everything possible to help civilians in Oleshky survive." Russia's chief of the general staff, Gen. Valery Gerasimov, said Russian forces "will cease fire on the Kherson axis" starting at 4 am on Tuesday in Moscow "in connection with the humanitarian operation near Oleshky". Russian forces will also carry out "engineering reconnaissance" and ensure "safe movement of the humanitarian convoy" into the city, Mr. Gerasimov said. Russia's human rights ombudswoman, Yana Lantratova, confirmed on Friday (October 23, 2026) that Melania Trump had brokered an agreement on "organising a humanitarian mission" in Oleshky. Lantratova, who said she participated in negotiations, said providing such assistance is Russia's priority. The first step will be to clarify what people need and organise the delivery of food, medicine, hygiene products and other essentials, Lantratova said in an online statement. Safe passage will be guaranteed for anyone who wants to leave the combat zone, she said, adding that it will require abiding by the ceasefire and creating safe conditions for humanitarian vehicles. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was grateful to the First Lady. He said Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump had recently discussed the effort. Mr. Peskov said "those who want to leave it would be able to do so". He would not say whether they would be taken to Russia- or Ukraine-held territory. He also demurred when asked how long the evacuation will last, saying only it would most likely take several days. Ms. Melania Trump has made helping children in conflict zones one of her signature issues in her husband's second term. She hosted a UN Security Council meeting on the issue earlier this year, and last year wrote Putin about efforts to reunite families with children who have been displaced by the war. She has helped reunite nearly three dozen children, according to her senior adviser, Marc Beckman. "What she wants to do is save children, and that is her focus," the President said about his wife during a question-and-answer exchange with journalists at the White House. Mr. Beckman portrayed the First Lady's work on the ceasefire as an extension of her efforts to help reunite Russian and Ukrainian children with their families after they were separated by Russia's war against Ukraine. The development comes as tensions have increased to new highs between the Trump administration and Ukraine's government. Kyiv has faced restrictions on the satellite internet system it relies on to knock down Russian attacks, with Mr. Trump and other top U.S. officials sending mixed messages about who was responsible for throttling the Elon Musk-made Starshield system. Mr. Trump also recently waived new Russia sanctions, reached an agreement with Russia to import diesel fuel and pushed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to make a deal to end the war that Russia began in February 2022. In renewed efforts to revive the peace process, Mr. Trump Envoy Steve Witkoff travelled to Norway this week for talks with Mr. Zelenskyy before meeting Mr. Putin in St Petersburg, Russia . Mr. Zelenskyy did not mention the ceasefire in Oleshky during a remote appearance at the Hudson Institute, a Washington think tank. He did note that American Patriot missile interceptors were still on hold and Starshield and Starlink speed limits were still in place. He also spoke of the importance of the United States to renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war, including a possible joint meeting with Trump and Putin. Food and medical supplies have been scarce for months in Oleshky, which sits on the Dnipro river that separates Ukrainian forces from the city's Russian occupiers. There is no electricity, heat or running water. Roads leading from town are mined and dotted with burned-out cars. Drones buzz overhead. Once a city of about 24,000 residents, Oleshky was captured by Moscow's forces on the first day of their full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its buildings were shelled and burned, and its infrastructure damaged. In June 2023, floodwaters inundated the city after the Kakhovka dam collapsed from an explosion that an Associated Press investigation found was likely caused by the Russian military. Hundreds of residents were killed. Those left in the city along Ukraine's southeastern front face death from hunger or disease as another harsh winter looms. Ukraine has appealed repeatedly for a local ceasefire to organise evacuations. https://www.thehindu.com/news/internatio.title_zh: 谈判代表称，与俄罗斯达成的当地人道主义停火将于10月27日启动
https://www.thehindu.com/news/internatio.body_zh: 除了 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinies 等内容外，还可享受订阅优惠。订阅即可解锁这些内容。乌克兰首席谈判代表参与由美国总统夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普主导的人道主义任务。美联社援引他的话称，当地与俄罗斯的停火将于周二（2026年10月27日）开始，比任务启动早两天，并将持续数日。乌克兰、俄罗斯和美国谈判代表于周五（2026年10月23日）达成协议，将向乌克兰南部战火分割的赫尔松州、被俄军占领的奥列什基市提供人道主义援助。乌克兰调解员兼该国首席谈判代表德米特罗·卢比涅茨表示，停火将在赫尔松州及行动所必需的邻近地区生效。他补充说，这一举措可能成为未来人道主义任务的范例。白宫表示，梅拉尼娅·特朗普在上个月联合国大会会议期间举办的一场活动中了解有关情况后，启动了相关讨论。白宫说，她与一名代表直接同俄罗斯和乌克兰领导层协作，确定停火条款。俄罗斯官员也证实了这一安排。卢比涅茨先生周五（2026年10月23日）早些时候感谢梅拉尼娅·特朗普参与此事，并表示达成协议并不容易。他说，协议要求先实现停火，随后运送亟需的人道主义援助。最后，他在一段发布于网上的视频信息中说，平民将获准离开奥列什基。卢比涅茨先生说：“行动将逐步实施，执行难度极大。”卢比涅茨先生说，在实际运送人道主义援助和安排撤离之前，行动将包括清除通往奥列什基沿途的地雷。他没有进一步说明停火或援助任务将如何监督和落实，理由是谈判内容敏感。被问及梅拉尼娅·特朗普是否会赴乌克兰时，他拒绝置评，但称她的参与不可或缺。他说：“梅拉尼娅·特朗普了解奥列什基的情况后，谈判进程便在她的协调下展开。几周来，我们讨论了许多问题、举措和想法。我们建立了新的方式、机制和工具，将尽一切可能帮助奥列什基的平民生存下去。”俄罗斯武装力量总参谋长瓦列里·格拉西莫夫将军表示，为配合奥列什基附近的人道主义行动，俄军将从莫斯科时间周二凌晨4时起“在赫尔松轴线上停火”。格拉西莫夫先生说，俄军还将开展“工程侦察”，确保人道主义车队“安全进入”该市。俄罗斯人权事务专员叶娜·兰特拉托娃周五（2026年10月23日）证实，梅拉尼娅·特朗普促成了一项关于“在奥列什基组织人道主义任务”的协议。兰特拉托娃表示，她参与了谈判，并称提供此类援助是俄罗斯的优先事项。她在一份在线声明中说，第一步是明确民众的需求，并组织运送食品、药品、卫生用品和其他基本物资。她说，任何希望离开战区的人都将获得安全通行，但要做到这一点，必须遵守停火规定，并为 Humanitarian 车辆创造安全条件。克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫表示，莫斯科感谢美国第一夫人。他说，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和唐纳德·特朗普总统最近讨论了这项努力。佩斯科夫先生说，“任何希望离开的人都能做到”。他不肯透露这些人将被送往俄罗斯控制区还是乌克兰控制区。当被问及撤离将持续多久时，他也未予正面回答，只表示最可能需要数日。梅拉尼娅·特朗普已把帮助冲突地区的儿童列为丈夫第二任期内的标志性工作重点之一。今年早些时候，她主持了一场讨论这一议题的联合国安理会会议；去年，她曾致信普京，讲述为因战争而失散的家庭与儿童团聚所作的努力。据她的高级顾问马克·贝克曼说，她已帮助近30名儿童与家人团聚。特朗普总统在白宫与记者问答时谈到妻子时说：“她想做的就是拯救儿童，这就是她关注的重点。”贝克曼先生称，第一夫人为促成此次停火所做的工作，延续了她帮助俄罗斯和乌克兰失散儿童与家人团聚的努力。这一进展之际，特朗普政府与乌克兰政府之间的紧张关系已升至新高。基辅依赖卫星互联网系统击退俄军攻击，但该系统受到限制；特朗普先生和其他美国高层官员对究竟是谁限制马斯克旗下 Starshield 系统的运行发出了矛盾的信息。特朗普先生最近还取消了新一轮对俄制裁，与俄罗斯达成进口柴油的协议，并敦促乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基达成结束战争的协议；这场战争由俄罗斯于2022年2月发动。为重启和平进程，特朗普特使史蒂夫·维特科夫本周前往挪威，与泽连斯基先生会谈，随后将在俄罗斯圣彼得堡会见普京先生。泽连斯基先生出席华盛顿智库 Hudson Institute 的远程活动时，没有提及奥列什基停火。他确实指出，美国 Patriot 导弹拦截系统仍处于搁置状态，Starshield 和 Starlink 的限速措施仍然有效。他还谈到美国对重启结束战争的努力至关重要，包括可能举行特朗普与普京的联合会晤。数月来，奥列什基的食品和医疗物资一直短缺。这座城市位于第聂伯河畔，该河将乌克兰军队与占据这座城市的俄军分隔开来。城内没有电、暖气和自来水。通往该市的道路布满地雷，分布着烧毁的汽车。无人机在头顶盘旋。这座曾有约2.4万居民的城市，在俄罗斯于2022年2月全面入侵乌克兰的第一天被莫斯科军队攻占。市内建筑遭炮击和焚烧，基础设施遭到破坏。2023年6月，卡霍夫卡大坝因爆炸坍塌，洪水淹没该市。美联社调查发现，这次爆炸很可能由俄军造成，数百名居民丧生。随着又一个严酷冬季逼近，仍留在乌克兰东南前线这座城市里的民众面临死于饥饿或疾病的危险。乌克兰多次呼吁实行当地停火，以便组织撤离。作为占领国，俄罗斯有义务依据国际法确保其控制下的平民获得生存所需的一切。评论必须使用英文，并且必须是完整句子。评论不得包含辱骂性或针对个人的言论。发布评论时请遵守我们的社区准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已是 https://www.thehindu.com/food/dining/tan.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription The Tangra special chilli chicken at Chao aka Tangra Chinese Eating Room, Panampilly Nagar, has a problem. That first bite is unsettling; it comes with the realisation that chilli chicken will never be the same. The juicy bite-sized pieces of chicken have a hint of mild smokiness, making it different from most Indo-Chinese versions, which usually get their flavour from a medley of sauces. Almost everything on the menu is either new to the city or is different from what we expect. Chao is Vijay Antony Felix’s ode to the Chinese food he grew up eating in Kolkata: “I grew up eating this food, and I wanted to bring it to Kochi. I wanted people to experience it!” Kolkata is known for its unique Tangra-style Chinese food, popularised by members of the Chinese community, who made the city their home for more than a couple of centuries. Tangra is one of Kolkata’s Chinatowns, with its concentration of the Chinese population, immigrants who came to work at tanneries. Though very few people of Chinese heritage remain, especially in the food business, Tangra Chinese has its committed fans like Vijay, who want to introduce it to other cities. An engineer by profession, Vijay says he is an entrepreneur with a passion for food and beverages, and that commitment shows in how he has put Chao together. Located on the main avenue in Panampilly Nagar, Chao is bustling at lunchtime. The walls of this compact space wear the ubiquitous Chinese-restaurant red, adding to the distinct Chinese-y vibe. The building’s white facade has a red, fine-line dragon painted on it. One of the meanings of chao, in Chinese, is stir-fry or sauté. The seating might seem too close for some, but it works because it adds a warm sense of community, made comforting by the buzz of conversation that hangs in the air. Though it has been barely more than two months, Vijay confesses, the response far exceeds his expectations, especially because it is not the regular Chinese food that one is used to. And he is not complaining. We dive straight into the food with the clear wonton soup. It is light and flavourful, and its simplicity easily qualifies as comfort food. Next come the starters — first up is Hakka paneer, slim squares of lightly toasted/fried paneer tossed with coriander and thinly sliced chilli. The chilli and coriander combination cannot disappoint the desi palate. Then there is honey crispy chilli beef, strips of beef — spicy with a hint of sweetness in parts. Although a starter, it works well with the very pale-looking Cantonese noodles, which looks bland. But if you are one of those people who like to taste your veggies in your noodles, this is for you. You don’t expect coriander and green chilli in Chinese food, but they feature in Tangra-style cooking. But it is the Indian influence on the cuisine that incorporates elements of local cooking. For paneer sceptics, this will be a new experience, especially the bite of the green chillies. “Rather than overdo the sauces, we use a lot of chillies for the spice,” Vijay says. Another popular dish is the string beans with minced pork. A word on the beverages served, apart from other aerated drinks. There is kombucha, and then there is the malted bevvie, which is non-alcoholic, and is a must-try. It is quiet like beer. As we scoop the burnt garlic fried rice, with a surfeit of fried garlic, and Tangra kungpao chicken onto our plates, Vijay tells us about the ‘Chinese’ Kali temple of Tangra, pointing to a photograph on the wall behind, and how Chinese vegetarian dishes are offered as bhog. Mounted alongside on the wall is a bottle of Pou Chong sauce made locally in Tangra. The kitchen staff is from Kolkata, and the menu is the result of Vijay’s research, which involved visiting Chinese restaurants in Kolkata. That said, he confesses the recipes are inspired by some of the fare. The menu is rather expansive; vegetarians have been given due consideration, apart from a considerable seafood section. The spread was filling, and dessert impossible. But the offerings are tempting — darsaan (honey noodles) with vanilla ice cream, whisky chocolate tart with vanilla ice cream, and ice cream bars. The darsaan and ice cream will have to wait for another day. Although a couple of months old, it might be prudent to get reservations before walking in. A disclaimer: If you go in expecting familiar fare, you are in for a surprise. The Tangra style is distinct and different, though most Indian-Chinese fare originated there. https://www.thehindu.com/food/dining/tan.title_zh: 在科钦品尝加尔各答唐拉风味中餐
https://www.thehindu.com/food/dining/tan.body_zh: 除 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等内容外，还可享受账号订阅权益。订阅即可解锁这些内容。位于 Panampilly Nagar 主干道上的 Chao（又称 Tangra Chinese Eating Room），其招牌唐拉辣子鸡有个问题。第一口就让人心生不安，因为你会意识到，辣子鸡从此再也不是原来的味道。多汁的一口大小鸡肉带着淡淡的烟熏味，与大多数印度中式辣子鸡不同，后者通常依靠各种酱汁调制风味。菜单上的几乎每道菜，要么是科钦此前未曾出现过的新品，要么与我们所预期的做法不同。Chao 是 Vijay Antony Felix 对他从小在加尔各答吃到的中餐的致敬：“我从小吃这些食物，就想把它带到科钦。我希望人们也能体验一番！”加尔各答以独特的唐拉式中餐闻名，这道菜系由中国社群推广开来；他们在当地扎根已有两个多世纪。唐拉是加尔各答的唐人街之一，华人聚居于此，许多人是来到当地制革厂工作的移民。尽管具有华裔背景的人已经很少，尤其是在餐饮业中，但唐拉中餐仍拥有 Vijay 这样忠实拥趸，他们希望把这种菜式介绍给其他城市。Vijay 本职是工程师，但他称自己是一位热衷餐饮的创业者，而这份投入也体现在他对 Chao 的精心打造上。Chao 位于 Panampilly Nagar 的主路上，午餐时段人来人往。店内空间不大，墙面采用中餐馆常见的红色，更添鲜明的中国风情。建筑白色外墙上绘有一条红色细线 dragon。“chao” 在中文中的一个含义是炒或煸。座位对有些人而言可能显得过于紧凑，但这样反而营造出温馨的社群感，空中回荡的谈话声也让人感到安心。餐厅开业才两个多月，Vijay 却表示，顾客反响远超预期，尤其是因为这里提供的是不同于人们惯常食用的普通中餐。对此他毫无怨言。我们直接从头品尝美食，首先是清爽的馄饨汤。汤品清淡鲜美，简单的做法完全足以称得上慰藉食物。接下来是前菜——第一道是客家芝士，烤至微焦或油炸的方形芝士薄片，拌有香菜和切得极薄的辣椒。辣椒与香菜的组合绝不会让印度味蕾失望。接着是蜂蜜脆皮辣牛肉，牛肉条辛辣中又略带一丝甜味。虽然是一道前菜，却很适合搭配看起来颜色很淡、乍看之下显得寡淡的广式炒面。不过，如果你喜欢在面中尝到蔬菜，这道菜正适合你。一般中餐里不会放香菜和青辣椒，但唐拉菜式却会使用这些食材。印度当地烹饪对菜系的 영향同样明显，融入了本地做法的元素。对芝士持怀疑态度的人来说，这会是一种全新体验，尤其是咬到青辣椒的那一口。“我们不会过度使用酱汁，而会放很多辣椒来增添辣味。”Vijay 说道。另一道热门菜品是猪肉末四季豆。除了其他汽水饮品外，餐厅还供应康普茶，以及不含酒精、值得一试的麦芽饮料。这种饮料喝起来很安静，几乎像啤酒一样。我们把满是焦香蒜末的蒜香炒饭和唐拉宫保鸡盛入盘中，Vijay 一边指着身后墙上的照片，一边向我们讲述唐拉的“华人” Kali 庙，以及中国素菜作为供品（bhog）供奉的情况。墙上还并排陈列着一瓶当地生产的 Pou Chong 酱。厨房员工来自加尔各答，菜单则是 Vijay 走访加尔各答各家中国餐馆、深入研究后的成果。他说，其中一些菜谱确实从当地菜品中获得了灵感。菜单相当丰富；除了数量可观的海鲜菜品外，也充分考虑了素食者的需求。这一桌让人吃得很饱，甜点则实在让人无法再装下。不过，甜品依然很诱人——darsaan（蜜制面条）配香草冰淇淋、威士忌巧克力挞配香草冰淇淋，以及冰棒。darsaan 和冰淇淋只能留待改日再尝。尽管餐厅开业只有几个月，但直接前往前最好先预订。温馨提醒：如果你期待的是熟悉的中餐口味，那么这里会让你感到惊喜。唐拉风格鲜明而独特，尽管如今多数印度中餐都起源于当地。评论必须使用英语，并以完整句子表达。评论不得带有辱骂性或人身攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已是 The Hindu 注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与文章互动。如果你没有账号，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录 Vuukle 账号后即可查看自己过去的评论。

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: Fugitive gangster Himanshu Bhau, who is wanted in India in connection with murder and extortion casesm is currently in the custody of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, according to officials. The US government’s online detainee locator lists two Indian-born men – Himanshu Sigroha and Neeraj Kaushik – as being in ICE custody at the Henderson Detention Center at 18 East Basic Road in Henderson, Nevada, outside Las Vegas. Their cases are handled by ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) office in Las Vegas. Bhau, 26, was hiding in Canada for over two years. He has been involved in several cases of gang war, extortion, assault and murder in Delhi and Punjab, officials said. The gangster, who is originally from Rohtak, fled India in 2022 after his name cropped up in three murder cases, which had taken place within a short span of 25 days, according to an earlier HT report. According to Delhi Police, Bhau fled to Dubai and towards Portugal before relocating to the US. This is a breaking news story. It will be updated with further details

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 据官员介绍，被通缉的逃犯、匪徒希曼舒·巴乌因涉嫌谋杀和敲诈勒索案件在印度被追捕，目前被美国移民与海关执法局拘押。美国政府的在线被拘留人员查询系统列出了两名在印度出生的男子——希曼舒·西格罗哈和尼拉杰·考希克——称他们被拘押在内华达州拉斯维加斯郊外亨德森市东基础路18号的亨德森拘留中心。他们的案件由美国移民与海关执法局拉斯维加斯执法与遣返行动办公室（ERO）处理。官员称，26岁的巴乌在加拿大躲藏了两年多。他曾卷入德里和旁遮普邦多起帮派争斗、敲诈勒索、袭击和谋杀案件。据此前《印度斯坦时报》报道，这名原籍罗塔克的匪徒在2022年逃离印度，此前他的名字出现在短短25天内发生的3起谋杀案件中。据德里警方称，巴乌先逃往迪拜，随后前往葡萄牙，之后转移至美国。这是一则突发新闻报道，后续将补充更多细节。

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.summary_zh: 共和党筹款优势很大程度上来自少数几位富有的印度裔美国捐助者，尤其是科技行业的捐助者。与此同时，民主党从印度裔美国人群体中吸引到的大额捐助者较少。资金差距还凸显出，尽管民主党仍得到较小额捐助者的支持，但富有的印度裔美国捐助者正日益倾向于支持共和党。
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: A group of major Indian-American business leaders and entrepreneurs have donated over $15.8 million to Republican Party-linked political action committees and funds since 2025, giving Donald Trump’s party a roughly 4:1 fundraising advantage over Democrats among prominent donors ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, an HT analysis of Federal Election Commission data shows. The Democratic party, which is fighting to take back control of the House of Representatives and the Senate from the Republicans, has raised roughly $3.7 million from key donors within the community. Much of the Republicans’ fundraising advantage comes from a handful of wealthy Indian-American donors, particularly those in the technology industry. Venture capitalist Asha Jadeja Motwani, who has donated an estimated $5.9 million to Trump-affiliated political action committee MAGA Inc and the Republican National Committee (RNC) since 2025, emerged as the party’s biggest Indian-American donor. Michelle D’Souza, an entrepreneur who grew up in Goa and heads IT firm Unified Business Technologies, contributed $4 million to MAGA Inc in October 2025, followed by more than $400,000 to the RNC in 2025 and 2026. Other major Republican donors include Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar, who contributed about $1.9 million to Republican political action committees and groups in 2025 and 2026. Sankar, a newly minted billionaire, was reportedly considered by the Trump administration for a senior Pentagon role. Orthopaedic surgeon Anjani Sinha, who was nominated by Trump as US ambassador to Singapore in March 2025, donated $1 million to MAGA Inc the previous month. Retired medical professional Krishna Tripuraneni also contributed $1 million to the committee. Tripuraneni, who pleaded guilty to filing a false tax return, is seeking a presidential pardon, HT reported earlier this year. Florida businessman Ramalinga Mantena, who made headlines in India last year over his daughter’s lavish wedding in Udaipur, donated $886,000 to Republican causes, in addition to a substantial contribution to Trump’s inaugural ball. Donations from billionaire sports team owner Vivek Ranadive, technology entrepreneur Vipul Prakash and Nvidia vice-president Sundeep Singh Madra added a further $750,000 to the Republicans’ election war chest. The Democrats, meanwhile, have attracted fewer big-money donors from the Indian-American community. Venture capitalist Vinod Khosla contributed about $2.09 million to Democratic causes in 2025 and 2026, with much of the funding directed towards the Senate Majority PAC, which aims to help the party regain control of the upper chamber. Khosla’s daughter, writer and brand strategist Anu Khosla, donated more than $250,000 to Democratic and progressive groups during the same period, while veteran Democratic donor and investment adviser Shekar Narasimhan contributed about $309,400. The Democratic-aligned Impact Fund also raised more than $1 million from prominent Indian-American donors, including Silicon Valley-based investor Sumir Chadha. The fundraising gap reflects a sharp increase in contributions to Trump-aligned groups by some prominent Indian-American donors since 2025. Motwani, for instance, donated $300,000 to a joint fundraising committee supporting Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign and the RNC before increasing her contributions roughly 18-fold in 2025. Sankar, meanwhile, gave less than $100,000 to Republican causes during the 2023-24 election cycle before contributing about $1.9 million in 2025 and 2026. Motwani said her increased funding was driven by a desire to help Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections. “I want the Republicans to maintain a major majority in the House and the Senate, so contributing to President Trump’s war chest is an important step towards funding the right candidates and their campaigns,” Motwani told HT. HT’s analysis also found that some prominent Indian-American donors backing Republicans were previously major supporters of the Democratic Party. Motwani, for instance, supported Barack Obama in 2012, Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Joe Biden in 2020 before becoming one of the community’s biggest donors to Trump. Ranadive, who contributed roughly $60,000 to the Democrats in the 2024 election cycle, donated $250,000 to Republican causes in 2025. Mantena, a major Trump supporter in 2020 and 2024, had also backed Obama in 2012. Motwani attributed her shift to a loss of faith in the Democratic Party, alleging that it had allowed undocumented migrants to enter the country and obtain documents that could be used to vote. “I lost trust in the Democratic Party after I discovered that they had opened the borders to import voters in swing states,” she told HT, making claims about election fraud. Motwani said she intended to continue backing Republican candidates in 2026 and 2028. The funding gap also highlights how wealthy Indian-American donors are increasingly favouring Republicans, even as Democrats retain support among smaller contributors. “Trump is soaking up the money among big Indian-American donors. The people giving less than $1,000 are Democrats now. The people giving more than half a million dollars are Republicans,” Narasimhan told HT. However, he said Democratic committees had seen a “big uptick” in small donors contributing $25 to $50 a month, describing it as evidence of a growing grassroots movement. The trend, he added, was difficult to capture fully through Federal Election Commission records, which do not always convey the scale of small-donor mobilisation. The Republicans’ fundraising advantage among wealthy Indian-Americans comes even as opinion within the community remains divided over Trump’s handling of relations with India. One Indian-American active in the Republican Party told HT, on condition of anonymity, that concerns over online attacks against Indians could erode support for Trump and his party. Democrats, meanwhile, believe tensions in US-India relations, visa difficulties and anti-immigration sentiment could win back voters who supported Trump in 2024. “Many of those who once supported Trump are now returning to the Democratic side,” Democratic fundraiser and organiser Ajay Bhutoria told HT, pointing to recent elections in New Jersey, Virginia and New York
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.title_zh: 美国中期选举前，印度裔美国捐赠者向共和党提供的资金是民主党的4倍
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 《Hindustan Times》对美国联邦选举委员会数据的分析显示，自2025年以来，一批印度裔美国商界领袖和企业家已向与共和党有关联的政治行动委员会和基金捐款逾1580万美元。在11月3日美国中期选举前夕，这些知名捐款人给唐纳德·特朗普所属政党带来的筹款优势约为民主党的4倍。民主党正努力从共和党手中夺回众议院和参议院的控制权，该党从社区内的关键捐款人处筹集了约370万美元。共和党的筹款优势主要来自少数几位富有的印度裔美国捐款人，尤其是科技业人士。风险投资家Asha Jadeja Motwani自2025年以来据估计已向特朗普阵营的政治行动委员会MAGA Inc和共和党全国委员会（RNC）捐款约590万美元，成为该党最大的印度裔美国捐款人。在果阿邦长大的企业家、信息技术公司Unified Business Technologies负责人Michelle D’Souza于2025年10月向MAGA Inc捐款400万美元，随后在2025年和2026年又向RNC捐款逾40万美元。共和党的其他主要捐款人包括Palantir首席技术官Shyam Sankar，他在2025年和2026年向共和党政治行动委员会和团体捐款约190万美元。据报道，这位新晋亿万富翁曾被特朗普政府考虑任命为五角大楼高级职位的人选。骨科外科医生Anjani Sinha于2025年3月获特朗普提名为美国驻新加坡大使，并在当月向MAGA Inc捐款100万美元。退休医疗专业人士Krishna Tripuraneni也向该委员会捐款100万美元。《Hindustan Times》今年早些时候报道称，Tripuraneni因提交虚假纳税申报书而认罪，目前正在寻求总统赦免。佛罗里达州商人Ramalinga Mantena去年因女儿在乌代布尔举办奢华婚礼而登上印度头条，除向特朗普就职舞会提供一笔可观捐款外，还向共和党事业捐款88.6万美元。亿万富翁、体育球队老板Vivek Ranadive、科技企业家Vipul Prakash和Nvidia副总裁Sundeep Singh Madra的捐款，又为共和党的选举资金库增加了75万美元。与此同时，民主党从印度裔美国社区吸引的大额捐款人较少。风险投资家Vinod Khosla在2025年和2026年向民主党事业捐款约209万美元，其中很大一部分流向参议院多数党PAC，旨在帮助该党重新掌控参议院。Khosla的女儿、作家兼品牌战略家Anu Khosla在同一时期向民主党和进步派团体捐款逾25万美元；资深民主党捐款人和投资顾问Shekar Narasimhan则捐款约30.94万美元。民主党阵营的Impact Fund也从包括总部位于硅谷的投资者Sumir Chadha在内的知名印度裔美国捐款人处筹集了逾100万美元。筹款差距反映出，自2025年以来，一些知名印度裔美国捐款人向特朗普阵营团体捐款的金额大幅增加。例如，Motwani曾向支持特朗普2024年总统竞选和RNC的联合筹款委员会捐款30万美元，随后在2025年将捐款额提高约18倍。与此同时，Sankar在2023至2024年选举周期内向共和党事业捐款不足10万美元，但2025年和2026年又捐款约190万美元。Motwani表示，她增加捐款是为了帮助共和党在11月中期选举中继续掌控国会两院。“我希望共和党在众议院和参议院保持明显多数，因此向特朗普总统竞选资金库捐款，是为合适的候选人和他们的竞选活动提供资金的重要一步。”Motwani告诉《Hindustan Times》。《Hindustan Times》的分析还发现，一些支持共和党的知名印度裔美国捐款人此前曾是民主党的主要支持者。例如，Motwani曾在2012年支持贝拉克·奥巴马，2016年支持希拉里·克林顿，2020年支持乔·拜登，后来成为特朗普在该社区内最大的捐款人之一。Ranadive在2024年选举周期内向民主党捐款约6万美元，却在2025年向共和党事业捐款25万美元。Mantena是特朗普在2020年和2024年竞选中的主要支持者，此前也曾在2012年支持奥巴马。Motwani将这一立场转变归因于对民主党失去信任，并声称民主党允许无证移民进入美国，获取可用于投票的证件。“当我发现民主党开放边境，把选民引入摇摆州后，我就失去了对民主党的信任。”她告诉《Hindustan Times》，并提出了有关选举舞弊的说法。Motwani表示，她打算在2026年和2028年继续支持共和党候选人。资金差距也凸显出，富裕的印度裔美国捐款人越来越倾向支持共和党，尽管民主党仍得到小额捐款人的支持。“特朗普正在吸走印度裔美国大额捐款人的钱。现在，捐款低于1000美元的人是民主党，捐款超过50万美元的人是共和党。”Narasimhan告诉《Hindustan Times》。不过，他表示，民主党委员会的小额捐款人捐款额每月在25至50美元之间，已经出现“大幅增长”，并将其视为草根运动不断发展的迹象。他补充说，这一趋势很难通过联邦选举委员会的记录得到完整反映，因为这些记录并不总能体现小额捐款人动员的规模。尽管共和党在富裕印度裔美国人群中拥有筹款优势，但该社区对特朗普处理印美关系的做法仍意见分歧。一名活跃于共和党的印度裔美国人士在匿名条件下告诉《Hindustan Times》，针对印度人的网络攻击所引发的担忧，可能削弱对特朗普及其政党的支持。与此同时，民主党认为，美印关系紧张、签证困难和反移民情绪，可能促使2024年支持特朗普的选民重新转向民主党。民主党筹款人兼组织者Ajay Bhutoria告诉《Hindustan Times》：“许多曾经支持特朗普的人如今正在回归民主党阵营。”他还提到新泽西州、弗吉尼亚州和纽约州近期的选举
